# Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations, Part II

## Purpose and boundaries

This roadmap connects roots of line bundles with sections to geometric class field theory with quadratic ramification. Its first endpoint is a coherent infinite root stack and its fpqc quotient/Kummer description. Its second is the normalized character sheaf on every degree of the root Picard stack, with the quadratic Frobenius trace identified with the idele character. These endpoints share finite-root and native line-bundle interfaces; neither the infinite tower nor its Kummer classification is an input to the character-sheaf proof.

The document assembles the accepted parent plan and all ten accepted layer refinements. It is the definitive mathematical specification: 834 stable target ids, with their hypotheses, proof outlines, named API, discriminating checks and source locators. The large inherited affine-algebra catalogue is retained as supporting contracts, rather than repeated chronological checkpoints. All ten layers have complete **planning** coverage. Their actual geometric carriers and the supplier frontiers below remain open; no target is asserted to be implemented or formally proved. Review verdicts in the eleven packets retain their original authorship.

Ordinary function fields, places, completions, weighted divisors, approximation and reciprocity belong to FunctionFieldArithmetic and the existing Tau Ceti/Mathlib library. Ordinary curve/Picard geometry and the function-field-to-curve dictionary belong to AlgebraicCurves, JacobianChallenge and their SchemeAndStackFoundations integration. General coherent tensor products, sections, duals and strong monoidal pullback belong to AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0C. This roadmap specializes those interfaces to root data; it does not plan their reconstruction.

Current **SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18 and 1.21** own generic stackification, two-fibre products and site-independent quotient stacks, the classifier of a line bundle with section, finite root stacks, their affine charts, transitions and nonreduced zero fibres. Its §3.4 owns the native Picard groupoid. The local `key/root-stacks` and finite-root ids below are stable compatibility anchors for these imported objects. RS.0 supplies native section/frame coordinates, RS.1 compares those triples with the upstream root stack and keeps relative/stack-base/coarse/wild refinements, and RS.2 owns the coherent infinite diagram, fpqc quotient and Kummer applications. DiamondsAndVStacks D0 is an instance on its own site, rather than the generic scheme-site owner. The finite diagonalizable coarse-space generality remains the exact request RS1-DIAGONALIZABLE-COARSE.

Existing tensor/exterior maps, their factorial and norm composites, naturality and finite-group transfer are imports from the current library. GC.3 adds the Koszul-action compatibility and the required invariant comparison/averaging consequences. Its sheaf construction can use monodromy and coarse spaces; the comparison with the source's nonrepresentable pushforward remains a separate target. Generic stack-lisse/fundamental-group and proper/coarse-pushforward interfaces have one intended owner, the proposed stacks Part II of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves. Its unregistered stage names are never treated as supplied prerequisites.

The separate symplectic central-L-value route in the parent brief is a proposed sibling, **SymplecticLFunctionsModSquares**, not another collection of layers here. Its 38 contracts and source/ownership corrections remain in the parent restructuring proposal and are collected in the assembly handoff. That proposal has not itself been applied by this assembly. Root ramification is not silently imposed on the everywhere-unramified symplectic route.

Ownership was checked against the read-only TauCetiRoadmap checkout at `0d144d044dacebca17b654695b6f1ad58f159b27`, the current Tau Ceti library at `a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039`, and current upstream SchemeAndStackFoundations at `9a305e195e7870e5136053897997f7538a01121e`. The reviewed AUDIT-20 function-field entries and AUDIT-01 SF.3 entry distinguish built arithmetic results from missing family/stack comparisons. Compilation uses the older mandatory pins, Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`. A current-library import can therefore be absent from the compilation baseline.

## Conventions

For RS.0–RS.2, let X be a scheme, or a stack when that extension is explicitly stated, with a native invertible sheaf L, section s and positive integer root exponent n. A root over T→X is (M,t,φ), with φ:Mⁿ≅L_T carrying tⁿ to s_T. An arrow is an **isomorphism** preserving the section and power identification. Use the core of `InvertibleSheaf`; its ambient native category also contains noninvertible module maps. Zero and nilpotent sections are legitimate. The fixed recursive tensor-power parentheses and their canonical comparisons are used throughout, including exponent-zero auxiliary powers.

Finite roots and Kummer torsors use fppf descent at every positive exponent. Étale Kummer requires invertibility of the exponent. Infinite roots and torsors use fpqc descent. The index arrow m→n means n divides m, with transition by the (m/n)-th power; composition uses specified tensor-power isomorphisms. A compatible system has objects, comparison arrows and their cocycle, rather than just compatible isomorphism classes. Factorial restriction starts at 1!. The inverse-limit band is the affine group scheme D(Q/Z)=lim μ_n, with its full functor of points, including wild/nonreduced inertia.

On a trivialized target line a normalized coframe β:M≅O satisfies βⁿ=φ. Use the left action ζβ, so the coordinate β(t) has weight +1. The coframe presentation inverts the scalar band on a zero-section gerbe. The band-preserving Kummer coordinate uses Isom(x_λ,y) after a chosen origin. Changing the frame λ to vλ multiplies this coordinate by [v]. Kummer quotient transitions send [a]_m to [a]_n without powering the representative.

For GC.0–GC.6, k is a finite field of odd characteristic, X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, R⊂X is reduced finite, U=X−R, g is the genus and ρ=deg_k R. The GC.0 refinement explicitly extends its native/frame argument to arbitrary fields of characteristic different from two with finite étale R/k; it does not generalize Frobenius results. After geometric splitting, the number of root coordinates is ρ; a letter r in a split-coordinate calculation means that number, rather than the number of closed points. Divisor degree is weighted by residue-field degrees. No degree-one rational point is chosen; ordinary Pic^d may be a torsor.

Write P^d=Pic_X^(√R,d). Its objects over T are (L,K_R,ι:K_R²≅L|_R_T); a root section α_R lies only on R_T. The whole section stack hat X_d^(√R) additionally retains a global section a, possibly zero, with ι(α_R²)=a|_R_T. The effective open X_d^(√R) requires a to be nonzero on every geometric curve fibre. This is not a condition that an arbitrary raw tuple over a nonreduced ring is nonzero. Full and relative inertia are distinguished. With empty R, root-coordinate equations are vacuous and the ordinary Picard scalar group persists.

Use Q̄_ℓ, with ℓ different from char k, and geometric Frobenius. The symmetric local system L_d is unshifted; L_d[d] is its perverse normalization. Branch inertia has order dividing two, while global rank-one monodromy may have order three or infinite image. Rational averaging permits every factorial to be inverted, even if ℓ divides d!. Permutations of degree-zero sheaf lines have ordinary symmetry; permutations of degree-one cohomology classes have the Koszul sign. Every character, translation and cohomology comparison includes Frobenius compatibility.

The uniform Abel–Jacobi bound is B=ρ+max(2g−1,1). For d≥B, put n=d−g+1 and a=n−ρ≥1. The split fibre chart keeps (u,α), while its section coordinate is (u,α²). For nonempty R, scalar weights are two on the a kernel coordinates and one on the ρ root coordinates. Its proper quotient supplies the descent proof; the punctured affine fibre is not claimed to be simply connected. For empty R, use ordinary weight one and a projective quotient. Smooth gluing and degree-zero proper base change establish effective descent.

Adelic coordinates use E(a)=Σ_x v_x(a_x)x. The associated line is O_X(−E(a)); thus an inverse uniformizer π_x⁻¹ corresponds to O_X(x)^♮. The signed right action groupoid A_F×/O_(√R)× retains a generic frame and all kernel labels. Only the separate further F×-quotient gives the root Picard groupoid. The map from modified units is not assumed injective. The norm complex is interpreted through based torsor fibres, coherent nullhomotopies and H² obstructions, rather than ordinary exactness on Picard classes.

All ambient universes and site changes must retain actual evaluation, pullback transformations and coherence modifications. No equivalence to every object of a larger universe, nor a same-universe claim for all schemes, is inferred from notation.

## Sources and reading convention

The principal geometric input is Yun–Zhang, *Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions (II)*, Annals 189 (2019), 393–526: Definitions A.1–A.3 and Lemmas A.4–A.5, pp. 514–518; Lemmas A.6–A.10 and Proposition A.11, pp. 519–523; and Proposition A.12, pp. 525–526. Infinite-root inputs use Talpo–Vistoli, arXiv:1410.1164v2, §3, pp. 12–16. Finite-root comparisons use Abramovich–Graber–Vistoli, arXiv:math/0603151v2, Appendix B.1–B.2, pp. 52–54. Each target gives its exact source locator and identifies authored extensions or missing supplier interfaces; the source register below records editions. No source passage is reproduced.

The assembly independently read the published Yun–Zhang Appendix A at these locators and the current upstream finite-root contract. Earlier source/version checks and per-node mathematical reviews remain attributed to their packets. A target catalogue is not a section-by-section account of a paper. In particular, source text concerning reduced geometric points is not used to erase nilpotents or inertia in a family.

## RS.0 — Native root objects and affine comparisons

Start with actual line sheaves and their isomorphisms. A coordinate root has both a section and an invertible power-identification coefficient. Native frames compare this groupoid with the accepted affine algebra; local normalization is an fppf cover, not a global root choice. Arbitrary coefficient maps preserve equations but can kill sections and stabilizers, so coefficient-change functors are not asserted faithful. The generic finite root is imported; the work here is its native coordinate and coherence comparison.

**Planets.** Affine root coaction — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction); Root objects in coordinates — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-trivialization-equation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-trivialization-equation); Pullback of root objects — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-root-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-root-pullback); Root-coordinate equivalence — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-framed-equivalence); Local normalization of roots — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-local-normalization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-local-normalization); Root-chart stackification — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-stackification-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-stackification-equivalence).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Objects and conventions

Let T be a scheme. Write O_T for the native trivial invertible sheaf, identified with the structure-module unit through the canonical free-PUnit isomorphism. For a native invertible sheaf M, the parent recursion is M^0=O_T and M^(n+1)=M^n⊗M. It fixes parentheses. Its section powers begin with the unit section1; the successor is the imported tensorSection of the preceding power and t. Tensor powers of actual line isomorphisms, together with c_n:O_T^n≅O_T, use the same recursion.

For n≥1, a root of a line with section (L,s) is (M,t,φ), where M is an invertible sheaf, t∈Γ(T,M) and φ:M^n≅L satisfies φ(t^n)=s. A root arrow h:(M,t,φ)→(N,r,ψ) is a line isomorphism satisfying h(t)=r and ψ∘h^n=φ. The root groupoid is not the full category of invertible sheaves: the latter also has noninvertible module maps. Nor is it the set of root isomorphism classes. These conventions reuse parent nodes `RS.0/root-object`, `RS.0/tensor-power`, `RS.0/section-power`, `RS.0/trivial-power-isomorphism` and `RS.0/section-power-transport`.

On Spec B with a chosen target frame l:L≅O and root frame e:M≅O, read the sections through the actual ΓSpec isomorphism. Put y=coord(e(t)), f=coord(l(s)). The automorphism

\[
l\circ\varphi\circ(e^{-1})^n\circ c_n^{-1}:O\longrightarrow O
\]

is multiplication by a unit u, and the root equation becomes

\[
u y^n=f.
\]

An arrow h from framed root p to framed root q has unit label w, the scalar of e_q∘h∘e_p^{-1}. Its two equations are

\[
y_q=w y_p,\qquad u_q w^n=u_p.
\]

Every label is retained. At a zero section the first equation imposes no restriction on w, but the second still does. Losing the second equation turns general units into false root automorphisms. Replacing arrows by their effect on y identifies different stabilizers. The parent `root-identification-unit`, `root-trivialization-equation`, `root-arrow-scalars` and `framed-groupoid` supply these contracts. The native equivalence below gives their inverse and actual unit/counit.

The geometric exponent is always positive, including exponents divisible by the residue characteristic. There is no reducedness, noetherianity or nonzero-section assumption. Arbitrary test changes may be nonflat and noninjective. The zero ring is allowed; its spectrum and coverings have their native empty-scheme interpretation. Exponent zero is used for tensor recursion and for the parent's scheme comparison of normalization algebras, with no assertion that its unit-root algebra is a covering algebra.

#### The comparison architecture

The native groupoid with a chosen root frame has **all root arrows**, rather than only frame-preserving arrows. Its coordinate functor is an equivalence with FramedRoot. Forgetting its frame is fully faithful, with essential image the roots whose root line is trivializable. This leaves the global root-line obstruction visible. A normalized affine chart has coefficient1; the parent fully faithful inclusion into FramedRoot remains the exact normalized inclusion.

For a framed root (u,y), the specified normalization algebra is D=B[T]/(T^n−u). The adjoined root r=T is a unit because u is a unit and n≥1; its inverse is u^{-1}r^{n−1}. The pulled root (u,y) is isomorphic to (1,r*y), with label r, since r^n=u. The parent supplies its finite basis, faithful flatness, finite presentation, actual singleton scheme fppf cover, functor on labelled arrows and Cartesian coefficient changes. Their use after native local line frames proves local essential surjectivity. The resulting associated-stack comparison uses the actual descent theorem and the current SF.1 stackification contract; it does not infer a stack from a set of chart points.

Both local obstructions matter. The root line can fail to be trivial on an affine test. Even if it is trivial, its coefficient u need not be an n-th power in Bˣ. The normalized chart misses the latter roots objectwise. Taking a Zariski cover for the line, followed by the specified fppf Kummer cover for u, removes the two obstructions and preserves all arrows. Different frames and different unit roots produce modifications rather than equality of all choices. This is what makes the local presentation independent of its choices.

For example, over B=Z/4, n=2, f=3, the coordinate data u=3,y=1 give a root with trivial line. Squares in B are0 or1, so the normalized chart has no B-point. In D=B[T]/(T²−3) that object becomes the normalized root with sectionT. The associated stack has the original root as a global object, despite the empty raw chart-point groupoid on B. A claim of objectwise essential surjectivity would fail this example.

At f=0 over Z/9, the sections3 and0 both have square zero. They are not isomorphic as root sections: multiplication by a unit cannot carry the nonzero3 to0. Replacing the full fibre by a reduced gerbe erases this distinction. AGV B.2, p.53, explicitly distinguishes the full nilpotent neighbourhood from its gerbe. This is also the correction required for Yun–Zhang A.1.3, pp.515–516, as inherited in source finding E2.

At n=2,y=0 over Z/4, unit labels1 and−1 give different automorphisms. Under Z/4→Z/2 they become equal. Native pullback and coordinate change still commute, so this is a required nonfaithfulness example, not a failure of naturality. The parent normalization functor's faithfulness is a separate assertion using its adjoined unit and faithful flatness; it does not imply faithfulness of arbitrary coefficient change. In characteristic p, over F_p[ε]/(ε²), the unit1+ε has p-th power1. At a zero section it is a visible infinitesimal μ_p automorphism. Wild exponents must therefore be tested on rings with nilpotents, not only on geometric field points.

#### Tensor powers used by root objects

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/tensor-power` · imported contract / native comparison · implementation unchecked.

For a native invertible sheaf M on a scheme T define M⁰=O_T and Mⁿ⁺¹=Mⁿ⊗M, with coherent transport of line-bundle isomorphisms. This is a root-object interface over the existing tensor operation, not a new definition of line bundles.

**Ownership.** The generic finite object/construction is imported, not planned again. This stable local contract records its native InvertibleSheaf/section/arrows specialization and compatibility with the chosen affine coordinates; RS.2 owns the coherent infinite diagram and its constraints. Supplier: SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, 3.4; AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0B.

**Hypotheses.** The exponent n is a natural number, including zero; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.trivial`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorProduct`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductCongrLeft`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductCongrRight`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductAssoc`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorTrivialLeftIso`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorTrivialRightIso`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Recurse using the native trivial bundle and tensor product.
2. Transport an isomorphism by the native tensor congruences; the recursion fixes parentheses.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower.zero` (simp): M⁰ is the native trivial sheaf.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower.succ` (simp): Mⁿ⁺¹=Mⁿ⊗M with the chosen parentheses.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower.mapIso` (functoriality): An isomorphism M≅N induces Mⁿ≅Nⁿ and respects identity and composition.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower.test_zero` (degenerate): At exponent zero the output is O_T.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower.test_one` (compatibility): At exponent one the output is isomorphic to M via the native unit isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower.test_two` (computation): At exponent two the output is O_T⊗M⊗M with the displayed parentheses, canonically M⊗M.

**Acceptance.** Zero exponent is the native trivial sheaf; exponent one is canonically M.

**Consumers.** where: AGV B.2; how: The root identification has domain the n-th tensor power of M.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — B.1–B.2 pp. 52–54

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.tensorPower`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-action"></a>

#### Diagonalizable action on the affine root chart

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-action` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For a commutative ring A, f∈A and n≥1, each ζ∈rootsOfUnity(n,A) induces an A-algebra automorphism of the existing AdjoinRoot(Tⁿ−f) sending T to ζT. The construction is natural on A-algebras and represents the μ_n group-scheme action, including infinitesimal points.

**Hypotheses.** The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:AdjoinRoot`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.lift`, `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The image ζT satisfies Tⁿ−f because ζⁿ=1; use the native quotient lift.
2. Use ζ⁻¹ for the inverse; generator evaluation proves identity and multiplication.
3. Apply the same construction on every A-algebra to retain the group-scheme action.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction.root` (simp): The distinguished quotient root maps to ζ times itself.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction.constant` (simp): Every coefficient from A is fixed.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction.mul` (structure): The automorphisms for ζξ and ζ composed with ξ agree.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction.test_one` (degenerate): The unit root of unity acts as the identity.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction.test_sign` (computation): For n=2 the element −1 sends T to −T.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction.test_infinitesimal` (non-example): On F_p[ε]/ε² at n=p, 1+ε has p-th power one and acts by T↦(1+ε)T.

**Acceptance.** In characteristic p the μ_p action is not detected by its geometric-point set.

**Consumers.** where: TV Corollary 3.13; how: Supplies the diagonalizable action in the finite root quotient chart.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3.1 pp. 14–16, P=N and Corollary 3.13

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.affineAction`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-root-relation"></a>

#### Canonical quotient-root relation

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-root-relation` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

The distinguished root t of the actual quotient B=A[T]/(Tⁿ−f) satisfies tⁿ=algebraMap(f), including over nonreduced and zero coefficient rings.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring and f∈A. The root relation and character-power identity allow every natural n; Euclidean reduction uses n≥1. No reducedness, regularity, invertibility of n, or unit condition on f is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:AdjoinRoot`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Evaluate the defining polynomial at the canonical quotient root using eval₂_root.
2. Expand evaluation of Xⁿ−C(f) and cancel the subtraction; the existing coefficient algebra map is the native quotient map.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineRoot.pow_eq.test_wild_branch` (computation): Over F₂, the canonical root of T² has square zero.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineRoot.pow_eq.test_regular_nonunit` (computation): Over Z, the canonical root of T²−2 has fourth power equal to the image of 4.

**Acceptance.** For A=F₂,n=2,f=0, t²=0 without any assertion that t vanishes.; For A=Z,n=2,f=2, t⁴=4; f need not be a unit.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3.1 pp. 14–16, character grading before Lemma 3.7 and finite chart of Corollary 3.13, P=N Root-specific calculation derived here from the finite P=N character grading and quotient chart. The native quotient and character algebra are imported. This is not a verbatim theorem attributed to the paper.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.affineRoot.pow_eq`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-character-power"></a>

#### Powers of the native root character

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-character-power` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

In H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)], the basis element e₁ at the existing roots-of-unity character generator satisfies e₁ⁱ=e_i for every i≥0. In particular e₁ⁿ=1, even when n is zero in A.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring and f∈A. The root relation and character-power identity allow every natural n; Euclidean reduction uses n≥1. No reducedness, regularity, invertibility of n, or unit condition on f is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.generator`, `mathlib:MonoidAlgebra.single_pow`, `mathlib:ofAdd_nsmul`, `mathlib:ZMod.natCast_self`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the native single_pow identity with coefficient 1.
2. Expand the existing generator to Multiplicative.ofAdd(1). Its i-th power is the additive multiple i•1, whose image is i modulo n. For i=n, natCast_self gives zero and e₀=1.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCharacter.pow.test_wild_order` (compatibility): In F₂[Multiplicative(ZMod 2)], the character basis element e₁ has square one.

**Acceptance.** Over F₂ at exponent two, e₁²=1 although μ₂ is not étale.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3.1 pp. 14–16, character grading before Lemma 3.7 and finite chart of Corollary 3.13, P=N Root-specific calculation derived here from the finite P=N character grading and quotient chart. The native quotient and character algebra are imported. This is not a verbatim theorem attributed to the paper.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCharacter.pow`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-coefficient-permutation"></a>

#### Cyclic root coefficient permutation

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-coefficient-permutation` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For positive n, construct the native equivalence σ:Fin n×Fin n≃Fin n×Fin n defined by σ(i,j)=(i,i+j) using cyclic addition on Fin n, with inverse σ⁻¹(i,k)=(i,k−i). Its representative is (i,(i+j) mod n); it reorders coordinates of the actual root action comparison.

**Hypotheses.** n≥1. The construction is independent of the coefficient ring.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Fin.addCommGroup`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the pinned cyclic additive group on Fin n, not addition of natural representatives without reduction.
2. Define the two pair maps and verify their composites by additive cancellation. No coefficient ring or choice of a root of unity enters.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.coefficientPermutation_apply` (projection): σ(i,j)=(i,i+j) in the cyclic Fin n group.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.coefficientPermutation_symm` (projection): σ⁻¹(i,k)=(i,k−i) in the cyclic Fin n group.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.coefficientPermutation_val` (compatibility): The natural representative of the second component of σ(i,j) is (i+j) mod n.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.wrap_iff_lower` (characterisation): The second component of σ(i,j) is smaller than its first iff n≤i+j, for natural representatives 0≤i,j<n.

**Checks.**

#### Affine root-chart coaction

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Put B=A[t]/(tⁿ−f), using native AdjoinRoot, and H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)], using the native Hopf group algebra. Write e_i for its character basis element indexed by i modulo n. Define the unique A-algebra map δ:B→H⊗_A B with δ(t)=e_1⊗t. Constants map to 1⊗a. This is a universal coordinate map, not an action of the geometric-point set.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:AdjoinRoot`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.algHom_ext`, `mathlib:MonoidAlgebra.single`, `mathlib:MonoidAlgebra.single_pow`, `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight`, `tauceti:TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.generator`, `mathlib:MonoidAlgebra.instHopfAlgebra`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-root-relation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-root-relation), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-character-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-character-power), `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.algebraMap_apply'`, `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_pow`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. In the native group algebra e_1ⁿ=e_0=1 because the character index is modulo n. Hence (e_1⊗t)ⁿ=1⊗f and the quotient polynomial evaluates to zero.
2. Apply the native AdjoinRoot algebra lift with this root and the coefficient map to H⊗_A B. The algebra-map law fixes constants.
3. Native quotient algebra-hom extensionality proves uniqueness. Counit and coassociativity are proved in separate nodes, not assumed fields.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.root` (simp): δ(t)=e_1⊗t in the native H⊗_A B.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.constant` (simp): For every a∈A, δ(algebraMap(a))=1⊗algebraMap(a).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.unique` (universal-property): An A-algebra map ψ:B→H⊗_A B with ψ(t)=e_1⊗t equals δ.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.coordinates_diagonal` (characterisation): Let b=Σ_{i∈Fin n} c_i t^i and use the existing native target-coordinate equivalence C on A[Z/n]⊗_A A[t]/(t^n−f). For q=(r,s), C(δ(b))_q equals c_s if r=s and zero otherwise.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.coordinates_constant_row` (characterisation): With b and C as above, C(1⊗b)_(r,s) equals c_s if r=0 and zero otherwise.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.invariants_sum_iff` (characterisation): For b=Σ_{i∈Fin n} c_i t^i, δ(b)=1⊗b if and only if c_i=0 for every i≠0.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.invariants_unique` (characterisation): Every universally coinvariant b∈A[t]/(t^n−f) has a unique coefficient a∈A with b=algebraMap(a), over every commutative base and positive exponent.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-framed-groupoid"></a>

#### The groupoid of framed root coordinates

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/framed-groupoid` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Construct a native Groupoid of framed root coordinates. An arrow p to q has a unit label w with q.y=w*p.y and q.u*w^n=p.u. Compose labels in categorical order as label(j)*label(h); identities have label1 and inverses have inverse labels. Both arrow equations remain even for the zero section.

**Hypotheses.** Arbitrary commutative A and commutative A-algebra B in a common universe; f arbitrary. The coordinate carrier and its groupoid exist for every natural n; the chart embedding and normalization comparison use positive n via NeZero. No invertibility of n, reducedness, nontriviality, unit-section, regularity, finite-generation, flatness or injectivity assumption.; A chosen-frame coordinate groupoid only. The actual sheaf RootObject-to-coordinate functor, existence of frames and unit roots locally, fppf stackification, effective descent, infinite coherent reindexing and genuine 2-limits remain separate obligations.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/framed-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-framed-object), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Groupoid`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Multiply the section equations and unit-power equations for composition; use the native unit inverse for both inverse equations. Subtype extensionality proves the category and inverse axioms.

**API.**

2. Use only invertible arrows from the core; impose the two compatibility equations on their isomorphisms.

- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.line` (projection): Forget an object to its native invertible sheaf M.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-comparison"></a>

#### Affine action comparison

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-comparison` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Let B=A[x]/(xⁿ−f) be native AdjoinRoot and H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)] the native Hopf group algebra, with character basis e_i. Define the A-algebra map Θ:B⊗_A B→H⊗_A B by the tensor universal property applied to δ:B→H⊗B and c↦1⊗c. Thus the right B-factor is unchanged; this is the coordinate map of the action comparison, not a freely chosen linear map.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction), `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.lift`, `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight`, `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.ext'`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the existing affine coaction and the native right-factor algebra inclusion. Their images commute because the target algebra is commutative.
2. Apply the native tensor-algebra lift, with these two specified maps. Its algebra-map laws fix coefficients and define a unique comparison; no torsor predicate or geometric-point set is introduced.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.left_root` (simp): Θ(x⊗1)=e_1⊗x for the distinguished quotient root x.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.right_factor` (simp): Θ(1⊗c)=1⊗c for every c∈B.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.unique` (universal-property): Any A-algebra map h:B⊗B→H⊗B satisfying h(b⊗c)=δ(b)(1⊗c) for all b,c equals Θ.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_exponent_one` (degenerate): For n=1 and arbitrary f, Θ is bijective; no unit condition is needed.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_zero_ring` (degenerate): For a subsingleton commutative ring A and every positive n,f, Θ is bijective.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_branch_kernel` (non-example): For n=2,f=0 over any field k, x⊗x is nonzero but Θ(x⊗x)=0.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_regular_nonunit` (non-example): For A=Z,n=2,f=2, Θ is injective but not surjective.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_nilpotent_parameter` (non-example): For A=Z/4,n=2,f=2, the source tensor 2(x⊗x) is nonzero and killed by Θ.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_wild_unit` (compatibility): For A=F₂,n=2,f=1, Θ is bijective while x−1≠0 and (x−1)²=0 in B. The finite fppf torsor is not thereby étale.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_nonflat_kernel` (non-example): The injective comparison for Z,n=2,f=2 becomes noninjective for F₂,n=2,f=0. Matrix coefficient change commutes, but kernels need not.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_cokernel_nonreduced` (computation): For A=Z/8,n=2,f=4, the A-module cokernel is A/(4) and contains z with 2z≠0,4z=0. Neither the reduced quotient F₂ nor the algebra quotient generated by im Θ has this property.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.test_branch_image` (computation): At n=2 over any commutative ring, Θ(t⊗t)=f • (e₁⊗1). In particular the branch parameter f=0 gives zero without a regularity assumption.

**Acceptance.** Θ is defined even at f=0 and over the zero ring. Its coordinate-algebra direction is opposite to the scheme action comparison.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-power-pullback` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For h:Y→T, an invertible sheaf M on T and n≥0, construct κ(h,M,n):(h*M)^n≅h*(M^n), natural in actual line isomorphisms. Use the inverse of the unit comparison at n=0 and the tensor comparison recursively at n+1, with M^0=O and M^(n+1)=M^n⊗M. It carries (h*t)^n to h*(t^n). Under any chosen frames its section equation is the image under the coefficient ring map of z^n; it is compatible with identity and composite pullback through the supplier’s strong monoidal comparisons.

**Hypotheses.** T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.; Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.; The exponent may be zero. Global-section pullback is the map obtained from the unit of module pullback–pushforward, or equivalently from the image of a morphism O→M, not an assumed isomorphism on global sections.; Fix the imported comparison directions as β₀:h*O_T≅O_Y and β₂:h*(M⊗N)≅h*M⊗h*N. Thus κ₀=β₀⁻¹ and each successor uses β₂⁻¹; these are inverses of the strong monoidal structural maps where that convention is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/tensor-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-tensor-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power-transport`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power-transport), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Import the strong monoidal module pullback and tensorSection from AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A, restricted to native rank one by L0B/SF.3. This is the existing generic operation, not a new monoidal structure.
2. At zero use O_Y≅h*O_T; in the successor step use κ_n⊗id followed by the inverse of the strong monoidal tensor comparison. The parent fixes parentheses and transport of line isomorphisms.
3. Apply the imported sectionwise tensor/pullback equation at each successor and the unit-section equation at zero. This induction supplies the root-specific section law; it does not require global sections to commute with tensor products as an isomorphism.
4. Identity/composition compatibility follows from the supplier’s monoidal unit and tensor diagrams, not from declaring different tensor powers equal.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-framed-category"></a>

#### Native root objects with chosen line frames

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-category` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Fix a commutative ring B, n≥1 and a target pair (L,s) on Spec B with specified frame l:L≅O. Let f∈B be the coordinate of s through l and Scheme.ΓSpecIso. A FramedNativeRoot object is a parent root object (M,t,φ) together with e:M≅O. A morphism between (a,e_a) and (b,e_b) is any root arrow a→b: it need not preserve e_a,e_b. Composition and inverses are those of the parent root groupoid. Forgetting e is fully faithful; its essential image consists exactly of roots whose line M is globally trivializable.

**Hypotheses.** B may be the zero ring, or nonreduced; f is arbitrary.; The target frame l is fixed. Frames are data on objects, not an additional preservation condition on arrows.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-object), `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ΓSpecIso`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.trivial`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Add e as object data and use the parent Hom type unchanged, so the groupoid laws are inherited.
2. The forgetful Hom map is the identity on actual root arrows and hence fully faithful. Essential-image membership is exactly existence of e; no affine Picard group is presumed zero.
3. For two frames on the same root, the identity root arrow is an isomorphism of the two framed objects. A frame-preserving arrow restriction would destroy this comparison.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot` (constructor): Pairs consisting of an actual root object and a line frame e:M≅O.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.root` (projection): The parent root object, with its line, section and power identification.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.frame` (projection): The specified line isomorphism e; it is not a quotient of choices.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.forget` (functoriality): Forget the chosen frame; act as identity on underlying root arrows.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.homEquiv` (equivalence): The Hom set is exactly the Hom set of the underlying parent roots.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.essentialImage` (characterisation): A root is in the forgetful essential image if and only if its root line admits a global frame.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.test_zero` (non-example): For a zero section and n=2 over Z/4, the −1 automorphism remains an arrow between a framed object and itself; requiring its frame to be fixed would incorrectly delete it.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.test_two_frames` (compatibility): Two frames of the same root are isomorphic by the identity root arrow, including frames differing by a unit a with a^n≠1.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.test_one` (degenerate): At n=1 a root has no nonidentity automorphism, since φ is an isomorphism and φ∘h=φ forces h=id.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot.test_nontrivial_line` (non-example): If Spec B has a nontrivial invertible sheaf M with a specified isomorphism M^n≅O for n≥2, then (M,0,φ) is a root of (O,0) but is outside the forgetful essential image. An affine base and a framed target alone cannot justify a frame of M.

**Acceptance.** Both e_a,e_b appear when computing the scalar label of an arrow.; The category is not the groupoid of roots with frame-preserving arrows.

**Consumers.** where: AGV B.2, p. 54; how: Local trivializations give quotient descriptions but need not exist globally on every affine test.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-equivalence; how: The comparison can read every native root arrow as a unit label.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, printed pp. 52–54 Appendix B.2 supplies the native triples. Adding a chosen line frame and retaining all root arrows is our coordinate-comparison construction, not a source definition of a globally trivial root stack.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.FramedNativeRoot`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-trivialization-equation"></a>

#### The native root equation in coordinates

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-trivialization-equation` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

With the native root object and chosen trivializations above, the computed coefficient u is a unit and u zⁿ=f, where z is the coefficient of the root section under e and f is the coefficient of s under l. The coefficient u is part of the comparison; no choice of an n-th root of u is assumed.

**Hypotheses.** Scheme X arbitrary; n≥1; root object and two specified native trivializations.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-identification-unit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-identification-unit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power-in-trivialization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power-in-trivialization).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use root-identification-unit to evaluate φ on the actual section tⁿ and establish that u is a unit.
2. Use section-power-in-trivialization to identify the coordinate of tⁿ with zⁿ.
3. Transport the defining root equation φ(tⁿ)=s by l; this gives u zⁿ=f. The example quantifies over a bundled unit and asserts equality to the computed coefficient, not just a renamed defining equation.

**Acceptance.** Over Spec(Z/4), n=2, u=3 and z=2 give f=0 with z nonzero; zero sections and nilpotent roots must remain. Over Q the root object u=2,z=1,f=2 exists without a rational square root of 2.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, pp. 52–54, root triples and trivial-bundle quotient calculation Root-specific coordinate derivation of the native object equation and its arrows. The source gives the geometric root data; the unit/coordinate proof decomposition here uses the pinned free-sheaf and tensor APIs, not a claimed printed standalone lemma.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.trivializationEquation`.

#### Scalar equations for arrows of root objects

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-arrow-scalars` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

For root objects a,b of the same (L,s,n), chosen trivializations e_a,e_b of their root lines and l of L, every actual root arrow h:a→b has a unit coefficient w. The section coordinates satisfy z_b=w z_a and the computed root-identification coefficients satisfy u_b wⁿ=u_a. Retain both equations and the unit condition, including when sections vanish.

**Hypotheses.** Scheme X arbitrary; n≥1; h is a native invertible root arrow, not an arbitrary module map.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-identification-unit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-identification-unit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power-in-trivialization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power-in-trivialization), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-object), `mathlib:SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Conjugate the underlying line isomorphism by e_a and e_b. The native free-sheaf Hom equivalence and its actual inverse give its unit coefficient w.
2. The arrow section equation gives z_b=w z_a.
3. Evaluate the tensor-power transport on the native unit section; sectionPower.mapIso and section-power-in-trivialization identify its coefficient with wⁿ.
4. Conjugate the arrow power equation φ_b∘hⁿ=φ_a by the chosen trivializations to obtain u_b wⁿ=u_a.

**Acceptance.** For a=b with zero section and u_a=u_b, the power condition still forces wⁿ=1; forgetting it incorrectly makes every unit an automorphism. Composition multiplies w coefficients.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, pp. 52–54, root triples and trivial-bundle quotient calculation Root-specific coordinate derivation of the native object equation and its arrows. The source gives the geometric root data; the unit/coordinate proof decomposition here uses the pinned free-sheaf and tensor APIs, not a claimed printed standalone lemma.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.arrow_scalar_equations`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-source-coordinate-equivalence"></a>

#### Source coefficient equivalence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-source-coordinate-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For B=A[x]/(xⁿ−f), H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)] and any commutative ring A with positive n, construct the specified A-linear equivalence B⊗_A B ≃ ((Fin n×Fin n)→A) extracting the unique coefficients in the ordered vectors x^i⊗x^j. The inverse coefficient map sends c to Σ_p c_p(x^i⊗x^j). This is the native linear equivalence determined by synthesis, including the zero ring.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-source-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-source-coordinates), `mathlib:LinearEquiv.ofBijective`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Define the native synthesis linear map by the finite linear combination in the statement. Linearity follows from addition and scalar multiplication distributing over a finite sum.
2. The listed coordinate existence-and-uniqueness lemma proves synthesis bijective: uniqueness gives injectivity and existence gives surjectivity.
3. Apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective to synthesis and take its inverse. The inverse evaluation is the exact sum, the forward evaluation of a synthesized family follows from the inverse law, and synthesis of a single coefficient gives the generator formula.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.sourceCoordinateEquiv_symm_apply` (projection): The inverse coefficient map sends c to Σ_p c_p(x^i⊗x^j).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.sourceCoordinateEquiv_apply_sum` (characterisation): Coefficient extraction of Σ_p c_p(x^i⊗x^j) is exactly c, for every coefficient family c.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.sourceCoordinateEquiv_monomial` (simp): The coefficient family of the vector x^i⊗x^j indexed by p is single(p,1), zero at every other index.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.sourceCoordinateEquiv.test_one` (degenerate): For n=1 and arbitrary f, the coefficients of 1⊗1 are single((0,0),1).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.sourceCoordinateEquiv.test_zero_ring` (degenerate): If A is subsingleton, coefficient extraction of every element of B⊗_A B is the zero coefficient family.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.sourceCoordinateEquiv.test_nonreduced` (computation): For A=Z/4,n=2,f=2, the coefficient of x⊗x at (1,1) is 1. The calculation uses the nonreduced quotient, not its reduction.

**Acceptance.** The construction fixes coefficient order and basis normalization, rather than choosing an unspecified isomorphism of free modules. Its specified inverse also determines the map over the zero ring.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-kernel; how: Provides the specified native coefficient extraction for the module comparison; the explicit synthesis inverse keeps the actual tensor map visible.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-kernel-coefficients; how: Supports interpreting the coefficient criterion for a tensor through a fixed inverse formula and generator normalization.

#### Target character tensor coordinates

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-target-coordinates` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Every z∈H⊗_A B has a unique coefficient family d:(Fin n×Fin n)→A with z=Σ_(i,k)d_(i,k)(e_i⊗x^k), where e_i is indexed by i modulo n, not by an A-valued root of unity.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

2. In the nontrivial branch construct the quotient basis from AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' and reindex by natDegree(Xⁿ−f)=n. Use the existing MonoidAlgebra.basis for all elements of Multiplicative(ZMod n).
3. Reindex characters through Multiplicative.toAdd and the inverse of ZMod.finEquiv n. By ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt, the forward Fin index i corresponds to the canonical residue class of i.val; MonoidAlgebra.basis_apply identifies its vector with e_i.
4. Tensor the actual character and root bases; tensorProduct_apply' fixes the vector e_i⊗x^k. The native equivFun sum and inverse formulas give existence and uniqueness. This uses the group-algebra basis, never the set of A-valued roots of unity.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-monomial"></a>

#### Weighted permutation formula

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-monomial` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For 0≤i,j<n, Θ(x^i⊗x^j)=f^⌊(i+j)/n⌋(e_i⊗x^((i+j) mod n)). The exponent is zero or one. The target index σ(i,j)=(i,(i+j) mod n) is a permutation: its inverse sends (i,k) to (i,k−i) when k≥i and to (i,n+k−i) when k<i.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-tmul`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-tmul), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction-weight`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction-weight), `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-root-power-reduction`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-root-power-reduction).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the pure-tensor formula and the coaction weight law to obtain e_i⊗x^(i+j).
2. Use the actual quotient relation xⁿ=f and Euclidean division i+j=nq+r. Tensor balancing moves f^q to the coefficient.
3. Check the two displayed inverse indices are between zero and n−1, with sum wrapping exactly in the k<i branch. This proves bijectivity of σ without cancellation in A.

**Acceptance.** The n=2 column (1,1) maps to f times target (1,0), explaining both branch and nonunit obstructions.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3.1 pp.14–16, character grading and Corollary 3.13, P=N The finite root-chart action motivates this root-specific coordinate calculation. Nonunit obstructions and matrix formulas are derived here using the listed native algebra declarations; no geometric stack theorem is inferred.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-weight-product` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For any commutative A, f∈A and n≥1, the product over p∈Fin n×Fin n of f^floor((p₁+p₂)/n) is f^E, E=n(n−1)/2.

**Hypotheses.** n≥1. Matrix and weight-product assertions use any commutative coefficient ring A and f∈A; index and sign assertions are independent of A. No nonzerodivisor, unit, reducedness or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Rewrite each weight as f on wrapping columns and1 on other columns.
2. Import the filtered product identity and constant product law. Identify the filter cardinality with the actual wrapping subtype.
3. Consume the existing native wrapping_card result; do not re-plan ordered-pair counting.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-root-pullback"></a>

#### Pullback of native root objects and arrows

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-root-pullback` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For n≥1 and (L,s) on T, define h*:Root(T,L,s,n)→Root(Y,h*L,h*s,n). Send (M,t,φ) to (h*M,h*t,h*φ∘κ(h,M,n)); send a root arrow a to h*a. The two arrow conditions are preservation of the section and φ_target∘a^n=φ_source. The resulting functor preserves both conditions and all automorphism labels. Given an isomorphism of target pairs, transport the last identification by that isomorphism; do not change the root section.

**Hypotheses.** T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.; Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.; n≥1; Root is the parent’s root-object groupoid, with only invertible line maps as arrows.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-object), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-power-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-power-pullback), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power-transport`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power-transport), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the parent root-object definition without redefining its carrier. Apply native line pullback to M and every isomorphism, and the supplier’s section pullback to t and s.
2. Compose κ with the pulled φ. The power-pullback section equation and functoriality give φ′(t′^n)=s′.
3. Apply pullback to each arrow square and use κ’s naturality; the separate pulled section equation proves the other arrow condition. Identity and composition are the inherited functor laws.
4. An isomorphism of target pairs gives a root functor by composing φ with the target line isomorphism; the assertion on s verifies its object equation.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback` (constructor): The functor on root objects and actual root arrows described above.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback_line` (projection): The root line is h*M, using the existing rank-one pullback.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback_section` (projection): The root section is h*t, through the actual section-pullback map.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback_identification` (projection): The identification is h*φ∘κ(h,M,n), including the indicated comparison of its domain.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback_arrow` (simp): The underlying line isomorphism of a pulled arrow is h*a.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.transportTarget` (functoriality): An isomorphism (L,s)≅(L′,s′) acts by postcomposing φ; identity and composite target transports agree.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback.test_identity` (compatibility): Pullback by id is naturally isomorphic to the original root, via the native line-pullback identity isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback.test_nilpotent` (computation): The normalized root y=2 over Z/4, n=2, f=0 pulls to y=0 over Z/2.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback.test_stabilizer` (non-example): At y=0 over Z/4, n=2, the unit −1 labels an automorphism distinct from identity; its Z/2 pullback is identity.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback.test_target` (compatibility): Changing the target frame by unit b multiplies the power-identification coefficient and f by b and leaves y unchanged.

**Acceptance.** No flatness condition is imposed on h.; A nonidentity automorphism can become identity under pullback.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-target-coordinate-equivalence"></a>

#### Target coefficient equivalence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-target-coordinate-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For B=A[x]/(xⁿ−f), H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)] and any commutative ring A with positive n, construct the specified A-linear equivalence H⊗_A B ≃ ((Fin n×Fin n)→A) extracting the unique coefficients in the ordered vectors e_i⊗x^k. The inverse coefficient map sends c to Σ_p c_p(e_i⊗x^k). This is the native linear equivalence determined by synthesis, including the zero ring.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-target-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-target-coordinates), `mathlib:LinearEquiv.ofBijective`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Define the native synthesis linear map by the finite linear combination in the statement. Linearity follows from addition and scalar multiplication distributing over a finite sum.
2. The listed coordinate existence-and-uniqueness lemma proves synthesis bijective: uniqueness gives injectivity and existence gives surjectivity.
3. Apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective to synthesis and take its inverse. The inverse evaluation is the exact sum, the forward evaluation of a synthesized family follows from the inverse law, and synthesis of a single coefficient gives the generator formula.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.targetCoordinateEquiv_symm_apply` (projection): The inverse coefficient map sends c to Σ_p c_p(e_i⊗x^k).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.targetCoordinateEquiv_apply_sum` (characterisation): Coefficient extraction of Σ_p c_p(e_i⊗x^k) is exactly c, for every coefficient family c.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.targetCoordinateEquiv_monomial` (simp): The coefficient family of the vector e_i⊗x^k indexed by p is single(p,1), zero at every other index.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.targetCoordinateEquiv.test_one` (degenerate): For n=1 and arbitrary f, the coefficients of 1⊗1 are single((0,0),1).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.targetCoordinateEquiv.test_zero_ring` (degenerate): If A is subsingleton, coefficient extraction of every element of H⊗_A B is the zero coefficient family.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTorsorComparison.targetCoordinateEquiv.test_wild_character` (computation): For A=F₂,n=2,f=0, the coefficient of e₁⊗1 at (1,0) is 1. This character remains visible although μ₂(F₂) has only one element.

**Acceptance.** The construction fixes coefficient order and basis normalization, rather than choosing an unspecified isomorphism of free modules. Its specified inverse also determines the map over the zero ring.

The weighted matrix, kernel and cokernel formulas are explicit derivations below, not standalone theorems quoted from the paper. <a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-root-coherence"></a>

#### Coherent root pullback on the scheme site

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-root-coherence` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For a fixed scheme X and (L,s) on X, T→X maps to Root(T,L_T,s_T,n) with L_T=T*L and s_T=T*s. The root pullback functors form a groupoid-valued pseudofunctor on (Sch/X)^op. Its identity and composition natural isomorphisms have the native line-pullback identity and composition isomorphisms as underlying components, corrected on the target L_T by the same comparisons. They preserve sections and root identifications. The triangle and pentagon hold, and every finite iterated pullback agrees with direct pullback through these specified comparisons.

**Hypotheses.** T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.; Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.; Fix n≥1. Coherence is equality of the specified natural transformations after associators; no strict equality of chosen pullback objects is asserted.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-root-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-root-pullback), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-power-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-power-pullback), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackId`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Restrict the supplier’s coherent native Picard pullback to roots using the section law and κ-composition law. Correct both the root line and the pulled target line; correcting only M gives an ill-typed φ square.
2. For identities use the native unit comparison. For a pair of morphisms use the native composition comparison on M and L and its compatibility with the n-th power.
3. Underlying line isomorphisms satisfy triangle and pentagon by the supplier’s coherence. Equality of root arrows reduces to their underlying line maps, because the two preservation conditions are properties.
4. Induct on a finite chain; the pentagon compares all bracketings. This is the general root-object coherence target beyond the parent’s chosen affine two- and three-step comparisons.

**Acceptance.** The n=1 root functor has the identity-pair groupoid behaviour.; A four-map chain has equal composite comparison arrows for all parenthesizations.; Nonflat coefficient change preserves these diagrams even when it identifies distinct arrows.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, printed pp. 52–54 The object description is base-change compatible. Our proof uses the imported monoidal pseudofunctor coherence to make this compatibility precise. [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3, Remark 3.1 and Proposition 3.4, pp. 12–13; Corollary 3.13, p. 16 Proposition 3.4 gives finite root base-change compatibility in the logarithmic setting; it motivates, rather than supplies in native Lean, the pair-level comparison here.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.RootObject.pullback_coherent`.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-determinant` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-frame-change"></a>

#### Coordinates under changes of source and target frames

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-frame-change` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

If e′=mul(a)∘e and l′=mul(b)∘l for units a,b∈Bˣ, the same root has coordinates y′=a*y, u′=b*u*a^{-n}, f′=b*f. This induces a groupoid equivalence from the framed coordinates for l to those for l′, with object formula (u,y)↦(b*u,y) when e is retained. Changing root frames e_p,e_q by a_p,a_q changes an arrow label to w′=a_q*w*a_p^{-1}. Both arrow equations are preserved. Root-frame changes with b=1 are connected by the identity native root arrow, whose coordinate label between the two readings is a. These comparisons have inverse unit formulas and composition cocycles.

**Hypotheses.** Use the conventions of native-framed-equivalence. n≥1; no condition on section y.; The target unit b is common to the source and target of a root arrow.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-framed-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power-transport`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power-transport), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-identification-unit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-identification-unit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/framed-groupoid`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-framed-groupoid).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Conjugate the scalar power identification by c_n and the two changed frames. The parent section-power transport gives (mul(a))^n=mul(a^n) under c_n, so the coefficient becomes b*u*a^{-n}.
2. Conjugating e_q∘h∘e_p^{-1} gives w′=a_q*w*a_p^{-1}. Substitute this into both arrow equations; cancel only the named units.
3. Compose frame changes by multiplying a and b. The identity native root arrow compares different readings of the same root, and its power square supplies u′*a^n=b*u.
4. These are calculations from the imported section/unit comparison, not new general scalar-automorphism or tensor coherence APIs.

**Acceptance.** At y=0 the u equation still carries information.; Over Q, n=2, u=1,y=1,f=1, a=2,b=1 gives u′=1/4,y′=2; omitting a^{-n} breaks the root equation.; For e_p changed by2 and e_q unchanged, w=1 becomes w′=1/2.; Target-frame changes require no root of b until one insists on normalized coefficient1.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, printed pp. 52–54 The G_m quotient and power action in B.1–B.2 lead to these gauge formulas. The signs and factors are authored computations with the fixed source/target coordinate conventions.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.framedNativeEquiv.changeFrames`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-injective"></a>

#### Sharp injectivity criterion

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-injective` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The A-algebra comparison Θ is injective iff n=1 or the map a↦fa on A is injective.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-kernel-coefficients`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-kernel-coefficients), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-source-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-source-coordinates), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-source-synthesis`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-source-synthesis).

**Construction/proof.**

1. For n=1 every coefficient is nonwrapping, so the kernel criterion makes the kernel zero.
2. For n>1 the source position (1,n−1) is wrapping. Place a−b there; if fa=fb the kernel criterion kills its actual synthesized tensor. Injectivity and source coefficient extraction imply a=b.
3. Conversely apply the kernel criterion to the source coordinate family of z−w. Injectivity of multiplication by f kills every wrapping coefficient, and target equality gives z=w.

**Acceptance.** For Z,n=2,f=2 the map is injective although f is not a unit.; The separate native proof extraction checks this declaration with no admission dependency. This is evidence for the unchecked plan, not certification of the whole suggested file or geometric root stack.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-kernel"></a>

#### Coordinate kernel equivalence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-kernel` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let W={(i,j)∈Fin n×Fin n:n≤i+j}. The native A-linear kernel of Θ is A-linearly equivalent to functions W→ann_A(f), where ann_A(f) is the kernel of multiplication by f on A. The forward map sends a kernel tensor to its W-coordinates in the source monic basis.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-kernel-coordinate-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-kernel-coordinate-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-source-synthesis`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-source-synthesis).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Take the specified wrapping kernel coordinate equivalence.
2. Apply its extraction formula and the existing source coefficient formula on every finite basis expansion. This proves the original existential statement with its specified forward map.

**Acceptance.** At n=1 W is empty, so the kernel is zero for every f, including f=0.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3.1 pp.14–16, character grading and Corollary 3.13, P=N The finite root-chart action motivates this root-specific coordinate calculation. `FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-coefficient-naturality` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

Fix A,f,n≥1 and the trivial target pair on Spec A. For every A-algebra map ψ:B→C, pull chosen native root frames along Spec ψ using the canonical pulled-unit comparison. <a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-local-normalization"></a>

#### Every native root has local normalized affine coordinates

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-local-normalization` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For any scheme T and native root (M,t,φ) of (L,s), n≥1, there is an fppf covering of T refining an affine Zariski covering which trivializes both M and L. On each affine member Spec B, native coordinates give (u,y) with u∈Bˣ and u*y^n=f. Refine it by the parent singleton cover Spec D→Spec B, D=B[T]/(T^n−u). The existing unit r=T in D has r^n=u, and the pulled root is isomorphic to the native chart image with coordinate r*y and coefficient1. The root isomorphism has label r. The construction retains both arrow equations and is stable under arbitrary pullback of test schemes; it asserts existence of local frames, not a functorially chosen global frame.

**Hypotheses.** T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.; Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.; n≥1. The family of affine trivializing opens can have arbitrary size allowed by the site; T need not be quasi-compact.; A positive exponent is essential for the finite-free unit-root cover; zero is not a covering exponent.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.ofIsInvertible`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-root-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-root-pullback), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-framed-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-chart-realization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-chart-realization), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-coefficient-naturality`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-coefficient-naturality), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/framed-fppf-cover`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-framed-fppf-cover), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/framed-normalization-iso`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-framed-normalization-iso), `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.affineCover`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the existing local trivialization atlases of M and L, intersect their opens, and refine by affine opens. Restriction/pullback comparison with native modules comes from AlgebraicVectorBundles, not a new general local-freeness theory.
2. Read the two frames through the native equivalence. Apply the parent positive-exponent finite-free, finite-presentation and singleton-cover package to the unit coefficient u.

<a id="rs-1"></a>

## RS.1 — Finite root stacks and relative geometry

Compare the native triple groupoid with the upstream line-section two-pullback. Universal roots and finite charts come from that supplier. The remaining native geometry must retain wild exponents, relative stack bases, a smooth frame atlas and the nonreduced closed fibre. A finite diagonalizable quotient can be tame without being Deligne–Mumford. The precise coarse universal property is not replaced by equality of invariant rings.

**Planets.** Root stacks — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks); Root stack comparison — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-upstream-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-upstream-equivalence); Universal root — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-universal-root-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-universal-root-comparison); Affine root quotient — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-quotient-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-quotient-comparison); Coarse space of a root stack — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-coarse-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-coarse-space); Regular root stack — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-regularity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-regularity).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Worked geometric checks

Take A=Z/4, n=2 and the trivial root line with section zero and power
identification coefficient 3. A normalized frame would require a unit r with
r²=3. No element of Z/4 satisfies this. The root nevertheless exists, and its
normalization cover is finite locally free and fppf. Consequently the quotient
must allow nontrivial torsors and effective descent. A quotient of A-valued
chart points by μ₂(A) misses this root. This also separates two different maps:
W→R is a μ₂-torsor, whereas W→Spec A is just the monic root cover and need not
be a torsor.

For a zero target section over a field K and n=2, take the test ring
K[ε]/ε². The root with t=ε has square zero, but cannot be isomorphic to the
root with t=0: an invertible module map cannot kill ε. The two roots have the
same reduced point. This is why the full fibre is the quotient of the
nilpotent chart and the closed gerbe is obtained by imposing t=0, a stronger
equation. For char K=p and n=p the group μ_p has only the identity K-point,
but the dual-number unit 1+ε is a nonidentity μ_p-point. Geometric-point
cardinality alone detects neither the full fibre nor the DM obstruction.

For X=A¹_F_p, D=(x) and n=p, the frame atlas has equation z^p=qx.
Eliminating x identifies it with Spec F_p[z,q,q^−1]. It is a regular smooth
atlas of the root stack. The finite chart itself is a μ_p-torsor over the
stack and is not a smooth atlas. Thus the root stack is regular, algebraic and
tame, but is not DM at its branch point. Regularity and the DM condition use
different hypotheses. Taking s=1 instead gives X for every n, with trivial
relative inertia even in characteristic p.

Over Spec Z with s=2,n=3, the only branch locus is V(2), where 3 is a unit.
The root stack is DM everywhere although 3 is not a unit on the whole base.
This concrete case detects the unnecessarily strong global invertibility
condition. For a stack base BG_m with s=1, all root fibres are trivial relative
to the base, but the base automorphisms remain. Relative coarse and relative
DM assertions cannot silently become absolute ones.
