#### Root stacks of line bundles and sections

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks` · imported contract / native comparison · implementation unchecked.

For n≥1 and a line bundle with section (L,s) on a scheme X or an algebraic stack X, define √[n]{(L,s)/X} on T→X as the groupoid of root objects of (L_T,s_T). Pullback and its coherent isomorphisms define the fibred stack. For an effective Cartier divisor D use (O_X(D),s_D). Arbitrary exponents use the fppf topology; the étale description is asserted only when n is invertible.

**Ownership.** The generic finite object/construction is imported, not planned again. This stable local contract records its native InvertibleSheaf/section/arrows specialization and compatibility with the chosen affine coordinates; RS.2 owns the coherent infinite diagram and its constraints. Supplier: SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, 3.4; AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0B.

**Hypotheses.** The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-object), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.Grothendieck`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fppfTopology`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the supplier’s line-bundle pullback and descent, retaining the root isomorphism and section equation.
2. Root-object morphisms descend since equality of sheaf maps is local; glue the line bundles, sections and φ effectively.
3. For a stack base, pull back to an atlas and descend with the same definition; do not replace the stack base by a coarse space.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.object` (characterisation): The fibre over T→X is exactly the root-object groupoid of (L_T,s_T).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.forget` (projection): Forget root data to the base T→X.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.baseChange` (functoriality): A base morphism induces pullback of root data with identity/composition coherence.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.universalRoot` (universal-property): The stack carries the universal line bundle, section and n-th-power isomorphism; maps into it are equivalent to such root data.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.affinePresentation` (compatibility): For a scheme affine chart X=Spec A and a trivialized (L,s)=(O,f), the root stack is [Spec A[t]/(t^n−f)/μ_n] with the grading action; this is the RS.1/affine-chart comparison, including wild exponents.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.coarseComparison` (universal-property): For a scheme base the projection is the coarse moduli map, is an isomorphism away from V(s), and has affine invariant algebra A. For an algebraic-stack base use the relative coarse assertion after scheme base change (RS.1/coarse-space).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.closedFibre` (characterisation): Over a geometric zero of s the full fibre is [Spec k[t]/(t^n)/μ_n], while its reduction is Bμ_n; this exposes RS.1/closed-fibre without discarding nilpotent root sections.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.regularDM` (compatibility): For a regular scheme X and regular Cartier divisor D the root stack is regular; it is DM when n is invertible. A geometric branch point of characteristic dividing n has non-étale μ_n inertia (RS.1/regular-dm).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.transitionLimit` (functoriality): The finite map from order nm to n sends (M,t) to (M^m,t^m), coherently under composition and base change. The infinite root stack is the genuine groupoid two-limit with these transition isomorphisms (RS.2/transition and infinite-root-stack).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.dvrGerbe` (compatibility): For a DVR, after choosing a neutralization the reduced infinite closed fibre is B_k lim_n μ_n in the fpqc topology; its isomorphism classes are H1_fpqc(k,lim_n μ_n), with the origin dependent on that choice (RS.2/dvr-infinite-gerbe and dvr-kummer-classes).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_exponent_one` (degenerate): The n=1 stack is equivalent to X over X.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_unit_section` (compatibility): For (O_X,1), every exponent gives a stack equivalent to X.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_zero_section` (non-example): Over an algebraically closed field, (O,0) at invertible n>1 has μ_n automorphisms and is not the coarse point.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_stack_base` (compatibility): At n=1 over BG the output is BG, rather than Spec k.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_affine_cartier` (computation): For X=Spec k[x], f=x and n=3, recover [Spec k[x,t]/(t³−x)/μ_3] with ζ·t=ζt, retaining the stack action as well as the ring.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_coarse_grading` (non-example): In characteristic p with n=p, the μ_p grading still gives (A[t]/(t^p−f))^{μ_p}=A; using only geometric μ_p(k)-points would incorrectly make every function invariant.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_nilpotent_fibre` (non-example): For n=2 and k of characteristic not two, the root t=ε over k[ε]/(ε²) is a nonzero section in the zero fibre, which a pure Bμ_2 replacement would lose.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_wild_branch` (non-example): For X=Spec k[x], D=V(x), char k=p and n=p, the root stack is regular but not DM along x=0; the unit-section case remains X even at this exponent.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_transition_coherence` (compatibility): A fourth root maps to its square at order two and then to its fourth power at order one, agreeing with the direct transition and its base changes. Unrelated finite roots without transition isomorphisms are not an infinite object.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack.test_dvr_origin` (compatibility): For a DVR the reduced infinite fibre has lim_n μ_n automorphisms after neutralization; changing the chosen origin translates its H1_fpqc coordinate, rather than canonically identifying all torsor classes with the trivial one.

**Acceptance.** At n=1 the projection is an equivalence. For an invertible section it is an equivalence for every n, including p|n.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.2, pp. 53–54: scheme-base triples and classifying-stack fibre product; algebraic-stack bases are an atlas-descent extension, not a sentence in this appendix. AGV gives the root-object definition for scheme bases. The extension to an algebraic-stack base uses the separately requested atlas and descent infrastructure; AGV Appendix B does not itself state that extension.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.rootStack`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-invariant-coefficient-criterion"></a>

#### Vanishing of the positive-degree invariant coefficients

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-invariant-coefficient-criterion` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For b=Σ_{i∈Fin n} c_i t^i, δ(b)=1⊗b if and only if c_i=0 for every i≠0.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor, finiteness, Noetherianity or invertibility-of-n assumption is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction-diagonal-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction-diagonal-coordinates), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction-constant-row-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction-constant-row-coordinates), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-torsor-target-coordinate-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-torsor-target-coordinate-equivalence).

**Construction/proof.**

1. If the tensors agree, compare their native coordinates at (i,i) for every nonzero i: the diagonal coefficient is c_i while the zero character row is zero.
2. Conversely all positive coefficients vanish; the diagonal and zero-row formulas agree at every coordinate, and injectivity of the existing coordinate equivalence identifies the tensors.

**Acceptance.** Retain the zero ring and wild characteristic; character weights are detected universally, not through field-valued points.

**Sources.** [AFFINE-INVARIANTS-J6LwjP](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Printed pp. 14–16: character grading before Lemma 3.7, its degree-zero proof and Corollary 3.13 finite chart, P=N The finite arbitrary-section calculation is derived here from the same character grading, using the existing native monic quotient and tensor bases; it is not attributed as a verbatim general theorem of the paper.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.invariants_sum_iff`.

#### Root stacks as a two-fibre product

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/two-pullback` · imported contract / native comparison · implementation unchecked.

Let A=[A¹/G_m] classify a line bundle with section and [n]:A→A take its n-th tensor power. The root stack is X×_{A,[n]}A with its universal root. For a stack base this is a two-fibre product, including the specified isomorphism, not an equality pullback of coarse points.

**Ownership.** The generic finite object/construction is imported, not planned again. **Construction/proof.**

1. Unpack a two-pullback object: (x,(M,t),φ) with φ identifying (Mⁿ,tⁿ) and (L_x,s_x).

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-invariants"></a>

#### Invariants of an affine root chart

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-invariants` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For every b∈B=A[t]/(tⁿ−f), δ(b)=1⊗b if and only if b=algebraMap(a) for some a∈A. Thus the scheme-theoretic invariant subalgebra is precisely the coefficient image, for all commutative A, f∈A and n≥1, including characteristic dividing n.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-coaction-weight`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-coaction-weight), `mathlib:Polynomial.monic_X_pow_sub_C`, `mathlib:Polynomial.natDegree_X_pow_sub_C`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.powerBasis'`, `mathlib:MonoidAlgebra.basis`, `mathlib:Module.Basis.tensorProduct`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-invariant-coefficient-criterion`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-invariant-coefficient-criterion).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Separate the subsingleton coefficient-ring case: its unital algebra B and tensor algebra are subsingleton, so both assertions hold with a=0. This avoids invoking the polynomial degree theorem without its nontriviality hypothesis.
2. For nontrivial A, Xⁿ−f is monic and has nat-degree n. Import the native monic AdjoinRoot power basis and reindex along that equality to write b uniquely as ∑_{0≤i<n} a_i t^i. The generic quotient basis is already library mathematics.
3. Use the weight lemma and the tensor-product basis of the native group-algebra basis and root power basis. In δ(b), a_i occurs at (i mod n,i); in 1⊗b it occurs at (0,i). For 0<i<n these index pairs differ, forcing a_i=0. This remains valid with torsion or nilpotents; it never divides by n or averages over field-valued points.
4. Only a_0 remains, giving b=algebraMap(a_0). Conversely the A-algebra-map law and tensor scalar relation give δ(algebraMap(a))=1⊗algebraMap(a).
5. Apply the separate native diagonal/zero-row coefficient criterion to the existing monic power-basis expansion, and use the coefficient algebra map for the reverse direction. The exact-pin native proof retains the separate zero-ring branch.

**Acceptance.** At n=1 every element is a coefficient. At f=0 the nilpotent root powers remain independent. In characteristic p, field-point invariance is strictly weaker than δ-invariance.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — §3.1 pp. 14–16, character grading before Lemma 3.7 and finite chart of Corollary 3.13, P=N Root-specific coordinate calculation derived here from the finite P=N character grading. Native Hopf, quotient and basis declarations are imported, not rebuilt. This is not a claimed verbatim theorem of the paper.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.affineCoaction.invariants`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-root-fpqc-descent"></a>

#### Fpqc descent of finite root data

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/root-fpqc-descent` · imported contract / native comparison · implementation unchecked.

For every positive n and line bundle with section (L,s), the finite root-object pseudofunctor is a stack for the pinned fpqc topology, including on scheme test objects over a stack base. Thus its fppf restriction and its fpqc construction give the same root objects and arrows on every test scheme; the stronger descent assertion is a theorem, not an automatic change of topology.

**Ownership.** The generic finite object/construction is imported, not planned again. This stable local contract records its native InvertibleSheaf/section/arrows specialization and compatibility with the chosen affine coordinates; RS.2 owns the coherent infinite diagram and its constraints. Supplier: SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, 3.4; AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0B.

**Hypotheses.** Any fpqc scheme cover; a fixed (L,s) and positive n.; Tensor and unit pullback comparisons are the explicit JAC-A contract.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks), `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fpqcTopology`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3/fpqc-quasicoherent-descent`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3/finite-locally-free-descent`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/tensor-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-tensor-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the imported QCoh descent equivalence to the root line; rank-one finite-local-free detection makes the descended module invertible.
2. Regard a section as a module map O→M. Fullness descends that map, and the unit comparison identifies its domain.
3. Tensor/pullback comparisons identify the power of the descended line with the descent of the local powers. Descend the power isomorphisms and their inverses using full faithfulness.
4. The displayed section equation holds after the covering pullbacks; faithfulness makes it hold globally.
5. Apply the same full faithfulness to isomorphisms of root data and check their section and power equations; this proves effective object descent and sheaf descent for arrows.

**Acceptance.** No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition3.10 proof p.16 and Definition3.8 p.15; fpqc quotient description; QCoh supplier is Stacks023T Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-effective-descent"></a>

#### Effective descent of the native root data

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-effective-descent` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For a scheme T, a native pair (L,s), an integer n≥1 and any fpqc cover U={T_i→T}, the canonical functor D_U:Root_n(T;L,s)→Desc_U(Root_n(L,s)) is an equivalence of groupoids. Its underlying module comparison is the restriction of the imported equivalence QCoh(T)≃Desc_U(QCoh), not a descent functor on chosen frames. The equivalence descends the root line, its section, its power identification and every root arrow, with the native tensor and pullback comparisons. It is compatible, up to specified natural isomorphisms, with refinement of covers and arbitrary base change of T.

**Hypotheses.** Schemes and covers lie in one fixed universe-bounded site; category values may lie in a larger universe.; No Noetherian, separation, finiteness or flatness hypothesis on a subsequent base-change map.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-root-coherence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-root-coherence), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-pseudofunctor`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3/finite-locally-free-descent`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fpqcTopology`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fppfTopology`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent on all quasi-coherent modules and all linear maps. Descend M_i and the transition isomorphisms; finite-locally-free-descent, including rank, makes the result a native invertible sheaf.
2. Through the imported strong symmetric monoidal pullback, identify the descended tensor power with M^n and the descended unit with O_T. Descend t_i as maps O→M and descend φ_i:M_i^n→L_i and φ_i inverse. Faithfulness checks that these maps are inverse and that φ(t^n)=s.
3. Fullness descends each compatible root arrow and its inverse; faithfulness detects its two defining squares, equality and the cocycle. This proves full faithfulness as well as essential surjectivity.
4. Compare two effective descents by the unique isomorphism inducing their local comparison. The same uniqueness proves refinement, base-change, identity and composition coherence; no chosen global frame enters.

**API.**

- `FiniteRoot.descentEquiv` (equivalence): The functor D_U is an equivalence; its unit and counit are root isomorphisms with the native underlying module descent unit and counit.
- `FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_section` (compatibility): The counit identifies the restriction of the descended t:O_T→M with t_i, through the unit and line-pullback comparisons.
- `FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_powerIso` (compatibility): After the tensor-power pullback comparison, the counit carries the restricted descended φ and its inverse to φ_i and φ_i inverse.
- `FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_hom` (characterisation): Compatible local isomorphisms descend uniquely to an isomorphism carrying t to t′ and satisfying φ′∘a^n=φ; neither condition is omitted.
- `FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_refine` (functoriality): For a refinement V→U, the two effective-descent equivalences are compared by their unique root isomorphism inducing the refinement counit; identity and composite refinements satisfy the triangle and pentagon.
- `FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_baseChange` (functoriality): Pulling the descent datum to Y→T and then descending is naturally isomorphic to pulling the descended root to Y; the comparison preserves t,φ and has the native pullback identity/composition laws.

**Checks.**

- `FiniteRoot.descent_identity` (degenerate): For the singleton identity cover, D_U is equivalent to the identity root functor with its native pullback-unit isomorphism.
- `FiniteRoot.descent_zero_automorphism` (non-example): For n=2 over Q and the zero root section, the arrows with unit labels 1 and −1 remain distinct after descent along any fpqc cover; replacing the fibres by isomorphism classes fails this test.
- `FiniteRoot.descent_nontrivial_line` (compatibility): For the Zariski cover of P¹_Q by its two standard affines, descend local frames of M=O(1), t=0, φ:M^2≅L=O(2). The descended root line is O(1), which has no global frame.
- `FiniteRoot.descent_nonflat_change` (compatibility): For the root (O,t=2,φ=identity) of (O,4) over Z and n=2, base change to F₂ descends to the zero-section root. The comparison does not cancel t or require Z→F₂ flat.

**Acceptance.** Every descent object is recovered with its section and power identification.; D_U induces a bijection on every Hom set, including the automorphisms of a zero-section root.

**Consumers.** where: RS.1 native-quotient-comparison and RS.0 native-stackification-equivalence; how: Makes the native root pseudofunctor an fpqc stack before identifying it with a geometric quotient.; where: RS.2 root towers; how: Supplies effective finite-level descent without imposing a global frame.

**Sources.** [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu) — Proposition 35.5.2 (023T) and Lemma 35.7.6 (05B2); tag pages, no fixed pagination Effective descent includes noninvertible module morphisms; finite locally free rank is fpqc local. Restricting these statements and the tensor comparison yields this root-specific equivalence. #### Coefficient equivalence with the affine invariant algebra

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-invariant-algebra-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Let I be the native AlgHom.equalizer of δ:A[t]/(t^n−f)→A[Z/n]⊗_A A[t]/(t^n−f) and the right inclusion b↦1⊗b. Construct the A-algebra equivalence A≃I induced by the actual coefficient map.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor, finiteness, Noetherianity or invertibility-of-n assumption is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-invariants`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-invariants), `mathlib:AlgHom.equalizer`, `mathlib:AlgHom.mem_equalizer`, `mathlib:AlgHom.codRestrict`, `mathlib:AlgEquiv.ofBijective`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.of.injective_of_monic_of_degree_pos`, `mathlib:Polynomial.degree_X_pow_sub_C`, `mathlib:Algebra.ofId`.

1. Use the native algebra-map equalizer and codomain restriction; coefficient coinvariance proves membership. This imports generic equalizer theory rather than constructing a second invariant predicate.
2. The existing affine-invariants theorem supplies surjectivity. The existing positive-degree monic AdjoinRoot coefficient-injectivity theorem supplies injectivity, with the zero-ring branch handled directly.
3. Apply the native bijective algebra-hom equivalence constructor. Its forward value is the coefficient inclusion and its inverse is the unique coefficient of the same invariant element.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineInvariantEquiv.apply_coe` (simp): For a∈A, the underlying root-chart element of affineInvariantEquiv(a) is the actual coefficient image of a.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineInvariantEquiv.inverse_coe` (compatibility): For x in the native invariant subalgebra I, including its inverse coefficient back into the root chart gives the underlying element x.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineInvariantEquiv.eq_iff` (characterisation): For x∈I and a∈A, the inverse coefficient of x equals a if and only if the underlying root-chart element of x equals the coefficient image of a.

**Checks.**

- `AffineInvariantTests.equivalence_linear_root` (computation): For A=Z/11, n=1 and f=7, the inverse invariant-algebra equivalence sends the actual root to 7.
- `AffineInvariantTests.equivalence_nilpotent` (computation): For A=Z/4, n=2 and f=0, the inverse equivalence recovers coefficient 2, and its image remains square-zero in the root chart.
- `AffineInvariantTests.equivalence_zero_ring` (degenerate): For a subsingleton coefficient ring, the inverse invariant-algebra equivalence sends every invariant element to 0 for every positive exponent.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-upstream-equivalence"></a>

#### Comparison with the upstream root stack

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-upstream-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

At T, it sends (x,M,t,φ) to the 2-pullback object (x,(M,t),φ), using the native line-section comparison; it sends (a:x→x′,b:M≅M′) to the corresponding pair of arrows with the same compatibility square. For a stack base, the square uses a to identify x*L with x′*L. The quasi-inverse retains the actual isomorphism φ and its section equation. E is pseudonatural in T and in isomorphisms of target pairs.

**Hypotheses.** X is a scheme or an algebraic stack on the fixed universe-bounded fppf site.; For a stack base, L and s mean compatible native sheaves and sections on all scheme test objects, as in SF.1/stack-quasi-coherent.

2. Apply the objectwise categorical-pullback universal property, retaining the comparison isomorphism and its section-preservation equation. On arrows use exactly the root-arrow square, including the arrow of X.
3. Full faithfulness of the line-section equivalence and the 2-pullback give full faithfulness of E; lifting a line-section object and its identification gives essential surjectivity.

**API.**

- `FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_hom` (characterisation): The map on Hom sets is bijective and retains both the root section square and power-identification square, as well as the arrow of X.
- `FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_pullback` (functoriality): For h:Y→T the strong naturality isomorphism has underlying native line-pullback comparison; its identity and composition modifications satisfy triangle and pentagon.
- `FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_targetIso` (functoriality): An isomorphism (L,s)≅(L′,s′) postcomposes φ and commutes with E; identity and composition comparisons use those of the native tensor/pullback API.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre"></a>

#### Full and reduced root-stack fibres

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre` · imported contract / native comparison · implementation unchecked.

For a geometric point x with s(x)=0, the full fibre is [Spec κ(x)[t]/tⁿ /μ_n]. Its reduction is Bμ_n. If s(x)≠0 the fibre is the point. For n>1 the full closed fibre must not be identified with its reduced gerbe.

**Ownership.** The generic finite object/construction is imported, not planned again. This stable local contract records its native InvertibleSheaf/section/arrows specialization and compatibility with the chosen affine coordinates; RS.2 owns the coherent infinite diagram and its constraints. Supplier: SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, 3.4; AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0B.

**Hypotheses.** The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/base-change`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-base-change), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-chart), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Pull the chart back to the geometric field, keeping the quotient ring tⁿ.
2. For s(x)=0 pass to the reduction t=0, then identify the residual classifying gerbe.
3. For s(x)≠0 the solution scheme is a μ_n-torsor and its quotient stack is the point.

**Acceptance.** Over Q at n=2 the full fibre has t≠0 and t²=0; only its reduction is Bμ₂.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.2, p. 53: nilpotent closed embedding of the root gerbe into the zero-section fibre. The source distinguishes the full zero-section fibre from its root gerbe. At a geometric field this is the nilpotent quotient chart and its reduced classifying gerbe.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/coarse-space` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For a scheme base X, the projection of the root stack to X is its coarse-space morphism. For an algebraic-stack base, it is relative coarse over X: after scheme base change it has the preceding coarse property. It is not an assertion that X is an absolute algebraic space.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-universal-root-comparison"></a>

#### Universal root and its classifying property

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-universal-root-comparison` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Under E, the upstream universal line U_n, section τ_n and power identification α_n:U_n^n≅π*L pull back to the accepted universal native root. For any scheme T→X, giving a map T→R_n over X with its base 2-identification is equivalent, naturally in T, to giving a native root (M,t,φ) on T; arrows of maps correspond to root isomorphisms. Pullback of the universal triple gives this equivalence and identifies both φ(t^n)=s and the two equations on arrows. Universality is a groupoid equivalence, not a bijection on isomorphism classes.

**Hypotheses.** Same X,L,s,n and universe bounds as native-upstream-equivalence.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-upstream-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-upstream-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/line-bundle-section-stack`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Evaluate the second projection of the upstream 2-pullback and its structural 2-isomorphism. The line-section comparison gives U_n,τ_n,α_n.
2. Apply the 2-Yoneda equivalence to native-upstream-equivalence. Naturality yields the classifying map and its action on arrows; full faithfulness gives uniqueness up to unique compatible 2-isomorphism.

**Acceptance.** Pullback along a classifying map recovers the whole input root triple, including φ.; For s=0 over a field, universal automorphisms retain their μ_n labels.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, pp.52–54 The tautological root line in the quotient and 2-pullback presentations gives the universal triple; the native comparison identifies that triple.

**Suggested name.** `FiniteRoot.nativeUniversalRoot`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-regular-dm"></a>

#### Regularity and the tame DM condition

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/regular-dm` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

If X is a regular scheme and D is a regular effective Cartier divisor, √[n]{(O(D),s_D)/X} is regular; when n is invertible on X it is Deligne–Mumford with μ_n inertia over D and trivial inertia outside D. If a geometric branch point has characteristic dividing n, its μ_n inertia is not étale, so the stack is not DM there. An empty divisor still gives X in every characteristic.

**Hypotheses.** X is a regular scheme, D is a regular effective Cartier divisor (possibly empty), and n is a positive integer. Use fppf root stacks for arbitrary n; the DM assertion requires n invertible on X.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-chart), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. On a local trivialization use the smooth G_m-torsor atlas V_σ from AGV B.2, with coordinates z,q,q⁻¹ and equation zⁿ=qf. At z=0, f cuts out a regular divisor, so zⁿ−qf has a nonzero linear regular-parameter term. At z≠0 the equation forces f to be a unit and solves for q. Verify these local rings are regular with the requested regular-divisor interface.
2. Descend regularity along this smooth G_m atlas. The finite chart Spec A[t]/(tⁿ−f)→root stack is only a μ_n torsor in general; when n is not invertible it is not a smooth atlas and must not by itself be used for smooth-local regularity descent.
3. For invertible n the branch inertia μ_n is étale, giving the DM condition. At a branch point of characteristic dividing n the same inertia is non-étale and obstructs DM; outside the divisor the root stack is the base.

**Acceptance.** On a DVR the n=2 root is regular in odd residue characteristic; the assertion is not that arbitrary sections cut regular divisors.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.2, pp. 53–54: the G_m quotient atlas; regularity is the local regular-parameter argument in proofSteps, rather than a smooth/normal-crossing theorem printed here. The G_m atlas can test regularity even at wild exponents. The requested regular-divisor and geometric quotient interfaces supply the commutative-algebra and descent details; Appendix B does not state a general regularity theorem.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-quotient-comparison"></a>

#### Native affine roots and the torsor quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-quotient-comparison` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let X=Spec A, choose a frame l of L and write s=f·l. Put W=Spec A[z]/(z^n−f), with the weight-one μ_n action on z. Under E the native root stack is equivalent to the existing quotient [W/μ_n] over X, naturally in arbitrary ring maps and compatibly with changes of l. For a native root, the sheaf P of frames e of M satisfying φ(e^n)=l is a μ_n-torsor; the coordinate t=z e defines a map P→W. With right action e·ζ=ζe, its coordinate satisfies z(e·ζ)=ζ^−1 z(e); this is equivariance for the left weight-one action on W. Conversely a torsor and such a map descend O_P,t and φ. This is an equivalence of groupoids, including torsor isomorphisms, not just an orbit-set calculation.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring and n≥1.; The frame l is local data; changes of l use the native frame-change comparisons, not globally chosen n-th roots.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-effective-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-effective-descent), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-upstream-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-upstream-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-basechange-square`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-basechange-square), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-local-normalization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-local-normalization), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-framed-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-framed-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-frame-change`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-frame-change), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/native-coefficient-naturality`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-native-coefficient-naturality), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/root-stack`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The normalized-frame sheaf is locally nonempty by RS.0/native-local-normalization; two frames differ by a unique μ_n section, proving the torsor identity. This uses fppf covers even in wild characteristic.
2. On P the root is trivialized; its section and power isomorphism satisfy the displayed equations. Effective descent constructs the inverse on objects and arrows.
3. Compare with the upstream affineChart via its tautological normalized root. The equality on frames and arrows determines the natural isomorphism by full faithfulness.
4. Use native-basechange-square and the RS.0 frame-change/coefficient comparisons for arbitrary ring maps and noncanonical frame changes; the cocycles are root isomorphisms.

**Acceptance.** For f=0 and n>1, W→Spec A is not a μ_n-torsor in general; W→[W/μ_n] is the torsor used here.; For A=Z/4, n=2, the root with t=0 and φ coefficient 3 need not have an A-valued normalized frame; its torsor still gives an object of the quotient.; The formula z(e·ζ)=ζ^−1z(e) prevents reversing the associated-line convention.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.2, pp.53–54 Normalize the power identification using an fppf μ_n-torsor to obtain the finite affine equation. [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Corollary 3.13, p.16, rank-one chart P=N The finite logarithmic root chart is a finite diagonalizable torsor quotient; the rank-one case agrees with this affine root chart.

**Suggested name.** `FiniteRoot.nativeAffineQuotient`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-native-smooth-presentation"></a>

#### A smooth presentation valid for wild roots

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/native-smooth-presentation` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For the affine pair (A,f) put V_n(f)=Spec A[z,q,q^−1]/(z^n−q f). Give it the left G_m action λ·(z,q)=(λz,λ^nq). The map V_n(f)→R_n(Spec A;O,f) sends (z,q) to the trivial root line with section z and power identification of coefficient q^−1. ## RS.2 — Coherent infinite roots and fpqc Kummer towers

Use the finite transitions as a pseudodiagram, then form compatible objects with their arrows and cocycles. Normalized coframes produce genuine finite torsor towers; their limit is an fpqc torsor, whose equivariant evaluation gives the infinite quotient. The intrinsic DVR zero-section gerbe needs an origin only for its Kummer coordinates. Compatible roots of two over Q separate fpqc from fppf local triviality.

**Planets.** Infinite root stacks — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-root-stack`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-root-stack); Infinite DVR root gerbe — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-infinite-gerbe`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-infinite-gerbe); Finite-free root transitions — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-faithfully-flat`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition-faithfully-flat); Infinite Kummer torsors — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit); Infinite affine root charts — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-affine-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-affine-quotient); Infinite unity-root coordinates — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-unit-qz-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-unit-qz-equivalence).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Worked boundary cases

**Zero root and its coframes.** For M=O, t=0 and φ=identity, the normalized
coframe torsor is μn and its evaluation map is zero. The root chart is
Spec k[z]/z^n. Conflating the torsor and chart would lose precisely the
distinction needed to reconstruct the root line at a vanishing section.

**A nonzero nilpotent root.** At exponent 2 over a field, the class of z in
k[z]/z² is nonzero and has square zero. The accepted transition injections
preserve it in the infinite chart. For every r, choose n>r; z_n^r remains
nonzero. Thus each zero-constant chart element is nilpotent, while the ideal
of all root coordinates has no fixed nilpotence exponent. The zero-section
gerbe is the quotient of the reduced chart, not the full fibre.

**Wild inertia.** In characteristic p, μp(k) contains only one element, but
on k[ε]/ε² the unit 1+ε is a nonidentity pth root of unity. It gives a
nonidentity automorphism of the zero-section p-root over that test scheme.
Every band and torsor statement therefore retains the full group scheme.

**Factorial compatibility.** A root at degree 6! induces a root at degree
5 by the 144th tensor power. Its comparison with a 5!-based extension is
provided by the factorial transition and the tensor-power compositor. The
comparison is an isomorphism of section-bearing roots; equality of their
classes would supply neither this arrow nor its compatibility at larger stages.

**Identity on Kummer representatives.** The quotient of z⁴=2 through
μ4→μ2 has coordinate w=z² and equation w²=2. Hence K_4(Q)→K_2(Q) sends
[2] to [2]. Squaring the representative would give [4]=1 and is the wrong
coordinate transition.

**The sign of the origin change.** In a chosen basis e of a zero-section
root y, write φ(e^n)=aλ. The coframe coefficient satisfies b^n=a. An arrow
x_λ→y instead has scalar c with a c^n=1, so the Isom coordinate is [a^−1].
For λ′=vλ the coefficient becomes a/v and the new Isom coordinate is
[v/a]=[v][a^−1]. In particular y=x_λ has old coordinate one and new
coordinate [v]. This checks both the band inversion of coframes and the
change-of-origin theorem. For π′=uπ, the normal-line frame scales by u^−1,
giving the residue-unit shift [u_bar^−1].

**Compatible classes with no rational frame.** The classes [2]_n over Q
lift to the actual tower z_n^n=2. Its fpqc limit exists, but a rational
point would include a rational square root of 2. An fppf-local point would
restrict to a finite residue field extension containing roots of 2 of
every degree, contradicting the imported degree bound. Finite local
triviality at each stage is insufficient for infinite fppf triviality.

**Real points.** Over ℝ, μ_n(ℝ) = {±1} for even n, but a compatible family
(ζ_n) satisfies ζ_n = ζ_2n² = 1, so G(ℝ) = lim μ_n(ℝ) is trivial: the trivial
root system over ℝ has no nontrivial automorphism, although each finite
component of even degree has two. The Kummer coordinates K_n(ℝ) are {±1} for
even n and trivial for odd n, and the compatible families are the trivial one
and ([−1]_n)_n. So the zero-section gerbe over ℝ has exactly two isomorphism
classes of real points; the nontrivial one comes from the tower z_n^n = −1,
which is trivial at odd degrees.

### Target catalogue

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-transition"></a>

#### Divisibility transition morphisms

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/transition` · imported contract / native comparison · implementation unchecked.

For positive m,n the transition √[mn]{(L,s)}→√[n]{(L,s)} sends (M,t,φ) to (Mᵐ,tᵐ,φ), using the coherent identification (Mᵐ)ⁿ≅Mᵐⁿ. Transitions are compatible with base change and with multiplication of positive integers.

**Ownership.** The generic finite object/construction is imported, not planned again. This stable local contract records its native InvertibleSheaf/section/arrows specialization and compatibility with the chosen affine coordinates; RS.2 owns the coherent infinite diagram and its constraints. Supplier: SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, 3.4; AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0B.

**Hypotheses.** The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/tensor-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-tensor-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/base-change`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-base-change).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use tensor-power reassociation from the line-bundle supplier.
2. Apply the same reassociation to the section equation.
3. The supplier’s monoidal coherence identifies composite transitions on root objects and arrows.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.transition.object` (simp): The root line and section become Mᵐ and tᵐ.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.transition.one` (simp): The m=1 transition is the identity.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.transition.comp` (functoriality): Transitions for a and b compose to the transition for ab with the specified coherence.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.transition.test_identity` (degenerate): Transition from n to n is identity.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.transition.test_four_to_two` (computation): A fourth root (M,t) maps to the square root (M²,t²).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.transition.test_base_change` (compatibility): Pulling a transition back to Y gives the transition of the pulled-back section.

**Acceptance.** The map is over X; n divides mn, and the direction goes from the finer root to the coarser root.

**Consumers.** where: TV Proposition 3.5; how: Provides the compatible diagram whose inverse limit is the infinite root stack.; where: Bresciani p. 135; how: Transition maps identify the finite DVR root tower.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition 3.2 and divisibility functors p. 13

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.transition`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-roots"></a>

#### DVR roots and change of uniformizer

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-roots` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

For a DVR A with uniformizer π and closed divisor D, the n-th root is [Spec A[t]/(tⁿ−π)/μ_n]. Replacing π by uπ gives a canonically equivalent stack as a root of the same Cartier pair; it does not require choosing an n-th root of u in A.

**Hypotheses.** The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-chart), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Identify the two trivializations of O(D), whose change-of-frame is u.
2. Transport the Cartier pair through this isomorphism and use the root universal property.
3. Keep the torsor of possible chart lifts rather than choosing a nonexistent scalar root of u.

**Acceptance.** For A=Z_(p), a unit need not have an n-th root; the stack construction is nevertheless uniformizer-independent.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p. 135 finite-root definition and uniformizer independence

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition"></a>

#### Affine divisibility transition

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For B_n=A[T]/(T^n−f) and positive n,m, construct the A-algebra homomorphism j_(n,m):B_n→B_(nm) sending its distinguished root to the mth power of the target root. Constants are unchanged. This is the contravariant affine-chart map for the stack transition from an nmth root to an nth root.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring; all exponents appearing as denominators are positive.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:AdjoinRoot`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.algHom_ext`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-root-relation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-root-relation).

**Construction/proof.**

1. In B_(nm), compute (t_(nm)^m)^n=f using the native distinguished-root relation.
2. Apply the native A-algebra quotient lift with root value t_(nm)^m. Its coefficient algebra is the algebra induced by this particular map.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.root` (simp): j_(n,m)(root_n)=root_(nm)^m.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.constant` (simp): j_(n,m) fixes the image of every coefficient in A.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.unique` (extensionality): An A-algebra map with the displayed root image equals j_(n,m).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.coefficientAlgebra` (instance): Use j_(n,m) as the coefficient map for the B_n-algebra structure on B_(nm); retain the original A-algebra and its compatible coefficient tower.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.test_one` (degenerate): The m=1 map is identity, with the evident exponent identification.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.test_four_to_two` (computation): For n=m=2 the coarse chart root maps to the square of the fourth-root chart variable.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransition.test_nilpotent` (non-example): For f=0, n=m=2 over a field, the source nilpotent root maps to the nonzero square of the target variable in k[u]/u^4; it is not killed.

**Acceptance.** No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

**Consumers.** where: TV17 Proposition3.2 and Section3.1; how: Makes the ring maps in the divisibility inverse system concrete.; where: Bresciani p.135; how: The finite DVR root tower uses these maps before taking its limit.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Section3.1 pp.14–16, P=N specialization Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-degree-bound"></a>

#### A degree bound for roots of two

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-degree-bound` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

If K/Q is a finite field extension and x∈K satisfies x^n=2 for positive n, then n≤[K:Q]. In particular no finite extension of Q contains compatible nth roots of2 for every positive n.

**Hypotheses.** K is a field with a Q-algebra structure and finite dimension over Q; n>0.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion`, `mathlib:Polynomial.IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast`, `mathlib:minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic`, `mathlib:minpoly.natDegree_le`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The monic integer polynomial X^n−2 satisfies Eisenstein at (2): nonleading coefficients are divisible by2 and its constant coefficient is not divisible by4.
2. Gauss comparison makes X^n−2 irreducible over Q.
3. Its root equation and monicity identify it with minpoly_Q(x).
4. The native degree bound gives n≤finrank_Q K. Choose n larger than that dimension to exclude roots at all levels.

**Acceptance.** For K=Q, only the n=1 case can have a root of2. A quadratic field may contain a square root but cannot contain a cube root of2. All positive n, including composite n, are covered by Eisenstein.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p.133 finite versus infinite torsor topology; explicit counterexample derivation by the listed Eisenstein and minimal-polynomial statements Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-iterated-reverse"></a>

#### Reverse map from the larger root chart

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/iterated-reverse` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Put D_(n,m)=B_n[U]/(U^m−t_n) as the native monic AdjoinRoot quotient with its inherited A-algebra. Construct v_(n,m):B_(nm)→D_(n,m) as an A-algebra homomorphism sending t_(nm) to the actual distinguished root U.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring; f∈A and n,m are positive natural numbers. No reducedness, Noetherian, unit-parameter or invertibility-of-exponent hypothesis is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-root-relation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-root-relation), `mathlib:AdjoinRoot`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom`, `mathlib:IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. In D_(n,m), U^m is the image of t_n, so U^(nm)=(U^m)^n is the image of f under the coefficient tower.
2. Apply the native A-algebra quotient lift using that equation. Keep the actual coefficient algebra and the quotient nilpotents.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.root` (simp): v_(n,m)(t_(nm))=U in D_(n,m).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.constant` (simp): v_(n,m) sends each a∈A in B_(nm) to its image in D_(n,m).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.coefficient` (compatibility): For every b∈B_n, v_(n,m)(j_(n,m)(b)) equals the coefficient image of b in D_(n,m).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.test_root` (computation): Over every field k with f=0 and n=m=2, the reverse map sends t_4 exactly to the distinguished U in B_2[U]/(U²−t_2), fixing its sign as well as its square.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.test_coefficient` (computation): For n=m=2, v_(2,2)(t_4²) is the coefficient image of t_2 in B_2[U]/(U²−t_2).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.test_fourth_power` (compatibility): For n=m=2, v_(2,2)(t_4⁴) equals the coefficient image of f from A in the iterated quotient.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse.test_zeroRing` (degenerate): When A is the zero ring, the reverse map sends every element to zero in the actual iterated quotient.

**Acceptance.** This is an actual map of the native quotient algebras for arbitrary A, rather than a map between representative coefficient arrays.

**Consumers.** where: TV17 §3.1, P=N finite local charts; how: The reverse lift supplies the specified inverse in the iterated quotient, needed for finite chart freeness.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-iterated; how: Its coefficient compatibility upgrades the A-algebra map to a B_n-algebra inverse.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Section3.1 pp.14–16, P=N specialization Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.affineIteratedReverse`.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-divisibility` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For positive n,N with h:n divides N, construct the actual A-algebra map B_n→B_N sending t_n to t_N^(N/n), on the native AdjoinRoot quotients. Its target is B_N itself, so its identity and composition need no quotient-carrier transports.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring and f∈A; every divisibility exponent n,N,K is positive. Factorial levels are (i+1)! for i∈N, so none is zero. No reducedness, Noetherian, unit-parameter or invertibility-of-exponent hypothesis is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/affine-root-relation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-affine-root-relation), `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The exact divisibility identity (N/n)n=N makes the proposed root image solve T^n−f in B_N.
2. Use the native quotient algebra lift, which fixes every A coefficient.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineDivisibility` (constructor): For positive n,N with h:n divides N, construct the actual A-algebra map B_n→B_N sending t_n to t_N^(N/n), on the native AdjoinRoot quotients. Its target is B_N itself, so its identity and composition need no quotient-carrier transports.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineDivisibility.root` (simp): The actual divisibility map sends the distinguished root t_n exactly to t_N^(N/n).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineDivisibility.constant` (compatibility): The actual map fixes every coefficient from A.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineDivisibility.unique` (extensionality): An A-algebra homomorphism with the specified root image equals the actual fixed-index transition.

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineDivisibility.multiplicative` (compatibility): At N=nm the fixed-index map B_n→B_(nm) equals the previously specified actual affine transition j_(n,m).

The root-object groupoids, factorial cofinality equivalence and infinite affine fpqc quotient retain their independent geometric/coherence obligations.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-root-divisibility-index"></a>

#### Positive divisibility root indices

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-divisibility-index` · definition · implementation unchecked.

The root-chart index stores an exponent n∈N and a proof n>0. Its preorder is n≤N exactly when n divides N, with decidable comparison, nonzero exponents and distinguished index 1. Products supply common upper bounds. The factorial adapter sends i∈N to d_i=(i+1)!.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A, and B_n is the actual AdjoinRoot algebra A[T]/(T^n−f). Root exponents are positive. No nontriviality, reducedness, Noetherian, unit-parameter or invertible-exponent hypothesis is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsDirected`, `mathlib:IsDirectedOrder`, `mathlib:Nat.factorial_pos`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Instantiate the native Preorder with divisibility reflexivity and transitivity; do not use numeric order.
2. The product nN is positive and divisible by both n and N, giving the native directed-order instance.
3. Use positivity of factorials for the adapter; no generic colimit or competing quotient carrier is defined.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootDivIndex` (constructor): The root-chart index stores an exponent n∈N and a proof n>0. Its preorder is n≤N exactly when n divides N, with decidable comparison, nonzero exponents and distinguished index 1. Products supply common upper bounds. The factorial adapter sends i∈N to d_i=(i+1)!.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootDivIndex.factorial` (functoriality): The factorial index has actual exponent (i+1)!, definitionally on the specified carrier.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootDivIndex.cofinal` (compatibility): Every positive index n divides d_(n.exponent).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.RootDivIndex.factorial_mono` (functoriality): If i≤j in numeric order, d_i divides d_j.

**Checks.**

- `rootDivIndex.test_zero` (non-example): Every root index has nonzero exponent; including exponent zero is rejected.
- `rootDivIndex.test_two_six` (computation): The index 2 precedes 6 in the divisibility preorder.
- `rootDivIndex.test_numeric_order` (non-example): The index 2 does not precede 3, despite 2<3 numerically.

**Acceptance.** Use the actual quotient rings and native directed colimits; keep every finite root and coefficient map visible.; This algebra comparison leaves coherent root arrows, grading, Spec limits and fpqc torsor/quotient comparisons as separate obligations.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-affine-quotient; how: Identify its actual all-divisibility affine algebra with the factorial algebra, with explicit finite coordinates; retain the separate geometric comparison contracts.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition 3.5, Remark 3.6 and Section 3.1, printed pp.13–16; rank-one local models Authored root-algebra comparison derived from the source’s divisibility and cofinal local-model constructions. These algebra declarations are not literal named theorems of the paper and do not establish its coherent root-groupoid or fpqc quotient equivalence.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.RootDivIndex`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-root-scalars"></a>

#### Coherent factorial root-of-unity points

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-root-scalars` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Define the subgroup S(A) of families σ:N→Aˣ such that σ_i^(d_i)=1 and σ_j^(d_j/d_i)=σ_i for every i≤j. Its identity, products and inverses are pointwise native unit operations. This is an A-valued point interface, not a replacement for the universal group scheme.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A and d_i=(i+1)! for i∈N. C_f is the existing actual factorial chart colimit with roots u_i and inclusions. No reducedness, Noetherian condition, coefficient field, invertibility of exponents or unit condition on f is imposed.; A coherent scalar is a family σ_i∈Aˣ satisfying σ_i^(d_i)=1 and σ_j^(d_j/d_i)=σ_i for all i≤j. The native carrier is a subgroup of the function group N→Aˣ; it models ring-valued points only. It is not the universal diagonalizable group scheme, its Hopf algebra or its fpqc torsors.; Algebra maps fix every coefficient. Scaling is u_i↦σ_i u_i. Inverse and composition use the actual inherited subgroup operations and native algebra-map equivalences, with actual inverse proofs.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Subgroup`, `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the native function group of units. The displayed root equations and compatibility define its subgroup.
2. Unit powers preserve identity and, since A is commutative, pointwise products; inverse powers preserve the same equations. Construct the actual subgroup instances, rather than assume closure.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.factorialRootScalars` (constructor): Define the subgroup S(A) of families σ:N→Aˣ such that σ_i^(d_i)=1 and σ_j^(d_j/d_i)=σ_i for every i≤j. Its identity, products and inverses are pointwise native unit operations. This is an A-valued point interface, not a replacement for the universal group scheme.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.factorialRootScalars.pow` (compatibility): For σ∈S(A), the underlying scalar σ_i∈A satisfies σ_i^(d_i)=1.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.factorialRootScalars.transition` (compatibility): For i≤j and σ∈S(A), the underlying ring values satisfy σ_j^(d_j/d_i)=σ_i.

**Checks.**

- `factorialRootScalars.test_one` (degenerate): The identity scalar family has value1 at every index.
- `factorialRootScalars.test_inverse` (compatibility): The actual inverse family cancels its scalar at each index in the native unit group.
- `factorialRootScalars.test_individual_roots` (non-example): Over Z the family with value−1 at index1 and1 elsewhere satisfies every individual d_i-th-root-of-unity equation.
- `factorialRootScalars.test_incoherent` (non-example): That family over Z is not coherent: the index2-to-index1 cube transition would require1=−1. Individual finite orders do not define an infinite point.

**Acceptance.** Define the subgroup S(A) of families σ:N→Aˣ such that σ_i^(d_i)=1 and σ_j^(d_j/d_i)=σ_i for every i≤j. Its identity, products and inverses are pointwise native unit operations. This is an A-valued point interface, not a replacement for the universal group scheme.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-unit-cyclic-character"></a>

#### The universal finite cyclic root character

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/unit-cyclic-character` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Define χ_n:Multiplicative(ZMod n)→*B_n by χ_n([k])=t_n^val(k), where B_n=A[T]/(T^n−1).

**Hypotheses.** A is an arbitrary commutative ring in one fixed universe; n is a positive natural number. If N occurs it is positive and n divides N. #### Normalized finite root character in Q/Z

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/qz-character` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For n>0 define the additive homomorphism c_n:Z/n→Q/Z by c_n([k])=[k/n] for every integer k. This is the unique lift of the integer map k↦[k/n].

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring in a fixed universe. Every finite exponent is positive; divisibility maps require n divides N. No nontriviality, reducedness, flatness, field or invertibility hypothesis is imposed.; The character group is the actual AddCircle of period 1 over the rationals, namely Q/Z; its group algebra means the actual MonoidAlgebra A (Multiplicative (AddCircle (1:Q))). The unity-root algebra U_A is the inherited FactorialAffineColimit(1).; Original QZCoordinates-codex-J6LwjP checkpoint: these planning declarations had admitted, then-uncompiled prototypes. The current separate native proof evidence does not certify the full canonical geometric file or the fpqc quotient.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:ZMod.lift`, `mathlib:AddCircle.coe_eq_zero_iff`, `mathlib:AddCircle.coe_period`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The integer map preserves addition. At n its value is [1]=0; descend it through ZMod.lift. This specifies its orientation, rather than merely choosing an isomorphism with an abstract cyclic subgroup.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.intCast` (simp): For k∈Z, c_n([k])=[k/n], including negative k.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.one` (simp): The chosen character sends [1] to [1/n].
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.injective` (characterisation): The homomorphism c_n is injective for every n>0.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.divisibility` (functoriality): If n divides N, then c_N([(N/n) val(k)])=c_n(k) for k∈Z/n. Thus c_N([N/n])=[1/n].
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.exhaustive` (compatibility): For every u∈Q/Z there are n>0 and k∈Z/n with c_n(k)=u.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.natCast` (simp): For every n>0 and k∈N, c_n([k])=[k/n], without reducing k before forming the rational quotient.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.apply` (simp): For n>0 and k∈Z/n, c_n(k)=[val(k)/n], where 0≤val(k)<n.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.test_one` (degenerate): At n=1 the character of [1] is zero.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.test_orientation` (non-example): At n=3, c_3(1) differs from [2/3]; reversing the chosen generator fails.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.test_two_six` (computation): The 2-to-6 transition sends [1] to [3], whose image is [1/2].
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.test_natcast_period` (computation): At n=3 the unreduced natural representative 7 maps to [7/3].
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineQZCharacter.test_negative_representative` (computation): At n=3 the canonical natural representative of −1 is 2, and its character is [2/3].

**Acceptance.** For n>0 define the additive homomorphism c_n:Z/n→Q/Z by c_n([k])=[k/n] for every integer k. This is the unique lift of the integer map k↦[k/n].

#### Actual algebra-valued finite root points

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-point-carrier` · construction · implementation unchecked.

**Hypotheses.** A,B,C are arbitrary commutative rings in a common universe, B and C are A-algebras, f∈A is arbitrary, and every root index is positive. The exponent need not be invertible. No reducedness, nontriviality, regularity, unit-section, Noetherian, injectivity or flatness hypothesis is imposed.; This is the finite affine chart action groupoid of actual algebra-valued points. The general scheme/stack-base line-bundle root groupoids, frame torsors, fppf stackification and infinite fpqc quotient/descent remain separate recorded obligations.

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineRootPointGroupoid.root_equation` (compatibility): Every actual point p satisfies p(t)^n=algebraMap_A,B(f), including over wild or nonreduced rings.

- `TauCeti.RootStack.rootPointTests.zero_test_ring` (degenerate): All actual second-root points at f=0 over the zero test ring Z/1 are equal.
