<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-transition-native"></a>

#### Native root transition pseudodiagram

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/transition-native` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For a scheme X with invertible sheaf L and section s, form the root-groupoid diagram indexed by positive integers with the arrow m→n when n divides m. At T→X, F(n,m) sends (M,t,φ) to (M^(m/n),t^(m/n),φ), using the specified tensor-power comparison to interpret φ. On arrows it takes tensor powers. Supply unit constraints and composition isomorphisms F(n,m)F(m,l)≅F(n,l), including their coherence and compatibility with arbitrary scheme pullback.

**Hypotheses.** Native finite root groupoids from RS.0–RS.1, using the core of InvertibleSheaf, not its full category.; One fixed coefficient universe and explicitly lifted object/morphism universes; no same-universe assertion for all schemes.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-object), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/tensor-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-tensor-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/base-change`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-base-change), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/transition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-transition).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Take the tensor-power functor and its section comparison supplied by RS.0 and SF.3. Transport the root equation through the associativity comparison.
2. Construct each compositor from the specified power associativity isomorphism. Its root-section equation and arrow naturality follow from the corresponding RS.0 laws.
3. Use the unit and associativity coherence of those same comparisons to obtain the pseudodiagram laws. Finite pullback comparisons induce a strong transformation of diagrams, including its modification laws.
4. Under the comparison of the RS.0–RS.1 native root groupoids with rootStack n (L,s) of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21, each F(n,m) is that roadmap's rootStack.transition. §1.21 states the transition maps only; the unit and compositor constraints, their coherence and their pullback modifications are the RS.2 content of this node.

**API.**

- `RootTransition.map` (functoriality): Object and arrow maps are tensor powers, with both root equations preserved.
- `RootTransition.unitIso` (compatibility): The n→n functor is coherently isomorphic to the identity.
- `RootTransition.compIso` (compatibility): For n|m|l, the specified natural isomorphism compares the composite with F(n,l) and satisfies the triple-composition law.
- `RootTransition.pullbackIso` (compatibility): Pullback commutes with each transition, with its unit and composite diagrams.

**Checks.**

- `RootTransitionTests.one` (degenerate): The 1-root diagram evaluation agrees with the groupoid of the given pair; its transition unit is retained.
- `RootTransitionTests.six` (compatibility): For 2|6|30 the two tensor-power routes preserve t^15 and the given power identification under the associativity isomorphism.
- `RootTransitionTests.zeroArrow` (non-example): On a zero-section root of exponent 6, a scalar ζ in μ6 is sent at exponent 2 to ζ^3, not to the identity in general.

**Acceptance.** For n|m|l and a root (M,t,φ), the compositor F(n,m)F(m,l)(M,t,φ) ≅ F(n,l)(M,t,φ) is the tensor-power associativity isomorphism (M^(l/m))^(m/n) ≅ M^(l/n) assembled from InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductAssoc and the unit isomorphisms; for n = m = l it is the unit constraint.; On objects and arrows each F(n,m) agrees with rootStack.transition of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21.; On the zero-section root (O,0,id) of exponent 6 over T, F(2,6) sends the automorphism ζ ∈ μ6(T) to ζ³ ∈ μ2(T).

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coherent-roots-native; how: The transitions and compositors define the compatibility equations.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-tower; how: Power comparisons determine the finite coframe-torsor transitions.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition 3.2 and the paragraph preceding it, p.13 Transitions and composition in the monoidal-functor model motivate this native line-bundle specialization. Strict equality in that model is not imposed on tensor powers. [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.2, p.53 The objects and arrows retain the section and the power identification.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-normalized-coframes"></a>

#### Normalized coframes of a finite root

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/normalized-coframes` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For a root (M,t,φ:M^n≅O_T) of (O_T,f), let P_n be the sheaf of coframes β:M≅O_T with β^n=φ. This sheaf is represented by a finite locally free μn-torsor of rank n. Use LEFT action ζ·β=ζβ. The coordinate x_n(β)=β(t) satisfies x_n^n=f and x_n(ζ·β)=ζ x_n(β). Root isomorphisms act by β↦β h^−1. This is the normalized coframe torsor; the chart t^n=f itself is a torsor only when f is a unit.

**Hypotheses.** A positive n, arbitrary scheme T, actual invertible sheaf and root section.; The target line has been trivialized; gluing for a general L uses root-limit-descent-native.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/root-object`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-root-object), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-chart), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-affine-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-affine-quotient).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Choose a Zariski local basis of M. If φ of its nth power is the unit a, normalized coframes are given by an invertible coefficient b with b^n=a.
2. Globally P_n is the relative spectrum over T of the O_T-algebra ⊕_(0≤i<n) M^(⊗i), with multiplication M^(⊗i) ⊗ M^(⊗j) → M^(⊗(i+j)) followed by φ in degrees ≥ n (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.1 relative Spec). It is finite locally free of rank n, locally O_T[b]/(b^n − a), and it is the μ_n-torsor attached to the pair (M,φ) in the description of H¹_fppf(T,μ_n) by line bundles with a trivialized nth power (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11; Stacks Lemma 59.28.5, tag 040Q). No gluing beyond relative Spec is needed, and n need not be invertible.
3. Evaluate t in the normalized coframe. The root equation gives x_n^n=f; scaling the coframe gives the LEFT scaling convention. Transport along a root arrow preserves normalization and the evaluation map.

**API.**

- `RootCoframe.torsor` (structure): P_n is a represented μn-torsor with LEFT scalar action, finite locally free of rank n.
- `RootCoframe.evaluation` (projection): Evaluation has equation x_n^n=f and the specified weight-one equivariance.
- `RootCoframe.mapIso` (functoriality): A root isomorphism h sends β to β h^−1 and preserves evaluation.
- `RootCoframe.pullbackIso` (compatibility): Formation of P_n and evaluation commutes with arbitrary pullback.
- `RootCoframe.localEquation` (characterisation): In a basis with φ(e^n)=a, P_n has equation b^n=a, where a is a unit, independently of whether f vanishes.
- `RootCoframe.relativeSpecIso` (characterisation): P_n ≅ Spec_T(⊕_(0≤i<n) M^(⊗i)), multiplied through φ in degrees ≥ n; the μ_n-action is the grading, ζ acting on M^(⊗i) by ζ^i.

**Checks.**

- `RootCoframeTests.zero` (non-example): For M=O, φ=identity, t=0, P_n=μn and evaluation is zero; Spec k[z]/z^n is not this torsor for n>1.
- `RootCoframeTests.unit` (computation): For M=O, t=c, φ(e^n)=a, P_n is b^n=a and evaluation is bc, hence (bc)^n=ac^n=f.
- `RootCoframeTests.wild` (compatibility): For n=p in characteristic p, the μp coframe torsor uses its full finite flat group scheme, even though μp(k) is trivial.
- `RootCoframeTests.nonflat` (compatibility): Reduction modulo a nilpotent ideal pulls back the coframe torsor and evaluation, without asserting injectivity on root arrows.

**Acceptance.** In a local basis e with φ(e^n) = a, P_n is Spec O_T[b]/(b^n − a) with a a unit, whether or not f vanishes, and the coordinate is x_n = b·c where t = c·e.; For the zero root (O,0,id), P_n is μ_n itself, while the chart fibre Spec k[z]/(z^n) is not a torsor for n > 1.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-tower; how: The normalized power condition makes every finite transition a torsor map.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-evaluation; how: The coframe coordinates construct the equivariant infinite chart map.

**Sources.** [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1–B.2, pp.52–54 Finite line-root and root-with-section presentations yield this normalized coframe specialization; no nonvanishing section is assumed. [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Definition 3.8 and Proposition 3.10, pp.15–16 The quotient requires a torsor and an equivariant chart map as distinct pieces of data. [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu) — Lemma 59.28.5 (tag 040Q) The fppf H¹ of μ_n is the group of pairs of a line bundle and a trivialization of its nth power; the coframe torsor is the torsor attached to (M,φ).

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-flat-torsor-tower-limit"></a>

#### Limits of finite flat torsor towers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let T be a scheme. Let G_n (n ≥ 1) be commutative group schemes over T, each finite locally free, with homomorphisms π(n,m): G_m → G_n for n|m such that π(n,n) is the identity, π(n,m)π(m,l) = π(n,l), and each π(n,m) is faithfully flat with finite locally free kernel. Put G = lim G_n, an affine flat group scheme over T. Let P_n be fppf G_n-torsors with π(n,m)-equivariant T-morphisms p(n,m): P_m → P_n, p(n,n) = id and p(n,m)p(m,l) = p(n,l). Then: (a) each p(n,m) is a torsor under ker π(n,m), hence finite locally free and surjective; (b) the limit P = lim P_n exists, is affine over T, and over an affine open U ⊆ T its coordinate ring is the directed colimit of those of the P_n|U; (c) P → T is faithfully flat, so {P → T} is an fpqc covering; (d) the action map G ×_T P → P ×_T P, (g,x) ↦ (gx,x), is an isomorphism, so P is an fpqc G-torsor, and for every n the G-map P → P_n induces an isomorphism P ×^G G_n ≅ P_n of G_n-torsors; (e) formation of P commutes with every base change T′ → T; (f) G-equivariant T-morphisms P → Q between two such limits correspond bijectively to compatible families of G_n-equivariant morphisms P_n → Q_n; (g) for every fpqc G-torsor Q the pushforwards Q_n = Q ×^G G_n are fppf G_n-torsors and the canonical map Q → lim Q_n is an isomorphism. Hence fpqc G-torsors and such towers, with equivariant maps, form equivalent groupoids. Neither finite presentation of P nor fppf-local triviality of P is asserted.

**Hypotheses.** T is an arbitrary scheme; the index set is the positive integers ordered by divisibility, which is directed.; Each G_n is finite locally free over T and each transition G_m → G_n is faithfully flat with finite locally free kernel. For G_n = μ_n,T and ζ ↦ ζ^(m/n) the transition is the qth-power map, q = m/n: the coordinate ring of μ_m is free of rank q over that of μ_n, and the kernel is μ_q.; Each P_n is an fppf G_n-torsor; the tower maps are equivariant and compose exactly.

**Prerequisites.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fpqcTopology`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.flat_and_surjective_iff_faithfullyFlat_of_isAffine`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. (a) Fppf locally on T choose a section of P_m, so P_m ≅ G_m; then p(n,m) becomes π(n,m) followed by a translation of G_n. π(n,m) is finite, flat and of finite presentation with kernel K = ker π(n,m), and G_m ×_(G_n) G_m ≅ G_m × K, so it is a K-torsor. These properties are fpqc local on the base (Stacks 02KY, 02L2, 02LA).
2. (b) The transition maps are finite, hence affine, and P_1 is finite over T, so the limit exists and is computed affine-locally (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9 affine_transition_limits; Stacks 01YW, 01YX). Over U = Spec R it is Spec of the directed colimit of the coordinate rings of the P_n|U.
3. (c) Each P_n|U is finite locally free and surjective over U, so its coordinate ring is a faithfully flat R-algebra; a directed colimit of faithfully flat R-algebras is faithfully flat (Stacks 090N). Translate with flat_and_surjective_iff_faithfullyFlat_of_isAffine. P is affine over T, hence quasi-compact, and {P → T} is an fpqc covering.
4. (d) Fibre products commute with limits: G ×_T P = lim(G_n ×_T P_n) and P ×_T P = lim(P_n ×_T P_n), and the action map is the limit of the finite action isomorphisms. The G-map P → P_n factors through P ×^G G_n (pushforward along G → G_n, merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3 NonabelianH1.map and §1.16), a G_n-map of G_n-torsors, hence an isomorphism (§1.15 Torsor.hom_isIso).
5. (e) Pullback of affine schemes is tensor product of coordinate rings, and tensor product commutes with directed colimits. (f) is the universal property of the limit together with equivariance at each finite stage.
6. (g) Q_n is an fpqc G_n-torsor. It is representable by a T-scheme affine over T, by effective fpqc descent of affine morphisms (Stacks 0245; merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1), and it is finite locally free and surjective over T because these properties descend. So Q_n → T is an fppf covering that trivializes Q_n. The map Q → lim Q_n is a G-map of G-torsors by (d), hence an isomorphism; Talpo–Vistoli sketch this direction in Remark 3.9.

**Acceptance.** Roots of 2: for G_n = μ_n over Spec ℚ and P_n = Spec ℚ[z_n]/(z_n^n − 2) with z_n = z_m^(m/n), P = Spec colim ℚ[z_n]/(z_n^n − 2) is an fpqc G-torsor with no ℚ-point (RS.2/roots-two-fpqc-native).; Trivial tower: P_n = G_n with p(n,m) = π(n,m) gives P = G with its translation action.; Faithful flatness in (c) is proved on coordinate rings from the faithfully flat finite stages; nonemptiness of geometric fibres alone is not used.; The comparison of (d) at each n is an isomorphism of G_n-torsors, not only of schemes.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-inverse-limit; how: The coframe tower with G_n = μ_n,T is a tower of this kind; its limit is P∞.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-fpqc-torsor; how: Parts (c) and (d) give faithful flatness, the action square and the finite quotient comparisons.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-native; how: Parts (d), (f) and (g) with G_n = μ_n,k give the equivalence of fpqc G-torsors with coherent finite towers.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/roots-two-fpqc-native; how: Gives the affine fpqc G-torsor of compatible roots of 2.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Remark 3.9, p.15 For a projective system of affine group schemes of finite type with limit G, the remark sketches that a G-torsor is the projective limit of its pushforwards to the finite stages; this is direction (g). The construction (a)–(f) of a torsor from a compatible tower is supplied here. [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu) — Lemmas 32.2.2 (tag 01YX), 10.39.20 (tag 090N), 35.37.1 (tag 0245), 35.23.13, 35.23.17 and 35.23.25 (tags 02KY, 02L2, 02LA) Limits of schemes along affine transition maps exist and are affine-local; directed colimits of faithfully flat algebras are faithfully flat; descent data for affine morphisms along fpqc coverings are effective; local finite presentation, flatness and finiteness are fpqc local on the base.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-coordinate-diagram"></a>

#### Kummer coordinates for the root gerbe

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-coordinate-diagram` · definition · implementation unchecked.

For a field k and positive n, use the existing quotient group K_n(k)=k×/im(a↦a^n). For n|m, the coordinate transition K_m→K_n is induced by the identity on k×: [a]_m↦[a]_n, not by raising a to m/n. These quotients and transitions form the multiplicative coordinate diagram used after a chosen root-gerbe neutralization. Via the finite Kummer comparison, a represents the torsor z^n=a; extension through μm→μn sends z to z^(m/n) and leaves a unchanged.

**Hypotheses.** A field of arbitrary characteristic and positive exponents.; Use existing group quotients and power homomorphisms; finite geometric Kummer identification belongs to SF.2.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:powMonoidHom`, `mathlib:QuotientGroup.mk'`, `mathlib:QuotientGroup.map`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `mathlib:QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-kummer-classes`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-kummer-classes).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Specialize the native quotient-group carrier to k× and the range of the nth-power homomorphism. All group laws and quotient universality come from the baseline.
2. For m=nq, each mth power is an nth power, so QuotientGroup.map applied to the identity defines the coordinate transition. Quotient surjectivity proves uniqueness and composition.
3. Apply the requested finite Kummer exact sequence and Pic(Spec k)=0 to identify this coordinate group with finite torsor classes, including wild n. Verify that the torsor quotient has equation w^n=a.

**API.**

- `RootKummer.coordinate` (data): K_n(k) is the existing quotient k×/(k×)^n, with its inherited commutative group structure.
- `RootKummer.ofUnit` (constructor): The quotient homomorphism sends a unit to its class.
- `RootKummer.ofUnit_eq_one` (characterisation): The class of a is one iff a=b^n for some b∈k×.
- `RootKummer.transition` (functoriality): For n|m, the unique homomorphism sends [a]_m to [a]_n; unit and composite laws follow on quotient generators.
- `RootKummer.finiteTorsorClass` (equivalence): Finite fppf μn-torsor classes identify with K_n(k), carrying z^n=a to [a].
- `RootKummer.transition_ofUnit` (simp): transition (n∣m) [a]_m = [a]_n for every unit a; this holds by definition.
- `RootKummer.transition_id` (simp): transition (n∣n) is the identity of K_n(k).
- `RootKummer.transition_comp` (functoriality): For n | m | l, transition (n∣m) ∘ transition (m∣l) = transition (n∣l).
- `RootKummer.compatibleFamilies` (data): The subgroup of ∏_(n≥1) K_n(k) of families (c_n) with transition (n∣m)(c_m) = c_n whenever n | m; this is lim K_n(k), the target of the Kummer classification.

**Checks.**

- `RootKummerTests.one` (degenerate): K_1(k) is trivial for every field.
- `RootKummerTests.two` (computation): The class of 2 in K_2(Q) is nontrivial, whereas 4 is trivial.
- `RootKummerTests.transition` (non-example): The transition K_4(Q)→K_2(Q) sends the class of 2 to the class of 2; squaring would incorrectly kill it.
- `RootKummerTests.wild` (compatibility): For k=F_p(t), the class of t in K_p(k) is nontrivial although μp(k) has only the identity; the torsor is finite flat.
- `RootKummerTests.realFamilies` (computation): compatibleFamilies ℝ has exactly two elements, the trivial family and ([−1]_n)_n, which is trivial at odd n; over an algebraically closed field the only compatible family is the trivial one.

**Acceptance.** RootKummer.transition is defined as the map of quotient groups induced by the identity of k×; transition_ofUnit holds by definition.; K_4(ℚ) → K_2(ℚ) sends [2] to [2]; the map induced by squaring would send it to [4] = 1.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-lift-native; how: Compatible quotient classes are the input to lifting an actual coherent torsor family.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/neutralization-change-native; how: Multiplication by the compatible unit classes records the change of origin.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — Section 3, p.135, displayed inverse-limit Kummer identification The coordinate quotients are the finite stages of the source formula. The transition convention is verified by the actual power map on torsors. [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.1, p.52, flat Kummer sequence Positive-degree finite Kummer uses flat cohomology rather than invertibility of the exponent.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-root-stack"></a>

#### Infinite root stacks

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-root-stack` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Define √[infinity]{(L,s)/X} as the two-inverse limit of the finite root stacks indexed by positive integers ordered by divisibility, on the fpqc scheme site. Its objects over T are compatible finite root objects with transition isomorphisms satisfying cocycles; arrows are compatible systems of root isomorphisms. It is an fpqc stack, hence also an fppf stack by restriction, and is not asserted to be an algebraic stack of finite presentation. Its affine quotient uses fpqc torsors.

**Hypotheses.** All finite exponents are positive. Infinite root objects and quotient torsors use the fpqc scheme site.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/transition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-transition), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/root-fpqc-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-root-fpqc-descent), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/limit-stack-descent`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the already planned compatible-family carrier, retaining objects, arrows and unit/composition equations.
2. Every finite root is an fpqc stack by root-fpqc-descent. Apply the imported limit-stack-descent theorem to those components and their finite transitions.
3. For a single effective Cartier divisor, TV17 Proposition3.5 identifies the compatible system with its logarithmic infinite root. The local quotient comparison is its separate infinite-affine-quotient leaf.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack.projection` (projection): Project a coherent system to its n-th root.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack.lift` (universal-property): A compatible family of maps into the finite roots determines a map into the two-limit, with compatible 2-morphisms.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack.baseChange` (functoriality): The two-limit commutes with base change in X.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack.test_unit_section` (degenerate): The infinite root of (O_X,1) is X.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack.test_projection` (compatibility): Its n-th projection followed by a finite transition is the corresponding lower projection.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack.test_coherence` (non-example): Choosing unrelated n-th roots without transition isomorphisms does not define an infinite root object.

**Acceptance.** A set-theoretic inverse limit of isomorphism classes discards coherent automorphism data and is insufficient.

**Consumers.** where: Bresciani p. 135; how: Defines the specialization gerbe for a DVR.; where: TV Proposition 3.5; how: Identifies the construction with the logarithmic infinite root in the single-divisor case.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Definition 3.3 p. 13 and Proposition 3.5 p. 14

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RootStack.infiniteRootStack`.

#### Root of the finite chart transition

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-root` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

The actual A-algebra map j_(n,m):B_n→B_(nm) sends the distinguished root t_n to t_(nm)^m.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring; f∈A and n,m are positive natural numbers. No reducedness, Noetherian, unit-parameter or invertibility-of-exponent hypothesis is imposed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition), `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom_root`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Evaluate the native quotient lift at its distinguished root; its chosen value is t_(nm)^m.

**Acceptance.** For n=m=2 the root of A[t]/(t²−f) maps to the square of the root of A[t]/(t⁴−f), including f=0.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Section3.1 pp.14–16, P=N specialization Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-scalar-coefficient-map` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Construct the native group homomorphism S(φ):S(A)→*S(B) by σ_i↦Units.map(φ)(σ_i). Both the finite-order and cross-level coherence equations are preserved.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-point-groupoid` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Preserve all stabilizer labels even when the root is zero or nilpotent.

**Hypotheses.** A,B,C are arbitrary commutative rings in a common universe, B and C are A-algebras, f∈A is arbitrary, and every root index is positive. The exponent need not be invertible. <a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coherent-roots-native"></a>

#### Coherent native root systems

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coherent-roots-native` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Specialize the imported compatible-family carrier to the native root pseudodiagram. A system over T consists of roots x_n and specified isomorphisms α(n,m):F(n,m)(x_m)≅x_n for every n|m. For n|m|l, α(n,m) composed with F(n,m)(α(m,l)) equals α(n,l) after the compositor; the unit equation uses the unit constraint. Arrows h are component root isomorphisms satisfying h_n α(n,m)=α′(n,m)F(n,m)(h_m). Pullback acts on components and comparisons. This groupoid, not a set of root classes, is the infinite-root fibre.

**Hypotheses.** The pseudodiagram and universe policy of transition-native.; All components are actual root objects with their sections and power identifications.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/transition-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-transition-native), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/compatible-limit-family`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-root-stack`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-root-stack).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Instantiate the generic compatible-family construction with the positive-divisibility root diagram.
2. Use the generic componentwise category structure and invertibility criterion, since every fibre arrow is already an isomorphism.
3. Construct scheme pullback from the strong transformation supplied by transition-native; evaluation and the section/power equations remain componentwise.

**API.**

- `RootSystem.component` (projection): Evaluation at n returns the entire root triple.
- `RootSystem.transition` (projection): The specified α(n,m) is a root isomorphism, with unit and compositor equations.
- `RootSystem.hom_ext` (extensionality): Two system arrows agree exactly when every component root arrow agrees.
- `RootSystem.pullback` (functoriality): Arbitrary test-scheme pullback acts on both roots and α, with coherent composition.
- `RootSystem.evaluation` (functoriality): Evaluation is a groupoid functor and its transition transformations recover α.
- `RootSystem.ofFrame` (constructor): For s = 0 and a frame λ: O_T ≅ L_T, the system x_λ with components (O_T, 0, e^n ↦ λ) and transitions given by the canonical isomorphisms (O^(⊗q))^(⊗n) ≅ O; its automorphism group over T is G(T) = lim μ_n(T).
- `RootSystem.ofFactorial` (constructor): A coherent system on the factorial indices 1!, 2!, 3!, … extends to all positive indices, with x_n = F(n,r!)(x_(r!)) for any r with n | r!; this is the inverse of restriction in RS.2/factorial-roots-native.

**Checks.**

- `RootSystemTests.nonvanishing` (computation): For an invertible section s, the groupoid of compatible root systems over every T→X is contractible: each t_n trivializes M_n and forces every component arrow to be the identity.
- `RootSystemTests.zeroBand` (characterisation): Over a field with L trivial and s=0, the compatible trivial roots have automorphism sheaf lim μn, including nonreduced μp in characteristic p.
- `RootSystemTests.incoherent` (non-example): A family of root triples and pairwise isomorphisms violating the 1|2|4 cocycle is rejected, even if every component isomorphism class exists.
- `RootSystemTests.realBand` (non-example): Over ℝ with (L,s) = (O,0), the trivial system has trivial automorphism group G(ℝ) = lim μ_n(ℝ), although each component of even degree has automorphism group μ_n(ℝ) = {±1}: every ζ_n is the square of ζ_2n. A definition that takes automorphisms componentwise without the compatibility squares gives a nontrivial group.

**Acceptance.** If s is invertible on X, the groupoid of systems over every T→X is contractible.; For X = Spec k and (L,s) = (O,0), the system (O,0,id)_n with identity transitions has automorphism group lim μ_n(T) over T; over T = Spec ℝ this group is trivial.; A family of root triples with pairwise isomorphisms that violates the 1|2|4 cocycle is not an object, even when every finite isomorphism class is correct.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-roots-native; how: Restriction must preserve compatible arrows as well as objects.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-quotient-native; how: This is the target groupoid of the torsor-and-equivariant-map equivalence.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition 3.5 and Remark 3.6, p.14 The infinite root stack is a genuine two-limit. The displayed cocycle presentation specializes that limit to roots of one pair.

#### Composition of affine root transitions

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-composition` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

With target exponents identified by associativity, j_(nm,k)∘j_(n,m)=j_(n,mk). The m=1 map is identity. These are equalities of actual algebra maps, not merely matches of closed points.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring; all exponents appearing as denominators are positive.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the existing canonical equivalence of AdjoinRoot quotients for X^(n(mk))−f=X^((nm)k)−f; it sends root to root and fixes A.
2. After composing j_(n,mk) with this equivalence, both A-algebra maps send t_n to t_(nmk)^(mk).
3. Apply native quotient extensionality. At m=1 use the same canonical quotient equivalence for n=n·1, giving the identity after identification.

**Acceptance.** No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-root-limit"></a>

#### Factorial reindexing of the root limit

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-root-limit` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

Restriction of compatible root systems from all positive divisibility indices to 1!,2!,3!,… is an equivalence of groupoids, naturally over every test scheme. It preserves actual root arrows and transition isomorphisms, not merely their isomorphism classes.

**Hypotheses.** A fixed pair (L,s), positive divisibility indices and the coherent finite transition maps.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-root-stack`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-root-stack), `mathlib:Nat.dvd_factorial`, `mathlib:Nat.factorial_dvd_factorial`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The factorial subsequence is increasing for divisibility, and each positive n divides N! once N≥n.
2. Extend a factorial root system to level n by taking its finite transition from a factorial multiple. For two choices use a larger factorial and the supplied transition isomorphisms to compare them.
3. The root-system cocycles make this comparison independent of refinements and make the extended transitions coherent.
4. Perform the same extension on arrows; restriction and extension have componentwise natural inverse comparisons.

**Acceptance.** No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition3.5 and Remark3.6 p.14, cofinal systems Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

#### Factorial reindexing of native roots

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-roots-native` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Restriction of coherent native root systems to the sequence 1!,2!,3!,… is an equivalence of groupoids, pseudonatural in T→X and compatible with all positive-degree evaluations up to specified natural isomorphism. The inverse extends both objects and arrows and supplies all transition cocycles. The same argument applies to coherent finite torsor systems.

**Hypotheses.** The native root pseudodiagram; the factorial sequence starts at 1.; Use cofinality of positive divisibility, not a bijection of index sets.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coherent-roots-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coherent-roots-native), `mathlib:Nat.dvd_factorial`, `mathlib:Nat.factorial_dvd_factorial`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-root-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-root-limit).

**Construction/proof.**

1. For an n-component choose a factorial r! divisible by n (n | r! once r ≥ n, Nat.dvd_factorial) and apply F(n,r!) to the r!-component. For comparing n|m, compare their chosen stages in a common larger factorial (r! | s! for r ≤ s, Nat.factorial_dvd_factorial).
2. Compose the supplied factorial transition isomorphisms and pseudodiagram compositors. Their cocycles show independence of the common comparison stage and give the all-positive cocycle.
3. Extend component arrows in the same way. Build the restriction–extension unit and counit from the original transitions; verify their naturality, triangle identities and pullback modifications. No uniqueness claim discards stabilizer arrows.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-limit-descent-native` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The native compatible-root pseudofunctor is an fpqc stack. A descent datum consists of a compatible root system on a cover, with compatible-system arrows on overlaps satisfying their cocycle. Descending all finite roots and all α produces the descended system, and descent on compatible arrows is fully faithful.

2. Effectiveness descends each x_n. Full faithfulness descends α(n,m) and the system arrows. Equality of their coherence diagrams is detected on the cover.
3. Use the supplied pullback constraints to compare the descended system with the original descent datum. The fppf stack restriction follows because fppf covers are fpqc.

#### Finite transition torsors of a coherent root

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-tower` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For a coherent root system of (O_T,f) and n|m with q=m/n, the map P_m→P_n sends β_m to β_m^q α(n,m)^−1. It is equivariant for μm→μn, ζ↦ζ^q, and is a torsor under its kernel μq, finite locally free of rank q. These maps satisfy composition exactly after the chosen root coherence and are compatible with arbitrary base change and root-system arrows.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Proposition 3.10 and Lemma 3.12, pp.15–16 Compatible trivializations of rational-power data give the transition torsors. The finite coframe formula is the native one-pair specialization.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-native"></a>

#### Actual infinite Kummer torsors and finite towers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-native` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

For any field k, extension of fpqc G_k-torsors through G_k→μn gives an equivalence with the groupoid of coherent finite μn-torsor towers. Its inverse is the represented affine limit of the torsors; it is fpqc locally trivial and recovers every finite extension. Evaluation and arrows commute with those extensions. The band-preserving comparison with the zero-section root gerbe of a trivial line uses Isom from its chosen origin; it differs by inversion from the LEFT coframe presentation.

**Hypotheses.** A field k, arbitrary characteristic, all positive divisibility indices.; Finite torsors are computed fppf; infinite torsors use fpqc.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-roots-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-roots-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-flat-torsor-tower-limit), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/compatible-limit-family`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/classifying-abelian-gerbe`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/neutralization-equivalence`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Form the actual coherent finite torsor groupoid; the trivial torsors and their specified quotient maps give an object, not merely a claimed nonempty limit.
2. Apply RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit with G_n = μ_n,k: turning the quotient comparisons into equivariant maps P_m → P_n, the limit of a coherent tower is an fpqc G_k-torsor recovering every finite stage, and every fpqc G_k-torsor is the limit of its pushforwards.
3. On equivariant torsor arrows, the inverse limit and finite extensions are inverse functors with their projection comparisons. Alternatively use the supplied neutralization equivalence after checking its band and nonemptiness.

**Acceptance.** Over ℚ the tower z_n^n = 2 gives a G-torsor with no ℚ-point; over an algebraically closed field every tower is isomorphic to the trivial one; over 𝔽_p(t) the degree-p stage z^p = t is finite flat and not étale.; The inverse functor is RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit applied to G_n = μ_n,k.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Remark 3.9, p.15 An inverse-limit group torsor is represented by the compatible affine limit of its finite extensions. [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p.133 fpqc convention; Section 3, p.135 The infinite Kummer classifying stack is interpreted on the fpqc site, before passing to isomorphism classes.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition-basis"></a>

#### The finite-free transition basis

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-basis` · construction · implementation unchecked.

B_(nm), as a B_n-module through j_(n,m), has a specified basis indexed by Fin m, whose ith vector is root_(nm)^i. The assertion includes the zero ring; it supplies a linear equivalence with Fin m→₀B_n.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring; all exponents appearing as denominators are positive.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-iterated`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition-iterated), `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.powerBasis'`, `mathlib:Module.Basis`, `mathlib:Module.subsingletonEquiv`, `mathlib:Module.Basis.map`, `mathlib:Module.Basis.reindex`, `mathlib:Polynomial.monic_X_pow_sub_C`, `mathlib:Polynomial.natDegree_X_pow_sub_C`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Split on whether the actual coefficient ring B_n is subsingleton.
2. In the nontrivial B_n branch, U^m−t_n is monic of nat-degree m. Reindex its existing native power basis along that degree equality and transport it through the specified iterated B_n-algebra equivalence.
3. In the zero B_n branch, the actual target module is subsingleton. Use the existing module equivalence to Fin m→₀B_n and the native basis constructor; do not assert positive polynomial degree.
4. The separate basis-vector and reconstruction lemmas expose the root-power and coefficient formulas; applying reconstruction to inverse coordinates gives the inverse-coordinate sum.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransitionBasis.apply` (simp): The ith basis vector is root_(nm)^i.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransitionBasis.repr` (data): Every element has unique coefficients in B_n at powers 0,…,m−1.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransitionBasis.repr_symm` (simp): The inverse coefficient map forms the displayed finite sum of powers.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransitionBasis.test_one` (degenerate): At m=1 the basis has one vector, namely1.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransitionBasis.test_four` (computation): At n=m=2 every class is uniquely a+b*u with a,b in B_2.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.affineTransitionBasis.test_zeroRing` (non-example): For the zero ring the indexed basis is still valid although the defining polynomial has natDegree0; no nontriviality premise excludes this case.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-limit-iso-detection"></a>

#### Finite stages detect Kummer tower isomorphisms

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-limit-iso-detection` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Two compatible finite μ_n-torsor towers over a field k are isomorphic if their n-th torsors are isomorphic for every positive n. Individual finite-stage isomorphisms need not be chosen compatibly in advance.

**Hypotheses.** Compatible finite μ_n-torsor towers over a field; equality of their finite-stage isomorphism classes.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/classifying-abelian-gerbe`, `mathlib:nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system`, `mathlib:rootsOfUnityEquivNthRoots`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. For each n take the set of equivariant k-isomorphisms between the two nth torsors. It is nonempty by the premise.
2. Once one isomorphism is fixed, this set is a torsor for μ_n(k); the pinned roots-of-unity equivalence and finite instance make it finite, even when μ_n is not etale.
3. The coherent tower quotient maps induce the restriction maps on these finite sets. Positive divisibility gives a cofiltered index category.
4. Apply the existing nonempty finite-system theorem to obtain a compatible sequence of isomorphisms. The groupoid limit comparison turns it into the required arrow.

**Acceptance.** No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p.135 H1/Kummer inverse-limit statement, with the native finite-isomorphism proof supplied here Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-limit-class-lift"></a>

#### Compatible Kummer classes lift to a torsor tower

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-limit-class-lift` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Every element of lim_n H1_fppf(k,μ_n) is the finite-stage class family of a coherent finite torsor tower, hence of an fpqc G-torsor. Compatible classes are converted to actual quotient isomorphisms, rather than treated as a preexisting compatible object.

**Hypotheses.** A field k; a compatible family of finite torsor classes.; The finite torsor/H1 comparison is the stated SF.2 contract.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-root-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-root-limit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. On the factorial subsequence choose a representative torsor at each level.
2. Equality of adjacent pushed-forward classes supplies an equivariant isomorphism from the quotient of the next torsor to the preceding torsor.
3. Compose these adjacent isomorphisms to obtain all transitions; a linearly ordered chain has no additional independent composition choices.
4. Extend the actual tower along the factorial cofinality equivalence and apply the fpqc torsor-limit comparison.

**Acceptance.** No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p.135 inverse-limit Kummer statement; TV17 Remark3.6 for cofinality Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring in a fixed universe. Every finite exponent is positive; divisibility maps require n divides N. No nontriviality, reducedness, flatness, field or invertibility hypothesis is imposed.; The character group is the actual AddCircle of period 1 over the rationals, namely Q/Z; its group algebra means the actual MonoidAlgebra A (Multiplicative (AddCircle (1:Q))). **Construction/proof.**

1. Choose the natural representative val(k). The rational identity ((N/n)val(k))/N=val(k)/n uses n>0,N>0 and exact divisibility. Integer-lift computations give equality in Q/Z. This is the scaled transition, not the map [k]↦[k].

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-iso-native"></a>

#### Isomorphism detection for coherent torsor towers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-iso-native` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Two coherent finite μn-torsor towers over k are isomorphic as towers if their torsors have the same class at every degree. Their compatible isomorphism set, when nonempty, is a torsor under G(k)=lim μn(k). For any fpqc G-torsor its automorphism sheaf is G_k, and its k-automorphism group is G(k). Class equality detects existence of a compatible arrow, not uniqueness.

**Hypotheses.** A field k; finite torsors and all specified quotient comparisons.; No surjectivity assumption on the maps between finite isomorphism sets.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-native), `mathlib:nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system`, `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`, `mathlib:card_rootsOfUnity`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-limit-iso-detection`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-limit-iso-detection).

**Construction/proof.**

1. At degree n, the isomorphism set is nonempty by class equality and is a torsor under μn(k), hence finite with at most n elements (card_rootsOfUnity). This uses actual torsor isomorphisms even when neither torsor has a k-point.
2. Conjugate through the two systems’ quotient comparisons to define the transition maps on these finite isomorphism sets; their cocycles make a cofiltered functor.
3. Apply the pinned finite-cofiltered-section theorem, which does not need surjective transition maps, to obtain a compatible arrow. The difference of two compatible arrows is a compatible finite translation. The sheaf version of torsor automorphisms retains the full G.

**Acceptance.** Over ℝ the trivial tower has two automorphisms at degree 2, yet its compatible automorphism group G(ℝ) = lim μ_n(ℝ) is trivial.; Two towers over ℚ whose classes agree at every degree are isomorphic, although finite-stage isomorphisms chosen independently need not be compatible.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — Section 3, p.135, inverse-limit Kummer formula Injectivity of the class formula is expanded into this finite-isomorphism-set argument; it is an authored justification, not an asserted interchange of H1 with arbitrary limits.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-lift-native"></a>

#### Lifting compatible classes to a coherent torsor

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-lift-native` · construction · implementation unchecked.

A compatible family c_n∈K_n(k) lifts to an actual coherent μn-torsor tower and hence an fpqc G_k-torsor. Choose representatives at factorial stages, finite torsors with those classes, and isomorphisms between each adjacent pushed-forward torsor and the preceding torsor. Compose these isomorphisms coherently, extend to all positive degrees, and take the affine torsor limit. Different choices yield isomorphic G-torsors; the construction makes no canonical choice of an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.** A field k and classical choices of finite representatives and adjacent isomorphisms.; Coordinate transitions and finite Kummer identification from kummer-coordinate-diagram.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-coordinate-diagram`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-coordinate-diagram), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-roots-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-roots-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-iso-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-iso-native), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-limit-class-lift`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-limit-class-lift).

**Construction/proof.**

1. At r!, choose a unit representative and the finite Kummer torsor for c_(r!). Compatibility supplies an isomorphism of its μ_(r−1)! extension with the previous representative.
2. Choose these adjacent isomorphisms. Composites, with extension-of-torsor associativity, give the factorial cocycle; no further independently chosen long transitions are allowed.
3. Extend objects and arrows by factorial reindexing and use the torsor-tower equivalence. Isomorphism detection proves independence of choices at the level of classes, while preserving all automorphisms.

**API.**

- `RootKummer.lift` (constructor): A compatible coordinate family has a G-torsor with the prescribed finite classes.
- `RootKummer.lift_evaluation` (characterisation): The μn-extension of the lifted torsor has class c_n for every positive n.
- `RootKummer.lift_choiceIso` (compatibility): Any two choices in the lift give isomorphic compatible towers and G-torsors.
- `RootKummer.lift_unit` (compatibility): The constant trivial coordinate family lifts to the trivial G-torsor up to isomorphism.

**Checks.**

- `RootKummerLiftTests.two` (computation): The compatible classes [2]_n lift to the tower z_n^n=2 and its fpqc limit, although it has no Q-point.
- `RootKummerLiftTests.closed` (degenerate): Over an algebraically closed field every finite coordinate class is trivial; the lift is isomorphic to the trivial G-torsor and retains its automorphisms.
- `RootKummerLiftTests.wild` (compatibility): Over F_p(t), the compatible family [t]_n lifts and has the nontrivial finite μp-torsor at degree p; no étale replacement is made.

**Acceptance.** Over ℚ the family ([2]_n) lifts to the tower z_n^n = 2; over ℝ the family ([−1]_n) lifts to the tower z_n^n = −1, trivial at odd n and the nontrivial μ_2-torsor at n = 2.; Different choices of representatives and adjacent isomorphisms change the lifted G-torsor only by an isomorphism.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-classes-native; how: This supplies surjectivity of the chosen-neutralization class comparison.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — Section 3, p.135, inverse-limit Kummer formula Surjectivity is justified here by actual representatives and adjacent quotient isomorphisms; the source formula alone is not used as a proof. [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Remark 3.6, p.14; Remark 3.9, p.15 Cofinal indexing and represented torsor limits supply the two geometric steps.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-not-fppf"></a>

#### An infinite Kummer torsor requiring fpqc descent

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-not-fppf` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Over Q, the compatible finite torsors P_n=Spec Q[T]/(T^n−2) define an fpqc G=lim_n μ_n torsor P_infinity. It has no section after any nonempty fppf Q-cover. Each individual P_n is fppf-locally trivial, so replacing all infinite torsors by fppf-locally trivial G-torsors loses this point of the infinite classifying gerbe.

**Hypotheses.** Base field Q; all positive root exponents.; The finite-type chart and closed-point residue comparison are the exact SF.1 contract.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-faithfully-flat`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition-faithfully-flat), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/affine-transition-composition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-affine-transition-composition), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-degree-bound`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-degree-bound), `mathlib:finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The element2 is a unit; each finite root chart is a μ_n torsor. The transition equations provide a coherent tower.
2. The fpqc torsor-limit comparison constructs P_infinity; the finite-free transition calculation also exhibits its affine fpqc cover.
3. Suppose it has a section on a nonempty fppf Q-scheme. Choose a nonempty affine finite-type open chart and a closed point. Its residue field is finite over Q by the pinned Zariski lemma.
4. Specialize the section to that field. It would contain an nth root of2 for every n, contradicting the degree-bound leaf.

**Acceptance.** Every finite P_n is an fppf torsor, while their actual fpqc limit admits no nonempty fppf trivializing cover. The contradiction retains the finite residue-field degree, rather than choosing a field of unbounded degree.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p.133 fpqc necessity for non-finite-type groups; explicit all-roots-of2 example supplied here Root-specific specialization and proof derivation using the stated source construction and the listed native baseline declarations; not a claim that the paper literally states every algebraic comparison below.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-roots-two-fpqc-native"></a>

#### A Kummer limit torsor without fppf trivialization

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/roots-two-fpqc-native` · application · implementation unchecked.

Over Q, the coherent finite torsors P_n=Spec Q[z_n]/(z_n^n−2), with z_n=z_m^(m/n), have an affine fpqc limit P under G_Q. No nonempty fppf Q-scheme U admits a section of P×U→U. Thus P is an actual fpqc torsor that is not fppf locally trivial, even though every P_n is fppf locally trivial.

**Hypotheses.** All positive degrees; finite exponents are invertible over Q.; The existing degree bound for roots of 2 in a finite extension is imported.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-lift-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-lift-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-degree-bound`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-degree-bound), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-flat-torsor-tower-limit), `mathlib:finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-not-fppf`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-not-fppf).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Each P_n is the finite μn Kummer torsor for the unit 2 and its quotient maps form an actual coherent tower. RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit gives the affine fpqc G-torsor P.
2. If a nonempty fppf U trivializes P, choose a nonempty affine open Spec B of U with B a finitely generated ℚ-algebra and a maximal ideal m of B. By Zariski's lemma (finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing) K = B/m is finite over ℚ, and the section restricts to compatible nth roots of 2 in K.
3. The imported Eisenstein/minimal-polynomial bound n≤[K:Q] contradicts a degree n>[K:Q]. Local finite presentation of U is essential to this closed-point argument.

**Acceptance.** The obstruction applies to every nonempty fppf test scheme, not only finite field extensions.; The example explains why replacing infinite fpqc H1 by fppf H1 changes the target.

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Remark 3.9 and Proposition 3.10, pp.15–16 The fpqc torsor convention and affine tower construction motivate this authored separating example; no claim that the paper states this roots-of-two counterexample is made.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/native-scheme-lift-unique` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

If g:T→Spec D_A(f) has composite g followed by π_n equal to the n-th leg of s for every positive n, then g=L_s.

**Hypotheses.** A, B and C are arbitrary commutative rings in one common arbitrary universe; f∈A and unital ring maps φ:A→B and ψ:B→C are arbitrary. All schemes, cones, ring maps and isomorphisms are native.; The limit and lift laws apply to all test schemes in the coefficient universe, including nonaffine schemes. `FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/divisibility-factorial-equivalence` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

The actual A-algebras C_div and C_f are canonically equivalent. Its forward map is α and its inverse is β, with the finite-coordinate formulas specified below.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, f∈A, and B_n is the actual AdjoinRoot algebra A[T]/(T^n−f). Root exponents are positive. No nontriviality, reducedness, Noetherian, unit-parameter or invertible-exponent hypothesis is imposed.

1. Turn the two actual algebra maps and both inverse equations into the native AlgEquiv.
2. Do not identify coherent root-object groupoids or an fpqc quotient from an algebra equivalence alone.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RootStack.divisibilityFactorialEquiv` (constructor): The actual A-algebras C_div and C_f are canonically equivalent. Its forward map is α and its inverse is β, with the finite-coordinate formulas specified below.
- `TauCeti.RootStack.divisibilityFactorialEquiv.inclusion` (compatibility): For n dividing d_i and x∈B_n, the equivalence sends κ_n(x) to ι_i(j_(n,d_i)(x)).
- `TauCeti.RootStack.divisibilityFactorialEquiv.root` (simp): For n dividing d_i, the equivalence sends v_n to u_i^(d_i/n), where u_i=ι_i(t_(d_i)).

**Checks.**

- `divisibilityFactorialEquiv.test_three` (computation): The nonfactorial index-3 root maps to the square of the factorial index-6 root.
- `divisibilityFactorialEquiv.test_coefficients` (compatibility): Over Z/4Z, the actual equivalence preserves every coefficient for arbitrary parameter f.
- `divisibilityFactorialEquiv.test_inverse` (characterisation): Applying the inverse equivalence after the forward equivalence gives every original element of C_div.

**Acceptance.** Use the actual quotient rings and native directed colimits; keep every finite root and coefficient map visible.; This algebra comparison leaves coherent root arrows, grading, Spec limits and fpqc torsor/quotient comparisons as separate obligations.

#### The represented inverse limit of coframes

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-inverse-limit` · construction · implementation unchecked.

The coherent finite coframe tower has an affine inverse limit P∞ over T, with projections to every P_n and a represented action of G_T=lim μn,T=D_T(Q/Z). Formation of P∞ commutes with arbitrary base change, and restriction to factorial indices gives the same limit. On an affine U⊂T, its coordinate algebra is the filtered colimit of the coordinate algebras of P_n|U. The action and projections agree with the parent Q/Z band and Spec-limit conventions.

**Hypotheses.** The finite coframe tower; T need not be affine or Noetherian.; The hypotheses of RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit, with G_n = μ_n,T.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-tower`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coframe-tower), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/factorial-roots-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-factorial-roots-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-flat-torsor-tower-limit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/native-scheme-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-native-scheme-limit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/native-base-change-tensor-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-native-base-change-tensor-equivalence).

**Construction/proof.**

1. A degree-one coframe is β_1 = φ_1, so P_1 = T and every P_n is finite locally free over T. The coframe tower of RS.2/coframe-tower, with G_n = μ_n,T, satisfies the hypotheses of RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit.
2. That theorem gives P∞ = lim P_n, affine over T, with affine-local coordinate rings the directed colimits of the finite coordinate algebras, its G_T-action and all finite projections, including indices outside the factorial subsystem.
3. Restriction to factorial indices gives the same limit by cofinality (RS.2/factorial-roots-native). Base change is part (e) of the tower theorem, compared with the parent tensor-colimit equivalence; the action and projections use the parent ℚ/ℤ band and Spec-limit conventions. No new direct-limit, Hopf or Spec theory is developed here.

**API.**

- `RootCoframeLimit.projection` (projection): Every P∞→P_n respects the finite tower maps.
- `RootCoframeLimit.action` (structure): The represented G_T action has its given μn-action at each projection.
- `RootCoframeLimit.pullbackIso` (compatibility): Pullback along T′→T is the limit of the pulled-back finite coframe torsors.
- `RootCoframeLimit.factorialIso` (equivalence): The all-positive and factorial relative affine limits are canonically isomorphic with all projections.
- `RootCoframeLimit.hom_ext` (extensionality): Maps into P∞ are determined by their compatible finite projections.
- `RootCoframeLimit.towerLimitIso` (compatibility): P∞ is the limit of RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit for the coframe tower with G_n = μ_n,T; its G_T-torsor structure and finite projections are those of that theorem.

- `RootCoframeLimitTests.nonrational` (non-example): The coherent torsors z_n^n=2 over Q have a represented affine limit; its existence does not supply a Q-point.
- `RootCoframeLimitTests.basechange` (compatibility): For A→A/I, the coframe limit base changes by tensoring its colimit algebra, including nilpotent I.

**Acceptance.** For compatible trivial roots, P∞ = G_T with its translation action; for the roots of 2 over ℚ, P∞ = Spec colim ℚ[z_n]/(z_n^n − 2).; The all-positive and factorial limits are isomorphic compatibly with every finite projection.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coframe-fpqc-torsor"></a>

#### The infinite coframe fpqc torsor

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-fpqc-torsor` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

P∞→T is affine and faithfully flat, hence an fpqc cover, and the action map G_T×_T P∞→P∞×_T P∞, (g,p)↦(g·p,p), is an isomorphism. For every n, extension through G_T→μn,T recovers P_n; equivalently the fpqc quotient P∞/ker(G_T→μn,T) is P_n. These statements are natural in root systems and arbitrary base changes. No finite-presentation or fppf local triviality is asserted for P∞.

**Hypotheses.** Positive divisibility or factorial tower with the finite faithfully flat coframe transitions.; Use the coordinate-ring argument of RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit, not compactness of field-valued torsor points.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-inverse-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coframe-inverse-limit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-flat-torsor-tower-limit).

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-affine-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-affine-quotient), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Part (c) of RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit: over an affine open, the coordinate ring of P∞ is a directed colimit of faithfully flat finite algebras, hence faithfully flat; P∞ is affine over T, so P∞ → T is an fpqc covering.
2. Part (d) gives the action-square isomorphism and the comparisons P∞ ×^G μ_n ≅ P_n, equivalently P∞/ker(G_T → μ_n,T) ≅ P_n.
3. Naturality in root systems and base change follows from parts (e) and (f), since root-system arrows induce compatible equivariant maps of the finite coframe torsors.

**Acceptance.** Do not infer faithful flatness from nonempty geometric fibres alone. Use the precise TOWER-AFF flatness and faithfulness contract.; All finite quotient comparisons are specified; no assertion of a compatible rational frame is made.; For the roots of 2 over ℚ, P∞ ×^G μ_2 ≅ Spec ℚ[z]/(z² − 2).

**Sources.** [TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) — Definition 3.8, Remark 3.9 and Proposition 3.10, pp.15–16 The infinite presentation uses an actual fpqc torsor. The faithfully flat limit argument is the supplier obligation made explicit in this root-specific target.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-affine-quotient"></a>

#### The infinite affine fpqc root quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-affine-quotient` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For B_n=A[T]/(T^n−f) with the displayed divisibility maps, put B_infinity=colim_n B_n and G=lim_n μ_n, with its diagonalizable grading action. The infinite root stack of (O_A,f) is [Spec B_infinity/G] as an fpqc quotient stack. Its morphism groupoids and finite projections agree with the two-limit of the finite roots. This is not asserted to be an algebraic stack of finite presentation.

**Hypotheses.** Any commutative ring A and f∈A.; Infinite quotient and torsors use the fpqc topology; TOWER-AFF is an explicit supplier obligation.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-quotient-native"></a>

#### The genuine infinite affine quotient equivalence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-quotient-native` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For any commutative ring A and f∈A, the fpqc stack of coherent native roots of (O,f) is equivalent over Spec A to [Spec C_A(f)/D_A(Q/Z)]. A quotient object over T is a represented fpqc G_T-torsor with an equivariant chart map. The equivalence retains arrows, finite projections, all transition comparisons, and arbitrary base change. For a general line bundle with section, these equivalences glue over target-line trivializations. With these LEFT coframe conventions a root-line scalar automorphism ζ acts on coframes by ζ^−1, so the quotient comparison inverts the usual scalar band on the zero-section gerbe. The infinite quotient is not claimed algebraic of finite presentation.

**Hypotheses.** Positive exponents of arbitrary characteristic; no regularity, reducedness or log-chart hypothesis on f.; Use LEFT torsors and LEFT chart scaling throughout.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-limit-descent-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-root-limit-descent-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-limit-base-change-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-root-limit-base-change-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/normalized-coframes`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-normalized-coframes), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-fpqc-torsor`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coframe-fpqc-torsor), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/coframe-evaluation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-coframe-evaluation), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-affine-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-affine-quotient).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Send a root system to its normalized coframe-limit torsor and evaluation map. Root arrows induce the corresponding equivariant torsor maps.
2. Conversely extend a G-torsor to each μn. The relation β^−1(a) explains this convention.
3. The finite projection comparisons give the root α and their cocycles. Reconstruct coframes and root lines to obtain the two natural inverse isomorphisms; verify them on the fpqc trivializing torsor and descend.
4. Use the supplied base-change and tensor comparisons to check every finite evaluation and to glue over changes of target-line trivialization. The quotient stack is the generic Stack.quotient of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21 on the fpqc site, for the action groupoid of G on Spec C_A(f). `FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-uniformizer-native` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

If π′=uπ, the equivalence between the two chart presentations is induced by the same intrinsic Cartier pair and its root-groupoid pullback comparisons. It preserves all finite evaluations and their α. It does not require a chosen compatible family of nth roots of u in R.

**Hypotheses.** A DVR R with residue field k, u∈R×; arbitrary residue characteristic.; The chart expression depends on the trivialization; the underlying pair and stack do not.

3. Check the resulting equivalence on finite roots and root arrows, then on all α; base change to k gives the residual-gerbe comparison.

**Acceptance.** For R = ℤ_3 with π = 3 and π′ = −3, the two chart presentations are identified through the intrinsic pair although −1 has no square root in ℤ_3; no scalar map z_n ↦ c_n z_n with c_n^n = −1 is used.; At each finite degree n the comparison restricts to the equivalence of the finite DVR charts [Spec R[t]/(t^n − π)/μ_n] ≃ [Spec R[t]/(t^n − π′)/μ_n] (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21, rootStack.test_dvr_chart).

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-residual-gerbe-native"></a>

#### The DVR zero-section gerbe and the full fibre

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-residual-gerbe-native` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Write N=O(D)|Spec k. The closed fibre of the infinite DVR root stack has chart C_k(0)=colim k[z_n]/(z_n^n); its nilradical is the ideal of the z_n and C_k(0)_red=k. The canonical substack obtained by imposing t_n=0 at every degree is the coherent root gerbe of N, banded by G_k. A chosen frame λ:k≅N supplies compatible trivial roots and a band-preserving equivalence with BG_k. Thus the reduced-chart quotient is this gerbe. The full closed fibre includes nonzero nilpotent root sections; the nilradical has no uniform nilpotence exponent. In arbitrary characteristic, this specifies the zero-section gerbe and reduced-chart quotient without assuming an unprovided general reduction functor for infinite fpqc stacks.

**Hypotheses.** A DVR and its residue field, with finite roots of all positive degrees.; A chosen frame of N is needed for BG identification; the band retains all wild group-scheme inertia.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-uniformizer-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-uniformizer-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-quotient-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-quotient-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/divisibility-affine-inclusion-injective`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-divisibility-affine-inclusion-injective), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/neutralization-equivalence`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.root`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.mk_ne_zero_of_natDegree_lt`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-infinite-gerbe`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-infinite-gerbe).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Base change the parent native chart to k. Its transition sends z_n to z_m^(m/n), and the parent divisibility-affine inclusion theorem gives injectivity. Every zero-constant element occurs at a finite level and is nilpotent; quotienting by all z_n gives k.
2. For any r choose n>r: the pinned monic quotient degree theorem makes z_n^r nonzero at degree n, and it remains nonzero in the colimit. Hence the radical ideal is not nilpotent with a fixed exponent; infinite reduction is not a finite nilpotent thickening.
3. Setting every root section to zero leaves exactly roots of N with their compatible power identifications and arrows. Their automorphism sheaf is lim μn=G_k.
4. A frame λ gives the coherent objects (O,0, e^n↦λ) with identity-compatible power maps. Apply the imported neutralization equivalence. For the char-zero source setting this is the reduced fibre of B24; the all-characteristic statement uses the explicit reduced-chart quotient.

**Acceptance.** Retain the full fibre, its zero-section gerbe and the chosen neutralization as three distinct pieces of data.; Do not replace G by its rational points, or claim a uniform nilpotent ideal for the infinite fibre.; At each finite degree the closed fibre restricts to [Spec k[t]/(t^n)/μ_n], not to Bμ_n (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21, rootStack.test_fibre_nonreduced).

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — Section 3, p.135, paragraph on the reduced closed fibre The DVR residual gerbe is noncanonically the infinite Kummer classifying stack. The arbitrary-characteristic and nonuniform-nilpotence qualifications are authored extensions. [AGV08](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0603151v2) — Appendix B.2, p.53, zero-fibre comparison The finite full zero fibre also permits nonzero sections whose nth power vanishes; the zero-section gerbe is a proper distinction.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-classes-native"></a>

#### Kummer classification after a neutralization

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-classes-native` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

After choosing a frame λ:k≅N, the isomorphism classes of the DVR zero-section root gerbe identify with H1_fpqc(k,G_k) and then with lim_(n|m) K_n(k). The latter comparison is a group isomorphism for G-torsor classes; on gerbe classes the group law is transported from the chosen origin. The maps are given by Isom(x_λ,y), finite torsor extension and finite Kummer coordinates. All automorphism sheaves are G_k and all k-automorphism groups are G(k).

**Hypotheses.** A field k of arbitrary characteristic and a specified neutralization x_λ from a frame of N.; Do not take inverse limits of classes before establishing the torsor-groupoid and lifting/detection results.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-residual-gerbe-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-residual-gerbe-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-coordinate-diagram`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-coordinate-diagram), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-tower-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-tower-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-iso-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-iso-native), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-lift-native`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-lift-native), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4/neutralization-equivalence`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-kummer-classes`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-kummer-classes).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the band-preserving neutralization equivalence y↦Isom(x_λ,y). It gives the actual torsor groupoid, before taking classes.
2. Map a torsor class to its finite Kummer classes. Isomorphism detection gives injectivity and class-family lifting gives surjectivity.
3. Finite torsor tensor product agrees with multiplication of Kummer coordinates, proving the group assertion. Retain the automorphism sheaf and identify its rational translations separately.

**Acceptance.** Over ℝ the zero-section gerbe has exactly two isomorphism classes of real points, with coordinates 1 and ([−1]_n)_n; over an algebraically closed field it has one; over ℚ the class ([2]_n)_n is nontrivial.; Contracted product of torsor towers corresponds to multiplication of Kummer coordinates: the towers z^n = a and z^n = b combine to z^n = ab.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — Section 3, p.135, reduced-fibre and displayed Kummer identification This expands the source identification into its groupoid, neutralization, injectivity and surjectivity obligations. Wild characteristic is handled through the imported flat Kummer contract.
