<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-infinite-gerbe"></a>

#### The infinite reduced DVR fibre

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-infinite-gerbe` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The reduced closed fibre of the infinite root of a DVR with residue field k is the inverse system of the root gerbes of the normal line, banded by lim_n μ_n=Ẑ(1). It is noncanonically equivalent to B_kẐ(1); a chosen trivialization of the normal line gives a compatible neutralization. The neutralization is not part of the canonical root stack.

**Hypotheses.** Finite roots are defined fppf and satisfy the stronger fpqc descent theorem. Infinite systems and infinite torsors use fpqc descent.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-roots`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-roots), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-base-change`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-base-change), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/infinite-root-stack`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-infinite-root-stack), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the normal line to identify each reduced finite closed fibre with its n-th-root gerbe.
2. A trivialization of that one-dimensional k-space supplies compatible trivial root objects at all n.
3. The automorphisms form lim μ_n, and coherent descent gives the banded gerbe; use the source’s reduced-fibre convention for the infinite limit.

**Acceptance.** The full fibre retains nilpotent finite charts; only the reduced gerbe is identified with the classifying gerbe.

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p. 135–136 reduced fibre H_c and its band

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-kummer-classes"></a>

#### Kummer classes of infinite-gerbe points

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-kummer-classes` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

After choosing a neutralization of the infinite reduced DVR gerbe over k, its k-points up to isomorphism identify with H1_fpqc(k,G), where G=lim_n μ_n, and with lim_n H1_fppf(k,μ_n)=lim_n k×/(k×)^n. Infinite torsors are fpqc; the finite Kummer calculation is fppf. The full groupoid retains G(k) automorphisms, and changing the neutralization changes the chosen origin.

**Hypotheses.** A DVR with residue field k of arbitrary characteristic and a chosen compatible neutralization.; G is the fpqc inverse-limit sheaf of all μ_n, with power transition maps.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/dvr-infinite-gerbe`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-dvr-infinite-gerbe), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-torsor-limit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-torsor-limit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-limit-iso-detection`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-limit-iso-detection), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/kummer-limit-class-lift`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-2-kummer-limit-class-lift).

**Construction/proof.**

1. The neutralization identifies the reduced gerbe with fpqc G-torsors.
2. The Kummer torsor-limit comparison gives its actual finite tower, including the quotient identifications.
3. Apply kummer-limit-iso-detection for injectivity on classes and kummer-limit-class-lift for surjectivity; do not commute isomorphism classes with limits without these leaves.
4. Apply the exact finite fppf Kummer comparison at each exponent and retain its transition maps. The result is an identification with a chosen origin, not a loss of the automorphism groupoid.

**Acceptance.** Changing neutralization translates the Kummer classes; no canonical origin is asserted.; The compatible roots-of2 torsor overQ is retained despite having no fppf local trivialization; H1_fppf(k,G) is not substituted for H1_fpqc(k,G).

**Sources.** [B24](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf) — p. 135–136 displayed H_c(k) and Kummer limit

<a id="gc-0"></a>

## GC.0 — Root Picard stacks

Root Picard objects retain a line on the curve and a square-root line along R. Tensor, dual, arbitrary integer degrees and all arrows are native. The square action on rigidifications and weight-one action on root sections give the two quotient descriptions. Relative inertia fixes the curve line; full inertia includes its scalar. Empty R and an empty test scheme require separate checks.

**Planets.** Root Picard stack — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard); Square-action Picard quotient — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/square-action-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-square-action-quotient); Root Picard sections — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard-section`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard-section).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### The native fibre and its arrows

For any actual scheme arrow j:Z→Y, the light native data type has fields

\[
 L\in\operatorname{InvertibleSheaf}(Y),\qquad
 K\in\operatorname{InvertibleSheaf}(Z),\qquad
 \iota:(K\otimes K).\mathrm{obj}\xrightarrow{\sim}
       (\operatorname{Modules.pullback}j)(L.\mathrm{obj}).
\]

GC.0 specializes j to i_S. An arrow to (L′,K′,ι′) consists of two
isomorphisms f:L≅L′ and v:K≅K′ subject to

\[
 \iota'\circ(v\otimes v)=i_S^*f\circ\iota.
\]

Every term lives in the native category of modules on R_S. Tensor congruence
on its left and right factors is already present at the pins. Identity,
composition and inverse of these compatible pairs give the root groupoid. This
retains the scalar automorphisms that the coarse Picard group forgets. A
restriction isomorphism has no section field, so it does not impose the
line-with-section root equation from RS.0.

For h:S′→S, with h_X and h_R the product maps, form h_X*L and h_R*K. The
new square is the composite

\[
 (h_R^*K)^2\xrightarrow{\sim}h_R^*(K^2)
 \xrightarrow{h_R^*\iota}h_R^*i_S^*L
 \xrightarrow{\sim}i_{S'}^*h_X^*L.
\]

The last isomorphism uses the commuting square and native pullback composition.
The first uses the imported strong monoidal pullback. Tensor and pullback
comparisons must be coherent: equality of objectwise isomorphism classes cannot
supply a pseudofunctor. Effective invertible-sheaf and morphism descent descend
the entire triple and the arrow equation, giving the stack.

#### Tensor, dual and degree conventions

For two root triples A=(L,K,ι) and B=(M,N,κ), tensor the lines separately. To
identify (K⊗N)² with (L⊗M)|R, first move its middle N and K past one another,
then use ι⊗κ, and finally the inverse of the strong monoidal restriction
comparison. This uses the ordinary unsigned symmetry of line bundles. The
integer degree is an external grading; it does not turn this into the signed
Picard groupoid of graded determinant lines.

For the inverse root use (L∨,K∨). Dualizing ι gives a map in the opposite
direction, so the required square comparison uses **the inverse of ι∨** after
identifying the tensor square of K∨ with (K²)∨. Native evaluation gives
A⊗A∨≅1. The associativity, unit, symmetry and duality diagrams can be checked
on their two underlying line isomorphisms, because these determine a root
arrow. This imports the coherent module structure instead of constructing it
a second time.

The degree of A is the ordinary degree of L on every geometric fibre, not half
that degree. The stack in degree d is the 2-pullback of the ordinary degree-d
Picard stack. Arbitrary families have a locally constant integer degree;
separate components of S may have different integers. Tensor adds degree and
dual negates it. All d∈Z occur geometrically. A rational point is useful for
an example over an algebraic closure, not an assumption in the definition.
The Picard sheaf's Pic^d is a torsor; neither a trivialization of that torsor nor
a universal line bundle is inferred from its notation.

#### Square-action orientation and descent

Import the native rigidified-line interface. Its objects are (L,γ) with
γ:L|R≅O_R, and its arrows satisfy γ′∘f|R=γ. Put

\[
 T(S)=\Gamma(R_S,O)^\times,\qquad V(S)=\Gamma(R_S,O).
\]

The generic supplier identifies these with the finite-étale restrictions of
scalars Res_R/k G_m and Res_R/k A¹. After an étale splitting of R they are
G_m^ρ and A^ρ. A degree-two closed point has T(k)=κ(x)×, not a product indexed
by k-rational points.

Fix γ in the direction L|R→O. The root atlas sends it to
(L,O,γ⁻¹), with the unit-square isomorphism inserted. For a root frame
e:O≅K of an intrinsic triple, its extracted rigidification is
γ=(ι∘e²)⁻¹. Replacing e by e′=e u⁻¹ gives

\[
 \gamma'=u^2\gamma.
\]

Consequently the square-action comparison from the old atlas object to the
new one is (f,v)=(1,u), since

\[
 (u^2\gamma)^{-1}u^2=\gamma^{-1}.
\]

The current native rigidified-line rescaling already composes γ with
multiplication by a unit. GC.0 uses that existing action through the square map;
it does not plan general rigidification or rescaling anew.

Frames of K form a T-torsor over S, and need not have an S-point. They do have
fppf-local frames, and each frame produces a rigidified line. The frame
transition units satisfy their cocycle and give the full quotient object. In
the reverse direction an equivariant rigidified line on a T-torsor descends to
a root triple. The local frame identifications give the unit and counit, with
the triangle identities checked on the cover and descended. Thus the comparison
is an equivalence on all arrows as well as on objects:

\[
 [\operatorname{Pic}_{X,R}/T]\simeq\operatorname{RootPic}_{X,R},
 \qquad (L,\gamma)\cdot u=(L,u^2\gamma).
\]

The quotient is a stack quotient, including torsors and their descent arrows.
A pointwise orbit set would miss nontrivial root lines and their inertia.
For R≠∅, rigidifying kills ordinary scalar automorphisms, since R_S→S is
faithfully flat and the curve has only base functions universally. This gives
the algebraic-space rigidified Picard supplier to which quotient algebraicity
applies. For R=∅ the rigidified object is the ordinary Picard **stack**, and the
acting group is trivial. That case retains G_m inertia and is handled directly.

#### The relative gerbe

Over a fixed L, the 2-fibre consists of K with K²≅L|R, including a specified
identification of the forgotten line with L. Its automorphisms therefore act
over the identity of L. They are exactly u with u²=1, giving the band

\[
 H=\operatorname{Res}_{R/k}\mu_2.
\]

A finite étale cover splits R; then local frames of L|R give roots. Kummer
lifting gives local comparison arrows between roots. These prove the gerbe
conditions. A chosen root identifies this fibre with BH_S; the choice is part
of the neutrality statement. No canonical global splitting is required.
Even over F₅, square identifications 1 and 2 of a fixed trivial root line are
not isomorphic over a fixed identity on L until a square root is adjoined.
The gerbe assertion is local and does not assert surjectivity of square maps
on k-points. At R=∅ the band is trivial and forgetting roots is an equivalence.

#### Sections on R and their weight-one chart

The second fibre adds α∈Γ(R_S,K) and requires v(α)=α′ on arrows. It adds no
global section of L. The square evaluation ι(α⊗α) is a section of L|R;
there is no extension-to-X operation in this API. On P¹ with R a rational point,
L=O(−1) admits root data and a nonzero α on R although L has no nonzero global
section. Definition A.2 on p. 515 belongs to GC.1: it separately adds a global
section a and imposes ι(α²)=a|R. Forgetting a, and forgetting α, are distinct
maps in A.1.5, p. 517.

If α=e(a), changing the root frame to e u⁻¹ changes a to u a. Combining this
with γ′=u²γ gives

\[
 \operatorname{RootPicSection}_{X,R}
 \simeq[(\operatorname{Pic}_{X,R}\times V)/T],\qquad
 (\gamma,a)\cdot u=(u^2\gamma,u a).
\]

The value γ⁻¹a² in the framed L_R is unchanged, because its two factors have
opposite total weight. For γ=a=1 and u=2 over F₅, the new pair is (4,2), and
its squared evaluation is still 1. Weight two on a, weight one on γ, or the
opposite convention for only one factor would fail this calculation.

The fibre of the forgetful map over a **fixed root object** is its actual
section sheaf, without a further quotient by its automorphisms. Splitting R
and framing K makes it A^ρ over the base. The linear transition maps descend
to an affine morphism with a closed zero section. The zero-section functor
exists for every degree. Tensor of sections makes a commutative monoid stack.
For R_S≠∅ the zero section has no tensor inverse. If S is empty, R_S is
empty even when R is not, and the unique section is a frame. A section is
tensor-invertible exactly when it is a frame everywhere on R_S; duality of a general section
cannot supply an inverse.

Nonreduced sections are retained. Over F₅[ε]/(ε²), the section ε of the trivial
root line is nonzero and has square zero. This lies on an actual k-scheme base,
and the native type accepts it. Neither square evaluation nor section descent
replaces it by its reduction.

#### Inertia equations on every test scheme

The universal equality of functions Γ(X_S,O)=Γ(S,O) identifies full
line-bundle automorphisms with c∈Γ(S,O)×. Root-line automorphisms are
u∈Γ(R_S,O)×. The defining arrow equation gives

\[
 u^2=c|_{R_S};\qquad\text{with section: }u\alpha=\alpha.
\]

These equations hold as group sheaves on all S′→S. For relative inertia over
an identity on L set c=1. At geometric split points they become u_j²=c and
u_j a_j=a_j. A nonzero a_j over a field forces u_j=1 and hence c=1. At zero
coordinates the relative μ₂ remains. On arbitrary rings retain the equations;
a nonzero section need not be cancellable.

For one branch point the full root inertia is G_m via u↦(u²,u), whereas its
relative inertia is μ₂. For two branch points and α=(1,0), the full section
inertia is μ₂ on the second coordinate. If there is at least one branch point
and all coordinates are nonzero it is trivial. For the zero section all full root automorphisms remain. For no branch
points the full inertia is still G_m and the relative inertia is trivial.
The phrase “μ₂^ρ stabilizer” in the parent applies to forgetting roots over a
fixed ordinary line, not to full inertia.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard"></a>

#### The graded root Picard stack

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Pic_X^√R(S) is the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι), where L is a line bundle on X×S, K_R a line bundle on R×S and ι:K_R²≅L|_{R×S}. Its degree-d component imposes degree d on every geometric fibre; d ranges over all integers. Tensor product and dual give the graded commutative Picard stack.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-key-root-stacks), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Import the ordinary line-bundle Picard stack and restriction to R.
2. Take the root-gerbe two-pullback for the restricted line bundle; do not require a section.
3. Tensor and dual root data with the imported coherent line-bundle isomorphisms.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.object` (constructor): Create (L,K_R,ι) from the two line bundles and the square identification.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.degree` (projection): The degree is the fibrewise degree of L, additive under tensor product.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.tensor` (structure): Tensor two objects and their root identifications; dual gives inverse up to coherent isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.forget` (projection): Forget K_R,ι to the ordinary Picard stack.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.test_empty_R` (degenerate): At R=∅ this is the ordinary graded Picard stack.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.test_degree_minus_one` (non-example): Negative-degree components contain line bundles and are not declared empty.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard.test_stabilizer` (characterisation): Over an algebraically closed field with r geometric branch points, forgetting roots has relative stabilizer μ₂^r.

**Acceptance.** Pic^d is a torsor component, with no chosen degree-one point required.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 A.2.2–A.2.3; how: Carries the character local system in every integer degree.; where: YZ19 A.3.1; how: Receives the ramified norm.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Definition A.1 p. 514; A.1.1 p. 515

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-square-action-quotient"></a>

#### Square-action presentation of the root Picard stack

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/square-action-quotient` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let Pic_{X,R} classify (L,γ:L|_R≅O_R). Then Pic_X^√R≃[Pic_{X,R}/[2]Res_{R/k}G_m], where the acting group changes the rigidification through its square. The forgetful morphism to Pic_X is a Res_{R/k}μ₂-gerbe.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Trivialize K_R fppf-locally; ι supplies the rigidification γ.
2. Changing the root-line frame by u changes γ by u², giving the square-action quotient.
3. The kernel is Res μ₂; verify the relative automorphism group and local lift property.

**Acceptance.** The unsquared action gives ordinary Pic_X and loses the ramification gerbe.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.1 p. 515

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-native-root-fibres"></a>

#### Native root Picard fibres and descent

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/native-root-fibres` · definition · implementation unchecked.

For i_S:R_S→X_S a root object is (L,K,ι), with L∈InvertibleSheaf(X_S), K∈InvertibleSheaf(R_S), and ι:(K⊗K).obj≅(Modules.pullback i_S).obj L.obj. An arrow to (L′,K′,ι′) is a pair of native isomorphisms (f:L≅L′,v:K≅K′) satisfying ι′∘(v⊗v)=i_S* f∘ι in R_S.Modules. Componentwise identities, composition and inverse make these a groupoid. Along S′→S pull back both lines and transport ι using the canonical tensor and pullback-composition comparisons. This defines the actual scheme-site stack refining the imported parent root-picard; its projection to the ordinary Picard stack forgets K and ι. No section of either line is part of this definition.

**Hypotheses.** k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.; For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.; Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use native invertible sheaves for each object field and native module isomorphisms for ι. The arrow equation is a fixed typed equality of module morphisms. Use tensor congruence to compose and invert it; no isomorphism-class quotient is taken.
2. Import the coherent symmetric monoidal pullback on the native Picard core from SF.3/picard-groupoid, including its AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A/L0B dependencies. For the Cartesian base-change square, compare restriction-after-pullback and pullback-after-restriction using Modules.pullbackComp and equality of the composites.

#### Coherent tensor product and dual of root data

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-tensor-coherence` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The native root stack is a symmetric monoidal stack of Picard groupoids. Tensor sends (L,K,ι),(M,N,κ) to (L⊗M,K⊗N, (K⊗N)²≅K²⊗N²→L|R⊗M|R≅(L⊗M)|R); the first comparison reorders the middle factors by the ordinary symmetry. The unit is (O_X,O_R,canonical O_R²≅O_X|R). The dual is (L∨,K∨, (K∨)²≅(K²)∨→(L|R)∨≅L∨|R), where the middle map is (ι∨)⁻¹. Associators, ordinary unsigned symmetry, unitors, evaluation and double dual descend from the native lines, satisfy triangle, pentagon, hexagon and inverse laws, and commute coherently with arbitrary base change and the forgetful functor. The degree grading introduces no Koszul sign.

**Hypotheses.** k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.; For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.; Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/native-root-fibres`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-native-root-fibres), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.trivial`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductAssoc`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductComm`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorTrivialLeftIso`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.tensorTrivialRightIso`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Import the coherent monoidal, rank-one dual and pullback interface from the native Picard groupoid supplier; do not redevelop sheaf tensor products or duals.
2. Define the displayed tensor square using associators and the middle-factor interchange. Apply duality to ι and invert it to obtain the correctly oriented dual comparison.
3. The ordinary coherence isomorphisms of both line factors satisfy the root-arrow square by naturality. Their underlying equalities prove every required root coherence diagram because an arrow is determined by its two line isomorphisms. Pullback comparisons follow the same argument.

**Acceptance.** For a root object A, A⊗A∨ is canonically isomorphic to the root unit, with its square identification respected.; On three root objects the underlying L and K associators are the native ones; fourfold products satisfy the pentagon.; Over an odd field a degree-one object exchanged with itself has ordinary symmetry, not multiplication by −1.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Definition A.1, p. 514; A.2.2, pp. 521–522 The all-degree root Picard objects support tensor translations and inverses. The explicit coherence is the categorical refinement of those operations, using the imported native Picard structure. The cited application is over a finite field; the displayed native and descent arguments justify the stated general-field, finite-étale extension.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.tensorDualCoherence`.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-frame-action` · construction · implementation unchecked.

The map to root triples sends (L,γ) to (L,O_RS,γ⁻¹), using the canonical O_RS²≅O_RS. For an intrinsic root triple, its root frames e:O_RS≅K form a T-torsor. Extract γ=(ι∘e²)⁻¹. Changing frame by e′=e∘mul(u⁻¹) changes γ to u²γ; this fixes the sign convention. This construction is natural in S, retains arrows on L, and identifies the atlas map Pic_{X,R}→RootPic with a T-torsor after every scheme base change. Rigidified line bundles themselves are imported, including the current native RigidifiedLineBundle carrier, not defined again here.

**Hypotheses.** k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.; For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.; Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/native-root-fibres`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-native-root-fibres), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-stack-curve`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/torsor-representability`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/affine-fpqc-descent`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/square-action-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-square-action-quotient).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the imported native rigidified-line groupoid along i_S. Finite-étale Weil restriction supplies the frame functor and T, with arbitrary base-change compatibility; this is the precise GC0-WEIL-FRAMES request.
2. Over a frame, apply ι to e² and invert to extract γ. Compare e and e′ to obtain the formula γ′=u²γ, including its identity and product laws.
3. For a map S→RootPic, objects of the 2-fibre product with Pic_{X,R} are rigidified lines together with a specified root isomorphism to the given triple. Sending this datum to its induced frame gives the frame torsor, including its arrows; the inverse uses that frame. Descent supplies frames locally even when K is not globally trivial.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.frameAtlas` (constructor): Send (L,γ) to (L,O,γ⁻¹), with the canonical unit-square comparison inserted.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.rescale` (structure): The right action is (L,γ)·u=(L,u²γ), acts identically on underlying f, and satisfies action identity/composition.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.frameChange` (characterisation): Frames differing by u⁻¹ give γ′=u²γ and the root arrow (1,u) between the resulting atlas objects.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.frameBaseChange` (functoriality): Root frames, their T-action and the atlas square commute with arbitrary S′→S, including nonflat maps.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.frameTorsor` (equivalence): The 2-fibre of frameAtlas over A is the T-torsor of frames of its actual K; no global frame is chosen.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC0.check_frame_empty` (degenerate): For R=∅, T is the trivial group scheme, Pic_{X,R} is the ordinary Picard stack and the atlas is its identity up to equivalence.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-degree-components"></a>

#### Root degree components in every integer degree

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-degree-components` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Define the fibrewise locally constant integer degree of (L,K,ι) to be deg(L), with no division by two. For every d∈Z, the root degree-d stack is the 2-pullback of ordinary Picard^d along forget. These open-and-closed components decompose the root stack as a coproduct indexed by Z. Tensor maps degrees (d,e) to d+e; dual maps d to −d. The decomposition commutes with arbitrary k-scheme base change. Ordinary Picard^d is imported as a G_m-gerbe over its Picard-sheaf torsor Pic^d under Pic^0. This neither chooses X(k) nor supplies a k-object in every component. Over an algebraic closure every integer component has objects.

**Hypotheses.** k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.; For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.; Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/native-root-fibres`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-native-root-fibres), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-tensor-coherence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-tensor-coherence), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-stack-curve`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-scheme-without-point`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Import the ordinary family degree and its open-and-closed components from SF.3/picard-stack-curve, and pull those components back along forget. Families with several degrees on disconnected bases correspond to the coproduct, not to a single fixed-degree fibre.
2. Compute tensor and dual degree on L via the imported ordinary degree formulas. Restriction to the zero-dimensional R imposes no parity condition on this degree.
3. Over an algebraic closure choose a point of X to exhibit O(d x); its restriction to finite reduced R has a square root. This is a test proof of geometric nonemptiness, not a point included in the definition over k. Keep Pic^d as the supplier torsor.

**Acceptance.** The object O(−1) in the native negative-degree test lies in component −1.; After base extension, the degree-d component is the pullback of the original degree-d component.; No equivalence Pic^d≃Pic^0 is asserted without a chosen degree-d class; no universal line is inferred from a rational point of the Picard sheaf.

#### Square quotient equivalence on objects and arrows

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/square-quotient-comparison` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The equivalence commutes with the map to the ordinary Picard stack and restricts to every d∈Z. On the atlas it is the stated (L,O,γ⁻¹) functor; on a change by u its root isomorphism is (1,u). The inverse uses the torsor of actual root-line frames, with unit and counit recovered by descent of the frame identification. For nonempty R the rigidified Picard stack has trivial inertia and is an algebraic space; SF.3 ordinary Picard algebraicity and SF.1 quotient algebraicity give algebraicity of RootPic. For empty R the statement reduces to the ordinary Picard stack, without treating it as an algebraic space.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/relative-root-gerbe` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

H is finite étale of rank 2^ρ for ρ=rank(R/k). Over an algebraic closure with r branch points the relative inertia is μ₂^r. The entire root stack has the ordinary scalar automorphisms in addition, as the full-stabilizer theorem specifies.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-stabilizers"></a>

#### Full and relative inertia, including root sections

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-stabilizers` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For any root object over S, its full automorphism sheaf consists of c∈Γ(S,O_S)× and u∈Γ(R_S,O_RS)× satisfying u²=c|R_S; here c acts on L via the universal identity Γ(X_S,O)=Γ(S,O). Relative to a fixed L and its identity, impose c=1, giving Res μ₂. With root section α, add uα=α. These are equalities of sheaves on every S′→S, including nonreduced S′. After base change to an algebraically closed field with r branch points and compatible frames, full inertia is {(c,u_1,…,u_r):u_j²=c}, and the section inertia additionally has u_j a_j=a_j. Relative section inertia is μ₂ on exactly the zero coordinates and trivial on nonzero coordinates over that field. If any a_j≠0 then c=1 in the full section inertia; if r>0 and every coordinate is nonzero the full section inertia is trivial. For r=0 the full inertia remains G_m, while relative inertia is trivial.

In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.; For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.; Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.

**Construction/proof.**

1. An automorphism of an invertible sheaf is multiplication by a unique unit. The imported universal global-functions identity for X_S identifies the unit on L with c from S; the root line has unit u on R_S.

<a id="gc-1"></a>

## GC.1 — Root divisors and Abel–Jacobi maps

Present root divisor spaces as relative evaluation two-pullbacks, rather than root equations on rational points. Scheme-theoretic incidence and frame directions prove smoothness; full branch fibres still have nilpotents. Root addition multiplies coordinates, while ordered maps have multiplication kernels at branch collisions. The four Abel–Jacobi maps distinguish forgetting global sections from forgetting root sections.

**Planets.** Root symmetric powers — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space); Root symmetric-power smoothness — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-smooth); Root symmetric coarse space — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-coarse); Addition of root divisors — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-addition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-addition); Root Abel–Jacobi maps — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-abel-jacobi`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-abel-jacobi); Ordered root divisors — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-inertia-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-inertia-comparison).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Imported objects and their usable interfaces

##### Root symmetric powers

The declaration `rootSymmetricPower`, imported from `FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`, has hat groupoid $\widehat{\mathcal X}_d(T)$ with objects
$$
(L,K_R,\iota,a,\alpha),\qquad
\iota:K_R^{\otimes2}\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_{R_T},\qquad
\iota(\alpha^{\otimes2})=a|_{R_T}.
$$
Here $L$ is an invertible sheaf on $X_T$ of degree $d$ on each geometric fibre, $K_R$ is an invertible sheaf on $R_T$, and $a,\alpha$ are sections on those respective spaces. An arrow to the primed tuple is a pair of isomorphisms $u:L\to L'$, $v:K_R\to K'_R$ satisfying
$$
u(a)=a',\qquad v(\alpha)=\alpha',\qquad
\iota'\circ v^{\otimes2}=u|_{R_T}\circ\iota.
$$
The effective open $\mathcal X_d$ requires $a$ to be nonzero on **each geometric fibre**. Its divisor gives the coarse map $c_d:\mathcal X_d\to\operatorname{Sym}^dX$. The open $U_d$ is the inverse image of $\operatorname{Sym}^d(X\setminus R)$. Hat objects admit $a=0$. A global section that is nonzero as an element can still be zero on every geometric fibre.

This object supports the ordered-map pushforwards in GC.3, the Abel–Jacobi descent in GC.4, and the hat pullbacks in GC.5. Its source locator is Yun–Zhang, Definition A.2, printed p. 515, and A.1.3, pp. 515–516, with the two inherited source corrections recorded below.

The imported API and tests retain their parent names:

| Name | API contract |
| --- | --- |
| `rootSymmetricPower.hatObject` | Construct a hat object from the five data and the restriction equation. |
| `rootSymmetricPower.effectiveOpen` | The open X_d consists exactly of sections nonzero on every geometric fibre. |
| `rootSymmetricPower.forgetRoot` | Forgetting the root line and section maps to the ordinary degree-d section space. |
| `rootSymmetricPower.awayFromR` | On divisors disjoint from R the root-forgetting map is an equivalence. |

| Name | Unit test |
| --- | --- |
| `rootSymmetricPower.test_d_zero` | At d=0 the effective space is Spec k; the section nowhere vanishes. |
| `rootSymmetricPower.test_empty_R` | At R=∅ the effective space is Sym^d X. |
| `rootSymmetricPower.test_closed_fibre` | Over a divisor containing a branch point the full fibre has the nilpotent root chart, rather than only Bμ₂. |
| `rootSymmetricPower.test_hat_zero` | The hat degree-d space admits a=0 and α_R=0 for any root-Picard object in that degree. |

##### Addition and ordered divisors

The imported `rootAddition` (`GC.1/root-addition`) sends two tuples to
$$
(L\otimes L',\ K_R\otimes K'_R,\ \iota\otimes\iota',\ a\otimes a',\ \alpha\otimes\alpha'),
$$
using the canonical rearrangement of the tensor factors in the power isomorphism. It is defined on both hat spaces and restricts to $\mathcal X_d\times\mathcal X_e\to\mathcal X_{d+e}$. Products of nonzero sections on each integral geometric curve fibre are nonzero. It also defines effective-divisor translation on the hat space. The degree-zero unit has both line bundles trivial and both sections $1$. General tensor associators, symmetry and units are imported, and their compatibility with the root equation is part of the contract.

The imported `orderedRootDivisors` (`GC.1/ordered-divisors`) is the iterated sum
$$
p_d:(\mathcal X_1)^d\longrightarrow\mathcal X_d.
$$
The empty sum is the unit and $p_1$ is the identity. Permutations of the ordered factors come with coherent isomorphisms over the target. This map is used to form symmetric direct images in GC.3; its coherence is required before any symmetric-group invariant operation. Yun–Zhang A.1.4, (A.2)–(A.3), printed p. 517, is the source for these operations. Their coordinate and inertia refinements appear below.

The imported API and tests retain their parent names:

| `rootAddition.unit` | Adding the degree-zero unit object gives the original divisor. |
| `rootAddition.coherence` | Associativity and symmetry are the imported coherent tensor isomorphisms, with the same section equations. |

| Name | Unit test |
| --- | --- |
| `rootAddition.test_empty` | Adding two empty divisors gives the empty divisor. |
| `rootAddition.test_ordinary` | At R=∅ this is ordinary symmetric-power addition. |
| `rootAddition.test_branch_section` | Two zero root-section values multiply to zero, rather than cancel or become nonzero. |

The imported API and tests retain their parent names:

| `orderedRootDivisors.permutation` | Every σ∈S_d acts on the source and p_d is equivariant with coherent target isomorphisms. |
| `orderedRootDivisors.blockAddition` | Concatenating ordered tuples agrees with root addition after their separate p_d maps. |

| Name | Unit test |
| --- | --- |
| `orderedRootDivisors.test_zero` | p_0 maps the point to the empty root divisor. |
| `orderedRootDivisors.test_one` | p_1 is identity on the root curve. |
| `orderedRootDivisors.test_collision` | p_2 is not representable at two equal branch points: its relative inertia contains diagonal μ₂. |

##### The four Abel–Jacobi maps

The imported `rootAbelJacobi` (`GC.1/root-abel-jacobi`) takes values in the **stacks** from `GC.0/root-picard` and `GC.0/root-picard-section`. Write them as $\mathcal P_d$ and $\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{sec}}$. Their objects are respectively $(L,K_R,\iota)$ and $(L,K_R,\iota,\alpha)$. The latter does not require that $\iota(\alpha^2)$ lift to a global section on $X_T$.

There are two hat maps and their two effective restrictions:
$$
\widehat{AJ}_d:\widehat{\mathcal X}_d\to\mathcal P_d,
\qquad
\widehat{AJ}^{\mathrm{sec}}_d:\widehat{\mathcal X}_d\to\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{sec}},
\qquad
AJ_d,\ AJ_d^{\mathrm{sec}}\text{ on }\mathcal X_d.
$$
The first forgets $a,\alpha$, while the refined map forgets only $a$. Their arrows are the corresponding forgetful operations on actual isomorphisms. They feed the unrefined high-degree geometry of GC.4 and the hat character pullbacks of GC.5. Yun–Zhang A.1.5, printed p. 517, gives both hat maps. For empty $R$, their effective versions are the ordinary degree-$d$ Abel map to the Picard stack; composition to its Picard sheaf is the usual map to $\mathrm{Pic}^d$. This specifies the stack/sheaf distinction in the inherited empty-branch test.

The imported API and tests retain their parent names:

| `rootAbelJacobi.refined` | The refined map forgets a and retains α_R. |
| `rootAbelJacobi.addition` | AJ_{d+e}∘add≅mult∘(AJ_d×AJ_e). |

| Name | Unit test |
| --- | --- |
| `rootAbelJacobi.test_empty_R` | At R=∅ the effective map is the ordinary Abel–Jacobi map to Pic^d. |
| `rootAbelJacobi.test_zero` | At d=0 the effective point maps to the tensor unit. |
| `rootAbelJacobi.test_hat_zero` | A zero global section still has a defined hatAJ image. |

#### Hat and effective root symmetric powers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space` · definition · implementation unchecked.

For d≥0 let hatX_d^√R classify (L,K_R,ι,a,α_R) of degree d with a∈Γ(X×S,L) and ι(α_R²)=a|_{R×S}. Define X_d^√R as the open where a is nonzero on every geometric fibre, and U_d^√R as the inverse image of Sym^d(X−R). Hat spaces admit zero global sections and nonreduced bases.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard-section`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard-section), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Impose the equality between the squared root section and the restriction of a.
2. Use the ordinary curve supplier to show fibrewise-nonzero sections define relative effective divisors of degree d.
3. Take the inverse image of divisors supported away from R.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.hatObject` (constructor): Construct a hat object from the five data and the restriction equation.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.effectiveOpen` (characterisation): The open X_d consists exactly of sections nonzero on every geometric fibre.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.forgetRoot` (projection): Forgetting the root line and section maps to the ordinary degree-d section space.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.awayFromR` (compatibility): On divisors disjoint from R the root-forgetting map is an equivalence.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.test_d_zero` (degenerate): At d=0 the effective space is Spec k; the section nowhere vanishes.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.test_empty_R` (compatibility): At R=∅ the effective space is Sym^d X.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.test_closed_fibre` (non-example): Over a divisor containing a branch point the full fibre has the nilpotent root chart, rather than only Bμ₂.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootSymmetricPower.test_hat_zero` (non-example): The hat degree-d space admits a=0 and α_R=0 for any root-Picard object in that degree.

**Acceptance.** Nonzero means fibrewise nonzero, not merely a nonzero element of the total section group.
