<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-smooth-criterion"></a>

#### The evaluation smoothness criterion

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-smooth-criterion` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Let Z be a smooth irreducible scheme over an algebraically closed field and let r line bundles with sections determine f:Z→[A^r/G_m^r]. Assume no section vanishes identically on Z, so each scheme-theoretic zero locus D_i is an effective Cartier divisor, possibly empty. Then f is smooth if and only if every D_i is smooth and all their intersections are transverse, with each nonempty intersection indexed by I of codimension |I|.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; Z is smooth and irreducible over an algebraically closed field; each section is not identically zero. Vanishing loci and their intersections are scheme-theoretic; an empty divisor is allowed.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/two-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-two-pullback), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Trivialize the line bundles and pull back the standard torus atlas.
2. Translate smoothness to the differential rank of the section coordinates on every vanishing stratum.
3. Smooth divisors and independent conormals supply that rank; conversely smoothness pulls back the coordinate normal-crossing strata.

**Acceptance.** A zero section on all of Z fails the smooth divisor condition.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Claim in the proof of Lemma A.4(1), p. 516; Definition A.3 on that page is a different item. The source claim assumes Z smooth and irreducible and each section not identically zero. Its scheme-theoretic vanishing divisors are smooth and meet transversely precisely when the classifying map is smooth.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-pullback"></a>

#### Evaluation description of root symmetric powers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-pullback` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

The root symmetric-power stack is the two-pullback of the ordinary evaluation map to [Res_R A¹/Res_R G_m] along its square-power map. Over a splitting field the latter is a product of copies of [A¹/G_m], one for each geometric point of R.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/two-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-two-pullback), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Evaluate the universal line bundle with section along R.
2. Identify the square-root fibre data with K_R,α_R,ι by the root two-pullback.
3. Descent through the finite étale splitting of R identifies the Weil restriction and product description.

**Acceptance.** ρ is the number of geometric branch points after base change, not the number of closed points over k.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.3 diagram (A.1) p. 516

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-incidence-transversality"></a>

#### Incidence divisors meet transversely

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/incidence-transversality` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

After splitting R, in Sym^d X each incidence divisor D_x of effective divisors containing x is smooth, and intersections for a subset I of distinct branch points identify with Sym^{d−|I|}X when d≥|I|, with codimension |I|; the intersection is empty when d<|I|.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use addition of the fixed reduced divisor Σ_{x∈I}x to identify the intersection.
2. The ordinary symmetric-power supplier gives smoothness and dimension d−|I|.
3. Use the dimension calculation to obtain normal-crossing transversality.

**Acceptance.** Repeated roots of the moving divisor do not replace distinct branch points in I.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.4 pp. 516–517

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-addition"></a>

#### Addition of root divisors

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-addition` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For d,e≥0 tensor L and K_R and multiply both sections to define hatadd_{d,e}:hatX_d^√R×hatX_e^√R→hatX_{d+e}^√R. Restriction gives addition on the effective opens; the same construction gives effective-divisor translation of the hat space.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use tensor products of the two root isomorphisms.
2. The product section satisfies the restriction equation because tensor and restriction commute.
3. A product of fibrewise-nonzero sections on an integral smooth curve is fibrewise nonzero.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition.object` (simp): Root addition tensors line bundles and multiplies sections.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition.unit` (simp): Adding the degree-zero unit object gives the original divisor.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition.coherence` (structure): Associativity and symmetry are the imported coherent tensor isomorphisms, with the same section equations.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition.test_empty` (degenerate): Adding two empty divisors gives the empty divisor.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition.test_ordinary` (compatibility): At R=∅ this is ordinary symmetric-power addition.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition.test_branch_section` (non-example): Two zero root-section values multiply to zero, rather than cancel or become nonzero.

**Acceptance.** The empty degree-zero divisor is the addition unit; root sections are multiplied, not added.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 A.2.1; how: Defines p_d and the multiplicativity maps.; where: YZ19 §6.1.4; how: The specialized hat translation consumer imports this operation.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.4, pp. 517–518; (A.2) on p. 517.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAddition`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-smooth"></a>

#### Smoothness of root symmetric powers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The effective root symmetric power X_d^√R is smooth over k of dimension d and is DM. Its evaluation map to [Res_R A¹/Res_R G_m] is smooth.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/incidence-transversality`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-incidence-transversality), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-smooth-criterion`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-smooth-criterion), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-pullback), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/regular-dm`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-regular-dm).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the incidence calculation to show ordinary evaluation is smooth.
2. Pull that map back along the square-power classifying map to obtain root evaluation smoothness.
3. The root chart and invertibility of two give the smooth DM stack and its dimension.

**Acceptance.** This is not a claim that the whole hat section space is smooth in arbitrary degree.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.4 pp. 516–517

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-coarse"></a>

#### Coarse symmetric-power space

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The root-forgetting projection X_d^√R→Sym^d X is its coarse-space morphism and is an equivalence over Sym^d(X−R).

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-pullback), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/coarse-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-coarse-space), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/base-change`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-base-change).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the relative root coarse-space theorem to the evaluation two-pullback.
2. Away from the incidence divisors the section is invertible, so the root universal property gives an equivalence.

**Acceptance.** The full fibre at an incidence divisor is still the quotient nilpotent chart.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.3 p. 516

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-divisors"></a>

#### The ordered root-divisor morphism

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-divisors` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Iterated addition defines p_d:(X_1^√R)^d→X_d^√R, with its S_d-equivariance and the degree-zero unit map.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-addition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-addition).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Iterate addition using the fixed associativity coherence.
2. Permute factors through the tensor symmetry and prove the symmetric-group relations.
3. Define the empty product as the degree-zero unit object.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors.one` (simp): p_1 is the identity.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors.permutation` (functoriality): Every σ∈S_d acts on the source and p_d is equivariant with coherent target isomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors.blockAddition` (compatibility): Concatenating ordered tuples agrees with root addition after their separate p_d maps.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors.test_zero` (degenerate): p_0 maps the point to the empty root divisor.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors.test_one` (compatibility): p_1 is identity on the root curve.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors.test_collision` (non-example): p_2 is not representable at two equal branch points: its relative inertia contains diagonal μ₂.

**Acceptance.** At a collision of two branch points the stabilizer map μ₂×μ₂→μ₂ has a nontrivial kernel.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 Lemmas A.6–A.8; how: Produces the invariant direct image and its symmetric-group action.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.4, (A.3), p. 517.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedRootDivisors`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-abel-jacobi"></a>

#### Root Abel–Jacobi maps

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-abel-jacobi` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Define hatAJ_d:hatX_d^√R→Pic_X^√R,d by forgetting a and α_R, and the refined map retaining α_R to Pic_X^{√R;√R,d}. Restrict the first map to AJ_d:X_d^√R→Pic_X^√R,d. Addition commutes with the product AJ_d×AJ_e and Picard tensor multiplication.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard-section`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard-section), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-addition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-addition).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Define both functors by explicit forgetful operations on objects and arrows.
2. Their composition forgets exactly the root section.
3. Compare tensoring and forgetting on data to obtain the product square with specified 2-isomorphism.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi.hat` (projection): The hat map forgets both sections and retains the two root line bundles and ι.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi.refined` (projection): The refined map forgets a and retains α_R.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi.addition` (compatibility): AJ_{d+e}∘add≅mult∘(AJ_d×AJ_e).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi.test_empty_R` (compatibility): At R=∅ the effective map is the ordinary Abel–Jacobi map to Pic^d.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi.test_zero` (degenerate): At d=0 the effective point maps to the tensor unit.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi.test_hat_zero` (non-example): A zero global section still has a defined hatAJ image.

**Acceptance.** The refined target retains α_R; the ordinary target does not.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 A.2.2–A.2.3; how: Defines high-degree descent and hat coefficient pullbacks.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.5, p. 517: both hat Abel–Jacobi maps and their effective restrictions.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAbelJacobi`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-relative-evaluation-equivalence"></a>

#### Relative evaluation and its chosen two-pullback equivalence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/relative-evaluation-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Let H_d(T) be the imported ordinary groupoid of degree-d line bundles L on X_T with section a. Let A_R(T) be line bundles with sections on R_T, with square functor theta_2(K,alpha)=(K tensor K,alpha tensor alpha). Restriction defines ev_R:H_d→A_R. Construct a pseudonatural equivalence from the parent hat root-symmetric stack to H_d times_{A_R,theta_2} A_R. Over every T it sends (L,K,iota,a,alpha) to ((L,a),(K,alpha),iota). On an arrow (u,v), iota prime composed with v squared equals u restricted to R composed with iota, and u(a)=a prime, v(alpha)=alpha prime. Its inverse retains exactly this data. The comparison commutes with arbitrary pullback on T with specified identity and composition modifications. After a finite separable splitting of R, A_R becomes a product of rho copies of [A1/G_m], with the descent action permuting geometric branch points.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor on X, possibly empty; rho is its degree, so after algebraic closure there are rho distinct branch points.; The degree d is a natural number. Test schemes T/k are arbitrary, including nonreduced schemes. All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-pullback), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/universal-section-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-stack-curve`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/line-bundle-section-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the ordinary section stack from SF.3 and the finite-etale restriction contract GC1-RESTRICTION; restriction of invertible sheaves and sections gives ev_R, without any assertion that a pushforward on X is locally free.
2. Apply the SF.1 two-fibre-product construction. The specified isomorphism between the two restricted section objects is exactly iota with iota(alpha squared)=a restricted to R.
3. Check the two arrow compatibility equations before constructing the inverse functor. Unit and counit are componentwise identities under the chosen two-pullback model.
4. Use imported coherent sheaf pullback (upstream AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0B) to give the pseudonaturality modifications. Verify their equations on L, K, both sections and iota.
5. Split the finite etale k-scheme R and use Galois descent to recover the unsplit comparison.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.object` (constructor): The forward functor sends a root tuple to its two section objects and iota, preserving a=0.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.arrow` (characterisation): An arrow is exactly a pair (u,v) satisfying the section and square-isomorphism equations in the statement.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.inverse` (equivalence): The inverse functor recovers the five pieces of root data, including the specified power isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.unitCounit` (relation): The unit and counit have identity components on all root data; their triangle equations hold.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.baseChange` (functoriality): For every T prime→T the pullback comparison is a natural isomorphism; identity and composition comparisons obey the pseudofunctor coherence equations.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.splitBranch` (compatibility): After a splitting field extension the restriction stack is the product over all geometric points of R, and the equivalence is Galois equivariant.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.test_empty_R` (degenerate): For R empty, A_R is terminal and the equivalence reduces to the ordinary section stack H_d, including zero sections.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.test_zero` (non-example): For d=0, trivial L and K and iota=1, the tuple a=0, alpha=0 exists in the hat stack and maps to the zero-section object.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.test_nilpotent` (non-example): For d=0 over T=Spec k[epsilon]/epsilon squared with R nonempty, trivial lines, iota=1, a=0 and alpha=epsilon is a hat object. It maps to alpha=0 after reduction, and is not isomorphic to that zero-root-section object over T.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence.test_arrow` (characterisation): Over an algebraically closed field, d=0, a=alpha=0 and trivial lines, automorphisms are v in (G_m)^rho and u in G_m satisfying v_x squared=u for every x. The comparison preserves this group, not only its set of isomorphism classes.

**Acceptance.** The specified iota and all automorphisms survive the equivalence.; The construction is natural for a map killing a nonzero nilpotent root section.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 Lemma A.4, pp. 516–517; how: Pull back ordinary evaluation to obtain root symmetric geometry.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-abel-jacobi; how: Retain the two different forgetful maps on arbitrary test schemes.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Definition A.2, p. 515, and diagram (A.1), p. 516. The moduli data and evaluation square determine the functor; the arrow and coherence formulas here spell out the relative equivalence. [UP-VB](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/0d144d044dacebca17b654695b6f1ad58f159b27/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicVectorBundles/README.md) — Layers L0A–L0B (unpaginated README and Suggested.lean). General tensor and pullback coherence is an import, not a second construction here.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.relativeEvaluationEquivalence`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-incidence-residual-equivalence"></a>

#### Scheme-theoretic incidence residuals

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/incidence-residual-equivalence` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Work over an algebraic closure K of k. For a set I of distinct points of R_K and d at least the cardinality r of I, construct an isomorphism Sym^{d-r} X_K→the scheme-theoretic intersection of D_x for x in I, where D_x is the vanishing of the universal divisor section at x. The forward map adds E_I=sum of x in I; the inverse removes E_I as a relative Cartier subdivisor. On arbitrary K-schemes T, membership means E_I times T is a closed subscheme of the universal relative divisor. The residual divisor is finite locally free of degree d-r and formation commutes with arbitrary T base change. If r>d the intersection is empty. In particular, all nonempty intersections are smooth of codimension r, including at divisors with repeated support at some x.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor on X, possibly empty; rho is its degree, so after algebraic closure there are rho distinct branch points.; The degree d is a natural number. Test schemes T/k are arbitrary, including nonreduced schemes. All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/incidence-transversality`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-incidence-transversality), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/universal-section-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the universal relative divisor from the ordinary symmetric-power supplier. Its restriction at x vanishes scheme-theoretically exactly when the graph x times T is contained in the divisor.
2. The graphs for distinct x are disjoint Cartier divisors, so joint containment is containment of E_I times T. Apply residual subtraction for relative effective Cartier divisors (Stacks Lemma 44.3.3).
3. Subtracting E_I and adding it back are inverse natural transformations of represented functors, including on nonreduced T; apply Yoneda.
4. Negative residual degree is impossible on any geometric fibre. Smoothness and the dimension d-r follow from ordinary symmetric powers, not a tangent-space calculation on geometric points alone.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.forward` (constructor): Add the fixed divisor E_I to the universal degree-(d-r) divisor.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.inverse` (equivalence): Take the unique relative Cartier residual D minus E_I; its degree is d-r.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.universalDivisor` (compatibility): Under the comparison, the pulled-back universal divisor equals the residual universal divisor plus E_I times the parameter scheme.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.baseChange` (functoriality): Residual subtraction and the scheme isomorphism commute with every base change of the test scheme, with identity and composition laws.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.nesting` (relation): For disjoint I and J, removing I then J agrees with removing their union under the canonical degree identifications.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.test_empty` (degenerate): For I empty the comparison is the identity of Sym^d X.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.test_degree_one` (computation): For d=1 and I={x}, the incidence scheme is the point x, identified with Sym^0 X.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.test_excess` (non-example): For d=1 and I={x,y}, x different from y, the intersection is empty, rather than a point of a fictitious negative symmetric power.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence.test_double` (compatibility): For d=2 and I={x}, the residual of the divisor 2x is x; D_x is smooth at 2x. Repeated multiplicity at one branch is not a second incidence equation.

**Acceptance.** The defining ideal is the sum of incidence ideals, rather than its radical.; For d=2, I={x,y} with x different from y, the intersection is the reduced point x+y; at 2x the single divisor D_x is smooth.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 Lemma A.4, pp. 516–517; how: Produces transverse incidence divisors for smooth evaluation.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-normal-crossing-chart; how: Provides independent local equations for the branch divisors.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.4, pp. 516–517, incidence intersections. The proof uses residual addition to identify simultaneous branch incidence with a smaller symmetric power. [STACKS-DIV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9C) — Lemmas 44.3.2–44.3.4 and Proposition 44.3.6 (HTML, unpaginated). Relative divisor addition and subtraction give the arbitrary-base functorial inverse and the needed dimension statement.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.incidenceResidualEquivalence`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-proper"></a>

#### Properness and tame finite relative fibres

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-proper` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

The ordered map p_d is proper and quasi-finite in the nonrepresentable stack sense; the generic distinct-point locus is an S_d-cover. Its finite relative stabilizers are tame μ₂-products. No representably finite morphism is asserted at branch collisions.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-divisors`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-divisors), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-coarse), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. On coarse spaces use proper finite ordinary symmetric-power addition from the curve supplier.
2. The root stacks are proper over their coarse spaces and have finite tame inertia; apply the supplier’s properness comparison.
3. Compute collision stabilizers by the multiplication maps μ₂^m→μ₂; their kernels account for nonrepresentability.

**Acceptance.** The two-equal-branch-point example detects misuse of a representable finite-map theorem.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.4 and A.2.1 pp. 518–519; source gate G4

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-effective-open-base-change"></a>

#### The relative effective open and nilpotent sections

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/effective-open-base-change` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For a hat root-divisor family over T, the locus T_eff of t where a on X over an algebraic closure of kappa(t) is nonzero is open. Pullback to T_eff is the effective root-symmetric family. For every T prime→T its effective locus is the inverse image of T_eff. This is the inverse image under relativeEvaluationEquivalence of the ordinary fibrewise-nonzero section open, and the resulting divisor is a relative effective Cartier divisor finite locally free of degree d. No condition alpha=0 or nonzero is imposed separately. The effective root space has degree-zero component Spec k. The hat stack retains zero and fibrewise-zero infinitesimal sections.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor on X, possibly empty; rho is its degree, so after algebraic closure there are rho distinct branch points.; The degree d is a natural number. Test schemes T/k are arbitrary, including nonreduced schemes. All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/relative-evaluation-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-relative-evaluation-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/universal-section-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the fibrewise-nonzero open and its relative Cartier-divisor comparison in SF.3/universal-section-stack. The exact section-functor restriction adapter is GC1-CURVE-FAMILY.
2. Pull back that open along the two-pullback projection. Fibrewise nonzeroness is unchanged by residue-field extension, giving arbitrary base-change compatibility.
3. Use the relative divisor dictionary of upstream JacobianChallenge C and Stacks Lemma 44.3.1 to obtain finite locally free degree d.
4. In degree zero, a nonzero-on-fibres section trivializes L. Its restriction is a unit, so alpha trivializes K as well, leaving the unit object with trivial automorphisms.

**Acceptance.** Over k[epsilon]/epsilon cubed take trivial lines, a=epsilon squared and alpha=epsilon. This is a hat degree-zero family, has empty effective locus, and has a nonzero global section.; For R empty the effective open is the imported Sym^d X.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Definition A.2, p. 515. The effective condition concerns the global section on every geometric fibre, while the hat object allows zero sections. [STACKS-DIV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9C) — Section 44.3, Lemma 44.3.1 (HTML, no page numbering). For a proper smooth curve, relative effective Cartier divisors of finite degree are finite locally free over the base.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootEffectiveOpen_baseChange`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-atlas-differential"></a>

#### The frame atlas and its differential

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-atlas-differential` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

Let Z be a smooth finite-type scheme over an algebraically closed field, with r invertible sheaves and sections determining f:Z→[A^r/G_m^r]. The pullback of the atlas A^r is the product of their frame torsors E→Z. In compatible local frames its map F:E→A^r is F_i=lambda_i times f_i. At z let I={i:f_i(z)=0}. The differential of F at a point over z is surjective precisely when the covectors df_i(z), i in I, are independent in the cotangent space of Z. Changing a frame multiplies these zero-coordinate covectors by units. Consequently f is smooth exactly when every vanishing stratum is smooth of codimension its number of equations; for the incidence system this applies to all degrees d, without requiring d! to be invertible.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor on X, possibly empty; rho is its degree, so after algebraic closure there are rho distinct branch points.; The degree d is a natural number. Test schemes T/k are arbitrary, including nonreduced schemes. All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.; For the frame criterion Z need not be irreducible; in the parent criterion each section is nonidentically zero on the smooth irreducible Z. The incidence application has this property.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/evaluation-smooth-criterion`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-evaluation-smooth-criterion), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/incidence-residual-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-incidence-residual-equivalence), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/line-bundle-section-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/stack-morphism-properties`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Pull back the quotient atlas by taking the product of frame torsors, not the finite root cover A^r→A^r.
2. Compute dF_i=lambda_i df_i+f_i d lambda_i. For i outside I the vertical frame direction supplies that coordinate independently. For i in I the remaining rank is exactly that of df_i.
3. Apply the prescribed-function smooth-coordinate criterion GC1-SMOOTH-COORDINATES. Independence is equivalent to a smooth complete intersection of the expected codimension at every stratum.
4. Use incidenceResidualEquivalence to supply the required smooth scheme-theoretic intersections.

**Acceptance.** For Z=A1, two equal sections both given by z fail surjectivity at zero: the two covectors coincide.; For Z=A1 and a section z squared, smoothness fails at zero in odd characteristic.; A nowhere-vanishing section has empty zero divisor and its frame direction contributes full rank.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Claim in the proof of Lemma A.4(1), p. 516, and its application on pp. 516–517. The smoothness claim is a criterion for the classifying map. The explicit frame-torsor differential supplies its atlas-level content.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.evaluationAtlas_differential`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-addition-chart-map"></a>

#### The equivariant coordinate map for root addition

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/addition-chart-map` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For a commutative k-algebra A and f,g in A, put C=A[u]/(u squared-fg) and B=A[s,t]/(s squared-f,t squared-g). Construct the A-algebra map C→B with u mapped to st. It is equivariant for the homomorphism mu_2 times mu_2→mu_2 given by multiplication: the source signs on s and t induce their product on st. For all branch coordinates take the product of these homomorphisms. With compatible local frames of the incidence line bundles these quotient maps equal the parent rootAddition, on hat families as well as effective families. The comparisons commute with arbitrary algebra change and with the imported tensor associator, symmetry and unit.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor on X, possibly empty; rho is its degree, so after algebraic closure there are rho distinct branch points.; The degree d is a natural number. Test schemes T/k are arbitrary, including nonreduced schemes. All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-addition`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-addition), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/relative-evaluation-equivalence`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-relative-evaluation-equivalence), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-chart), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.0/section-power`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-0-section-power), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`, `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`, `mathlib:restrictRootsOfUnity`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.EffectiveDivisorOfDegree.equivSym_add`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The relation (st) squared=fg gives the quotient-ring lift. General polynomial-quotient lifts and tensor products are imported, not separate theory targets.
2. On all test A-algebras the sign action sends st to (zeta eta)st. This gives an equivariant scheme morphism in the opposite direction and then the quotient-stack morphism.
3. The universal ordinary divisor of a sum is the sum of divisors, so in compatible frames its section is the product fg; compare the root data component by component using relativeEvaluationEquivalence.
4. Pullback and the tensor coherence isomorphisms give arbitrary-base naturality and the unit, block and permutation comparisons. Their equality is checked on the root line, the section and its square identification.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootAdditionChart.coefficient` (simp): The algebra map is the identity on the coefficient image A.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-normal-crossing-chart"></a>

#### Smooth quotient charts for root symmetric powers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-normal-crossing-chart` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

Over an algebraic closure K, let D in Sym^d X_K and I be the set of branch points contained in its support. There is an etale neighbourhood V=Spec A of D avoiding other incidence divisors, on which D_x, x in I, has equation f_x and the f_x form part of a smooth coordinate system. Over V the effective root-symmetric stack is [Spec B/(mu_2)^I], B=A[t_x:x in I]/(t_x squared-f_x). The action changes each t_x by its own sign. Spec B is smooth over K of dimension d, and its quotient atlas is finite etale and surjective. These charts, with descent over a splitting field, make the effective root space a smooth separated Deligne–Mumford stack of dimension d. No smoothness statement for the whole hat stack is included.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-block-permutation-coherence` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-inertia-comparison` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let q=(q_1,...,q_d) be a geometric point of the product of d root curves and let its coarse divisor be D=sum m_x x. On geometric inertia the parent orderedRootDivisors map is the product, over branch points x with m_x>0, of multiplication homomorphisms mu_2^{m_x}→mu_2. The relative inertia is the product of their kernels. On every commutative K-algebra B, each kernel for m=n+1 is naturally isomorphic to (Fin n→rootsOfUnity 2 B) by discarding coordinate zero; the inverse inserts the inverse of the product in coordinate zero. The multiplication homomorphism and its kernel are canonical under reindexing, and the coordinate isomorphism is natural in B. Its permutation compatibility transports the distinguished omitted index as well as the other indices: if that index is kept fixed, use the action conjugated through this isomorphism, which need not be a permutation of the remaining coordinates. No geometric signs are chosen as the definition of mu_2. Consequently a collision with m_x at least two makes the ordered morphism nonrepresentable in odd characteristic. A divisor containing a branch once has no kernel at that branch.

All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-divisors`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-divisors), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/addition-chart-map`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-addition-chart-map), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/full-fibre-inertia`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-full-fibre-inertia), `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`, `mathlib:restrictRootsOfUnity`, `mathlib:Pi.evalMonoidHom`, `mathlib:MonoidHom.finsetProd_apply`, `mathlib:map_prod`, `tauceti:TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.schemePointsMulEquiv`, `tauceti:TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.schemePointsMulEquiv_mapValue`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/representable-stack-morphism`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the coordinate addition comparison to show that each branch sign acts on the output root line by the product of all signs over that branch. The output has one inertia factor per distinct branch by rootFullFibre_inertia.
2. The fibre automorphism group is the kernel of this actual inertia homomorphism; separated branch factors give a product of kernels.
3. In native rootsOfUnity the kernel coordinate formula and its inverse are finite-product identities in a commutative group. Natural algebra change follows from restrictRootsOfUnity and map_prod, and agrees with the existing schemePointsMulEquiv comparison.
4. Finite products are invariant under reindexing. For an omitted index j, a permutation sigma intertwines the coordinate map omitting j with the one omitting sigma(j). Keeping j fixed instead gives the conjugated action on the remaining coordinates. For three factors and omission of zero, swapping factors zero and one sends (zeta,eta) to ((zeta eta) inverse,eta).
5. For m at least two the element with -1 in two coordinates and 1 elsewhere is a nonidentity kernel point. A morphism representable by algebraic spaces has injective maps of geometric stabilizers, so it cannot have this kernel.

**Acceptance.** For d=0 both source and target inertia are trivial, and for d=1 each inertia map is the identity.; At two equal branch points the source has mu_2 squared, the target has mu_2, and the relative kernel is diagonal mu_2.; At a double collision away from R both inertia groups are trivial; any symmetric-group ramification of the coarse ordered map is a different phenomenon.; No invertibility of d! is used, including when the characteristic divides d!.; For a block of three factors, write its kernel element as ((zeta eta) inverse,zeta,eta). The transposition of factors zero and one induces (zeta,eta) mapped to ((zeta eta) inverse,eta) in the fixed omitted-zero coordinates, rather than the transposition of zeta and eta.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.4, (A.3), p. 517; proof of Lemma A.7, pp. 519–520. The ordered sum and its local multiplication homomorphism identify the geometric inertia. The kernel character-triviality conclusion remains owned by GC.3/collision-kernel. <a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-geometric-fibres"></a>

#### Geometric two-fibres of ordered divisors

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-geometric-fibres` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Fix a geometric effective root divisor y over an algebraically closed K, with coarse divisor D=sum m_x x. The underlying points of the ordered-map two-fibre over y are in bijection with the ordered tuples of the multiset D, so their number is d! divided by the product of the m_x!. After choosing a lift and its isomorphism to y for each ordering, the reduction of the two-fibre is the disjoint union of classifying stacks B K_q, where K_q is the product over branch points with m_x>0 of ker(mu_2^{m_x}→mu_2). The full two-fibre can have nilpotent directions and is not replaced by this reduction. In particular these field-valued two-fibres have discrete underlying spaces, providing the missing fibre criterion for the parent proper quasi-finite theorem. All morphism-property conclusions are in the nonrepresentable stack sense.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor on X, possibly empty; rho is its degree, so after algebraic closure there are rho distinct branch points.; The degree d is a natural number. Test schemes T/k are arbitrary, including nonreduced schemes. All products of stacks are two-fibre products and all equivalences include arrows and pullback coherence.; No rational basepoint of X and no coefficient local system is required for this geometric stage.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-divisors`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-divisors), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-coarse-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-coarse-chart), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-inertia-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-inertia-comparison), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/stack-morphism-properties`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/universal-section-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The coarse ordered map X^d→Sym^d X is finite locally free (Stacks Proposition 44.3.6), and its geometric points are precisely the orderings of the multiset D. Each geometric root-curve point over a fixed coarse point is unique up to isomorphism.
2. At each ordering q, orderedInertia identifies the source-to-target inertia map. It is surjective: the product map has at least one factor over every branch occurring in D. Thus the set of isomorphisms from p_d(q) to y modulo source automorphisms is a singleton. The fibre stabilizer is the stated kernel. Local root charts are finite over ordinary divisor charts; after fixing y the remaining root-isomorphism choices are finite too. Together with the finite ordinary ordering fibre this gives a finite-type zero-dimensional DM two-fibre, without assuming the parent proper quasi-finite conclusion.
3. A finite-type zero-dimensional DM stack over an algebraically closed field with finitely many points has reduction a disjoint union of its residual gerbes. The chosen lifts neutralize them. This exact residual-gerbe fact is included in GC1-PERMANENCE; it gives the displayed reduced-fibre description without erasing nilpotent directions in the full fibre.
4. For parent ordered-proper, rootCoarseChart in degree one makes the source proper over k, and the target is separated. Apply Stacks Lemma 101.37.5(2). The map is quasi-DM and locally of finite type, has the discrete fibres just computed, and is quasi-compact by properness. Apply Definitions 101.23.2 and 101.24.1. These properties commute with arbitrary base change.
5. Away from R on the multiplicity-free locus the same map is the ordinary finite etale S_d-torsor of orderings. Constant S_d is etale even when the characteristic divides d!, so no factorial-invertibility hypothesis is used.

**Acceptance.** For d=0 the two-fibre is Spec K, and for d=1 it is Spec K because p_1 is the identity.; For d=2 and D=x+y with x different from y, there are two fibre points and both relative stabilizers are trivial, including when x or y is a branch point.; For X=P1, R={0}, d=2 and D=2 times 0, local coordinates give the full two-fibre [Spec K[s,t]/(s squared+t squared,st)/mu_2], with diagonal sign action. Its reduction is Bmu_2; the full fibre retains s and t as nonzero nilpotents.; At a double collision away from R the reduction is one point with trivial inertia; the ordinary ordering fibre can still be nonreduced.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.4, (A.3), p. 517; A.2.1, p. 519. The source uses the ordered map for pushforward. The explicit stack property convention here preserves its nonrepresentable collision behaviour. [STACKS-PROP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CL4) — Lemma 101.37.5(2) and Lemmas 101.37.2–101.37.3 (HTML, unpaginated). A morphism from a proper stack to a separated stack over the same base is proper; base changes preserve it. [STACKS-QF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06PT) — Definition 101.23.2 and Definition 101.24.1 (HTML, unpaginated; latter in tag 0G2L). Quasi-finiteness for stacks includes quasi-DM and the discrete two-fibre condition; representability is not part of this definition. [STACKS-DIV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9C) — Proposition 44.3.6 and its proof (HTML, unpaginated). The coarse ordering morphism is finite locally free of degree d!, in every characteristic. [STACKS-RES](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06MC) — Lemma 101.21.4, with its quotient-groupoid proof; Lemma 101.31.2 (HTML, unpaginated). A reduced singleton DM stack has an etale field atlas. Over the algebraically closed field in this finite-type situation, a chosen object identifies the singleton component with its automorphism classifying stack.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.orderedGeometricFibre`.

## GC.2 — Adelic root Picard groupoids

Native completions and restricted ideles are imports. Simultaneous generic, integral and branch-root frames identify geometric objects and every labelled arrow with the right and double action presentations. The signed right quotient keeps the generic trivialization; no quotient by principal ideles or effectivity condition is imposed until the appropriate separate operation. The exact remaining request is GC2-COMPLETED-LATTICES.

**Planets.** Ramified root units — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units); Adelic root Picard groupoid — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/adelic-root-groupoid`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-adelic-root-groupoid); Framed Picard groupoid — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/fully-framed-root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-fully-framed-root-picard); Degree of the root Picard groupoid — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/valuation-degree-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-valuation-degree-comparison).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Modified units and the two action groupoids

Put \(B_R=\prod_{x\in R}\kappa_x^\times\). The inherited group of modified
units has the equalizer presentation

\[
 H=\{(u,v)\in U\times B_R:\bar u_x=v_x^2\ (x\in R)\}.
\]

Multiplication is componentwise, and \(p:H\to I\) forgets the \(v\)-coordinate.
This is a group fibre product. Squaring is not additive in odd characteristic,
so a fibre-product ring along the square map is not an appropriate carrier.

The imported `rootUnits` API constructs a pair satisfying the square relation,
projects its ordinary unit tuple, and characterizes its kernel by \(u=1\) and
\(v_x^2=1\). Its tests require \(H=U\) at \(R=\varnothing\), a nonidentity
\((1,-1)\) kernel label at a branch point, and failure to lift a unit whose
branch residue is nonsquare. These are tests of the actual homomorphism, not
only of its image.

The new theorem **root-unit-exact-sequence**, proposed name
`TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits_exact`, gives

\[
 1\longrightarrow\prod_{x\in R}\mu_2(\kappa_x)
 \longrightarrow H\longrightarrow U
 \longrightarrow\prod_{x\in R}\kappa_x^\times/(\kappa_x^\times)^2
 \longrightarrow1.
\]

The middle image is exactly the unit tuples having square residue at every
branch point. Reduction on units is surjective at each \(x\), by the native
valuation-subring theorem. Lift the finitely many prescribed residues and take
the other units to be one; this proves surjectivity onto the square-class
product. The kernel of \(p\) consists of the freely retained square roots of
one, proving exactness without any choice of square roots as a homomorphism.

Define the inherited right and double presentations by

\[
 \mathcal D_R=I//H,\qquad
 \mathcal P_R=I//(F^\times\times H),
 \qquad (f,h):a\longrightarrow\operatorname{diag}(f)a\,p(h).
\]

The functor \(Q:\mathcal D_R\to\mathcal P_R\) is the identity on objects and
sends \(h\) to \((1,h)\). It is faithful; it need not be full. The inherited
`rootDivisorGroupoid` API has constructors from an idele and a labelled
modified-unit arrow, the functor \(E\) to the discrete groupoid of signed
divisors, tensor by idele multiplication, inverse by idele inversion, \(Q\),
and the kernel description of every automorphism group. Tensor and functor
laws must be stated for arrows as well as objects.

Four inherited tests pin that API. At empty \(R\), the right groupoid is
equivalent to all signed divisors, with a uniformizer and its inverse giving
\([x]\) and \(-[x]\). An inverse uniformizer outside \(R\) maps under \(Q\) to
\(O_X(x)^\natural\). A branch sign gives a nonidentity automorphism of the
unit idele. Finally, for \(f\in F^\times\) with nonzero principal divisor,
\(1\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(f)\) have no arrow between them in the empty-
\(R\) right quotient, although \((f,1)\) is an arrow in the double quotient.
These tests forbid inserting a principal-idele quotient into
\(\mathcal D_R\), or imposing effectivity there.

#### Degree and sign acceptance

The theorem **valuation-degree-comparison**, proposed name
`TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootPicard_degree`, states that for the equivalence
\(\Phi:\mathcal P_R\simeq\operatorname{Pic}_X^{\sqrt R}(k)\),

\[
 \operatorname{underlyingLine}(\Phi(a))=O_X(-E(a)),\qquad
 \deg\Phi(a)=-\deg E(a)
   =-\sum_x\operatorname{ord}_x(a_x)[\kappa_x:k].
\]

The ordinary degree/divisor comparison supplies the second equality from the
first. A right arrow preserves \(E\). A double arrow changes \(E\) by the
principal divisor of \(f\); the pinned product formula gives degree zero
for that difference. Hence the integer grading is invariant on all arrows,
additive under tensor, and negated by inverse. It also agrees with the degree
of the generic-framed object before applying \(Q\).

Three calculations must commute through the geometric comparisons. At a
closed \(x\notin R\) of degree \(d\), a coefficient \(\pi_x^{-1}\), with
all other coefficients one, gives \(E=-[x]\), line \(O_X(x)^\natural\), and
degree \(d\). Its inverse gives \(E=[x]\), line \(O_X(-x)^\natural\), and
degree \(-d\). A diagonal \(f\) gives \(E=\operatorname{div}(f)\) and a
trivial ordinary line up to isomorphism with degree zero, while still
retaining its generic frame in the right quotient. For \(R=\varnothing\)
these specialize to the ordinary divisor/Picard diagram. For general \(R\),
the square through \(D\mapsto O_X(-D)\) commutes after forgetting root data
to the ordinary Picard groupoid. The root data remain on the separate
\(Q\)-leg. The \(E\)-leg forgets the root labels and their residue square
classes; for nonempty \(R\), the root-sign arrows prevent a factorization
of the root Picard functor through the discrete ordinary divisor groupoid.

There is a convention discrepancy in the proof of Lemma A.5 on published
p. 518. With the source's displayed directions of \(\tau_\eta\) and
\(\tau_x\), the coefficient printed there is the reciprocal of the one used
here. The line \(O_X(x)\) with local frame multiplication by \(\pi_x\)
would then have coefficient \(\pi_x\), conflicting with the lemma's
inverse-uniformizer normalization. The convention here uses
\(\tau_\eta\tau_x^{-1}\), so its rational lattice is \(a_xO_x\) and the
line is \(O_X(-E(a))\). The same ratio occurs in arXiv v2, printed p. 85.
Packet finding EGC2-1 records the correction and the scoped correction search;
the inherited E9 records the separate root-frame tuple notation slip.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units"></a>

#### Modified local units at ramified places

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units` · definition · implementation unchecked.

At x∈R let O_{√x}×={(u,v)∈O_x××k(x)× : ū=v²}, with componentwise multiplication. For x∉R use O_x×. Let O_{√R}× be their product. Its map to adelic units forgets v and has kernel ∏_{x∈R}μ₂(k(x)); do not assume it is injective.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the parent’s local completions, valuation-ring units and residue map.
2. Take the fibre product of multiplicative groups along reduction and the square homomorphism.
3. Form the finite modification of the ordinary unit product, with its actual map to ideles.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits.mk` (constructor): Create (u,v) with ū=v².
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits.forget` (projection): Project to u in O_x× and to the corresponding idele unit.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits.kernel` (characterisation): The kernel consists of u=1 and v²=1.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits.test_empty_R` (degenerate): At R=∅ the product is the ordinary unit product.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits.test_minus_one` (non-example): At a ramified place, (1,−1) is a nontrivial kernel element.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits.test_nonsquare` (computation): A unit with nonsquare residue has no lift to this group.

**Acceptance.** The square operation on residue elements is not additive in odd characteristic; no fibre-product ring is defined here.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 Lemma A.5; how: Gives the action group used in the idele groupoid.; where: YZ19 Proposition A.12; how: The quadratic character is trivial on its image.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.6, pp. 517–518, modified local-unit groups.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-generic-framed-root-picard"></a>

#### Root lines with a generic trivialization

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/generic-framed-root-picard` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Let G_R(X) be the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι,τ_η), where (L,K_R,ι) is the inherited k-point of Pic_X^√R and τ_η:L|Spec F≅F is an F-linear trivialization. An arrow (φ,ψ) satisfies φ|R∘ι=ι′∘ψ^{⊗2} and τ′_η∘φ_η=τ_η. Tensor product multiplies generic trivializations, the unit has its standard generic trivialization, and duality inverts it. Forgetting τ_η maps to the existing root Picard groupoid. Degree is deg L and may have either sign.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.; Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.; I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.; All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/class-group-picard-locally-factorial`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/vector-bundle-degree`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-12-the-dictionary--function-fields--curves-and-the-comparison-contracts`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Add only a generic trivialization to the existing root-line triple; use its existing line-bundle isomorphisms, tensor product and duality.
2. Restrict arrows to those preserving the generic frame. The square-root diagram remains part of each arrow, so root automorphisms are retained.
3. Tensor, dual, restriction and their coherence are imported from GC.0 and the ordinary Picard-groupoid supplier.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.mk` (constructor): Build an object from a root-line triple and an actual generic-fibre isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.forget` (projection): Forget the generic trivialization to Pic_X^√R(k), on both objects and arrows.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.hom_ext` (extensionality): Two arrows are equal exactly when their line-bundle and root-line isomorphisms agree; a root label is never inferred from the line isomorphism alone.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.hom_iff` (characterisation): A pair of isomorphisms is an arrow exactly when it respects both the root square diagram and the displayed generic-frame equality.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.tensor` (structure): Tensor the line bundles, roots, square identifications and generic frames; associators, unitors and symmetry are inherited coherently.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-adelic-root-groupoid"></a>

#### The adelic root Picard groupoid

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/adelic-root-groupoid` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

There is an equivalence Pic_X^√R(k)≃F×\A_F×/O_{√R}× as a double-action groupoid. The right action uses the actual noninjective homomorphism to idele units. Degree and all stabilizers are retained. At x∉R, π_x⁻¹ represents O_X(x)^♮.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Choose a generic trivialization of L and compatible local trivializations; the root-line frame along R yields the residue-square data.
2. Changing the generic and integral frames produces the left F× and right root-unit actions.
3. Reverse by gluing line bundles and root data, and identify automorphisms; use the divisor/idele dictionary with the π⁻¹ sign.

**Acceptance.** For R=∅ recover the Picard groupoid, not just the class group; root-unit kernel elements remain stabilizers.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.5, (A.4) and complete proof, p. 518.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-unit-exact-sequence"></a>

#### The modified-unit kernel and residue-square quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-unit-exact-sequence` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The projection H→U has kernel canonically ∏_{x∈R} μ₂(κ_x), via the retained root coordinates, and image U_sq={u∈U : ū_x is a square in κ_x× for every x∈R}. Reduction followed by residue square class induces U/p(H) ≅ ∏_{x∈R} κ_x×/(κ_x×)². Thus 1→∏ μ₂(κ_x)→H→U→∏ κ_x×/(κ_x×)²→1 is exact as a sequence of abelian groups. The last arrow is onto. At R=∅ its last two nontrivial terms identify H with U. No fibre-product ring is required.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.; Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.; I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.; All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units), `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2/projective-ideles`, `mathlib:MonoidHom.eqLocus`, `mathlib:ValuationSubring.surjective_unitGroupToResidueFieldUnits`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the native valuation-subring residue-unit surjection at each branch point. The curve/completion residue comparison is part of FA.2/projective-adeles and its AlgebraicCurves Layer 5 prerequisite.
2. An element of the projection kernel has u=1 and v_x²=1. Conversely these labels produce every kernel element, without identifying different labels.
3. A unit tuple lifts exactly when all branch residues have square roots. Reduction onto the finitely many branch residue-unit groups is onto; the product of their square-class quotients is therefore the cokernel.

**Acceptance.** For a branch point in odd characteristic, the coordinate (1,−1) is a nonidentity kernel label.; A residue nonsquare is excluded from p(H), even though it belongs to U.; The product is over closed branch points: |ker p|=2^{#|R|}, not 2^{deg R}.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.1.6, pp. 517–518; Lemma A.5 proof, p. 518 The source supplies the residue-square fibre products and their frame-changing action. The exact kernel/image/cokernel sequence is an explicit algebraic deduction from those definitions, not a separately numbered claim of the paper.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootUnits_exact`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-fully-framed-root-picard"></a>

#### The fully framed root Picard groupoid

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/fully-framed-root-picard` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Let F_R(X) have objects (L,K_R,ι,τ_η,(τ_x)_x,(t_x)_{x∈R}), extending G_R(X). Each τ_x is an O_x-linear isomorphism L⊗O_x≅O_x; each t_x is a κ_x-linear isomorphism K_x≅κ_x, and (τ_x mod m_x)∘ι_x=t_x^{⊗2}. Morphisms preserve the root triple and every frame. The transition coefficient is a_x=τ_η∘τ_x^{-1} after extension to F_x. There is no extra summability axiom: for an algebraic line bundle and a rational frame these coefficients are units at all but finitely many x. The forgetful functor to G_R forgets τ_x and t_x. Tensor and dual are componentwise.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.; Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.; I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.; All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the ordinary curve/divisor dictionary and local freeness to obtain the generic and completed local frames; root fibres are one-dimensional over their residue fields.
2. Forgetting a compatible root frame and its root line over a fixed ordinary frame has contractible fibre: the framed residue line with square identification is uniquely isomorphic to the standard one.
3. The requested completed-lattice dictionary proves that local transition coefficients are integral units away from a finite divisor; use the reciprocal of the source proof’s printed transition ratio, as recorded in EGC2-1.
4. Frame-preserving arrows and tensor coherence are inherited; a line map fixed on the generic fibre is determined everywhere on the integral curve.

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.forgetLocalFrames` (projection): Forget all local and root frames to G_R; preserve τ_η.

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.coefficient` (projection): The coefficient at x is the scalar τ_η∘τ_x^{-1}; it is a unit of F_x, and these coefficients form an idele.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.hom_ext` (extensionality): A fully frame-preserving isomorphism is unique when it exists; both the ordinary line and the root line maps are fixed by their frames.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.changeFrames` (functoriality): For (f,h) with h=(u,v), change τ_η to fτ_η, τ_x to u_x^{-1}τ_x and t_x to v_x^{-1}t_x. The root frame equation is preserved, and the coefficient changes to diag(f) a p(h). This is an action functorial on arrows, with identity and composition laws; forgetLocalFrames intertwines it with changeGenericFrame.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.tensor` (structure): Multiply the coefficients under tensor product; unit coefficients are 1 and dual coefficients are inverse. The inherited associator, unitor and symmetry maps preserve all frames.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-divisor-groupoid"></a>

#### The signed root-divisor groupoid

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-divisor-groupoid` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Define Div^√R(X) to be the action groupoid A_F×/O_{√R}× for the actual homomorphism O_{√R}×→A_F×. It contains signed divisors in all degrees; neither quotient by F× nor an effectivity condition is imposed. The forgetful map to A_F×/O×=Div(X) uses E(a)=Σ_x v_x(a_x)x. With this valuation convention its Abel–Jacobi functor lands in the double quotient Pic_X^√R(k) and has underlying line bundle O_X(−E(a)), with the retained square-root line along R. The quadratic character is pulled back along this functor. Effective section moduli are a separate construction; they are not identified with this entire groupoid.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/adelic-root-groupoid`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-adelic-root-groupoid), `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Groupoid`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Form the right-action groupoid of the modified-unit homomorphism. Arrows retain their full labels, including the kernel ∏_{x∈R}μ₂(k(x)); an orbit set would lose these automorphisms.
2. Use the parent’s divisor/idele dictionary E(a)=Σv_x(a_x)x to obtain the ordinary signed divisor, without imposing nonnegative valuations or dividing by F×.
3. Apply the canonical functor to the double quotient and Lemma A.5. Its sign is fixed by a uniformizer π_x⁻¹: E=−x and the associated Picard line is O_X(x). At branch points retain the root line and square isomorphism.
4. Pull back the idele character along this Abel–Jacobi functor; the specialized matrix quotient and 1/#Aut integration remain with ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.ofIdele` (constructor): An idele a determines its object in the right-action groupoid.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.arrow` (constructor): A modified unit h gives the arrow a→a·forget(h); its label h is retained even when forget(h)=1.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.forget` (projection): The ordinary signed divisor is E(a)=Σ_x v_x(a_x)x, and modified-unit arrows preserve it.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.tensor` (structure): Idele multiplication supplies addition of root divisors; identity and inverse give the unit and additive inverse, with their groupoid coherence.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.abelJacobi` (functoriality): The right quotient maps to F×\A_F×/O_{√R}×; its underlying line is O_X(−E) in the stated valuation convention.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.automorphisms` (characterisation): The automorphism group of every idele object is ker(O_{√R}×→A_F×)=∏_{x∈R}μ₂(k(x)); at R=∅ it is trivial.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.test_empty_R_signed` (non-example): For R=∅ the groupoid is equivalent to the discrete groupoid of all signed divisors. A uniformizer idele and its inverse give x and −x; both occur.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.test_uniformizer_sign` (computation): For x∉R the idele equal to π_x⁻¹ at x and 1 elsewhere has E=−x and Abel–Jacobi line O_X(x).
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.test_branch_kernel` (characterisation): At any branch point in odd characteristic, the modified unit with u=1,v=−1 there and identity elsewhere gives a nonidentity automorphism of the unit idele.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid.test_principal_not_quotiented` (non-example): For R=∅ and a nonconstant f∈F× with nonzero principal divisor, the identity and diagonal-f objects are not isomorphic in the right quotient, but their images in the double Picard quotient are isomorphic.

**Acceptance.** At R=∅, both x and −x occur as signed divisors; neither is discarded by an effectivity condition.; A scalar from F× changes the signed divisor by a principal divisor and only becomes identified after the further Picard quotient.; At x∉R, π_x⁻¹ has E=−x but its Abel–Jacobi line is O_X(x).; At a branch point a nontrivial modified-unit kernel label remains a nontrivial automorphism; matrix integration retains 1/#Aut.

**Consumers.** where: Yun–Zhang §6.2.3, p. 498, definition of Div^√R(X) and simultaneous translation on four root divisors; how: Signed root divisors form a group-like action groupoid before quotienting by principal ideles; this supplies the matrix-stack inputs and their automorphisms.; where: Yun–Zhang Lemma 6.4, (6.9), p. 499; how: The pulled-back quadratic character is evaluated on a difference E₁^♮−E₂^♮ and the groupoid sum keeps automorphism weights.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — §6.2.3, p. 498: definition of Div^√R(X), its two maps and O_X(−E); Lemma 6.4, (6.9), p. 499. The source defines the right idele action quotient on all signed divisors. The left F× quotient occurs only in the subsequent Picard map; it is not an effective symmetric-power moduli problem.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootDivisorGroupoid`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-divisor-fibres"></a>

#### Signed divisor fibres with their square classes and stabilizers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-divisor-fibres` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For each signed divisor D of X, the fibre of E:I//H→Discrete(Div(X)) is nonempty. Its isomorphism classes form a torsor under U/p(H)≅∏_{x∈R}κ_x×/(κ_x×)². Every object has automorphism group canonically ker p≅∏_{x∈R}μ₂(κ_x), using its arrow labels. Choosing an idele with E(a)=D and representatives of the square classes yields an equivalence with the disjoint union, indexed by that square-class product, of the classifying groupoid of ∏μ₂(κ_x). This last presentation depends on the choices; the torsor action and the labelled stabilizer identification do not. For r=#|R| there are 2^r components, each with automorphism group of order 2^r.

#### Full morphism descent for the Picard double quotient

Every root-line triple admits generic and compatible local/root frames, so they give the inherited Lemma A.5 equivalence with full faithfulness and essential surjectivity. Q:I//H→I//(F××H) is faithful, with arrow label h↦(1,h), and is the functor that forgets the generic frame.

#### The stabilizer extension in the double quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/picard-stabilizer-extension` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For finite odd k, C_R=(k×)² if R has an odd-degree closed point, and C_R=k× if every closed branch point has even degree; the latter includes R=∅. At R=∅, A_R=k×.

3. For κ_x/k of degree d and q=|k|, a nonsquare constant stays nonsquare exactly when d is odd: the exponent (q^d−1)/(q−1) has parity d. Apply the finite-field square criterion.
4. The kernel is the same labelled root-sign group, but its quotient is only the constants locally square at all branch points. Check the nonsplit example rather than choosing an unjustified section.

The exact extension, parity criterion and nonsplit examples are deductions given here; the source does not state them as a separate theorem.

#### The valuation divisor and Picard degree have opposite signs

The separate Q-leg retains the root data; for nonempty R the retained root-sign arrows prevent a factorization of the root Picard functor through the discrete ordinary divisor groupoid.
