<a id="gc-3"></a>

## GC.3 — Symmetric local systems and exterior cohomology

First construct the symmetric lisse line by monodromy on the root-divisor stack; this route avoids using a stack pushforward merely to define the line. The tensor character is trivial on ordered relative inertia. A rational coarse-space model then reduces cohomology to scheme Künneth and twisted curve cohomology, with the exterior power forced by Koszul signs. The parent pushforward/perverse description is retained as a separate comparison. Existing exterior maps and transfer are imported, with only the additional signed-action and averaging consequences planned.

**Planets.** Tame root-curve local systems — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/tame-local-systems`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-tame-local-systems); Symmetric tensor local systems — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-local-system); Collision descent — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/collision-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-collision-descent); Exterior-power cohomology — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/exterior-cohomology`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-exterior-cohomology); Symmetric local-system multiplication — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-multiplicativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-multiplicativity); Cohomology of symmetric powers — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-power-cohomology`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-power-cohomology).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Graded symmetric invariants of a degree-one space

The cohomology of a product is a graded tensor product, and exchanging two
classes of odd degree costs a sign. On the $d$-th tensor power of a space
concentrated in degree one, the symmetric group therefore acts by the sign
twist of the ordinary permutation action. Tau Ceti already has the ordinary
action, `PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation`, and its invariants (the span
of the pure powers when $d!$ is invertible). The three targets of this section
add the sign and its compatibility/comparison with the existing exterior maps. They are generic
algebra; the packet records that they move to a generic owner if one is
designated.

**New target:** `GC.3/koszul-sign-action`, proposed name
`TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction`. For a commutative ring $K$, a
$K$-module $V$ and $d\ge0$, let $\sigma\in S_d$ act on $V^{\otimes d}$ by

$$
 \sigma\cdot(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_d)=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,
 v_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\sigma^{-1}(d)} .
$$

This is a representation, natural in $V$; it is the action on the degree-$d$
part of the graded tensor power of a module placed in degree one. On degree-zero
factors the same permutation acts without sign.

| Name | Role | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `koszulPermAction` | data | $\sigma\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)P_\sigma$ on $V^{\otimes d}$. |
| `koszulPermAction.apply_tprod` | simp | The formula above on pure tensors. |
| `koszulPermAction.one`, `.mul` | structure | The identity acts trivially; $\sigma\tau$ acts as the composite. |
| `koszulRepresentation` | constructor | The representation $S_d\to\operatorname{End}_K(V^{\otimes d})$. |
| `koszulPermAction.eq_sign_smul_reindexRepresentation` | compatibility | The action is $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$ times Tau Ceti's unsigned `reindexRepresentation`. |
| `koszulPermAction.swap_tprod` | relation | For $d=2$ the transposition sends $v\otimes w$ to $-w\otimes v$. |
| `koszulPermAction.naturality` | functoriality | $f^{\otimes d}$ commutes with the action for every $K$-linear $f$; a $K$-linear Frobenius is a case. |

| Test | Kind | Instance and error detected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `koszulRepresentation.test_degree_zero` | degenerate | For $d=0$ every element of $V^{\otimes0}\simeq K$ is invariant. |
| `koszulRepresentation.test_degree_one` | degenerate | For $d=1$ every element of $V$ is invariant. |
| `koszulRepresentation.test_line_square` | computation | With $2$ invertible the invariants on $K^{\otimes2}$ are zero; the unsigned action would keep the whole line. |
| `koszulRepresentation.test_pure_square` | non-example | With $2$ invertible, $x\otimes x$ is fixed by the unsigned action, but by the Koszul-signed action only when $x\otimes x=0$; forgetting the sign gives symmetric tensors. |
| `koszulRepresentation.test_char_two` | non-example | Over $\mathbf Z/2$ the sign is trivial, so $(\mathbf Z/2)^{\otimes2}$ is invariant although $\wedge^2(\mathbf Z/2)=0$. |

**Existing maps, with one new compatibility lemma:** `GC.3/antisymmetrization`.

in `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basic.lean` at commit

$\alpha_d:\wedge^dV\to V^{\otimes d}$ is

$$
 \alpha_d(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_d)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,
 v_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\sigma(d)},
$$

obtained from Mathlib's `MultilinearMap.alternatization` of the tensor map and
the universal property `exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv`. The exterior

factors. Then $\pi_d\circ\alpha_d=d!\cdot\mathrm{id}$ (Mathlib

invariant under the Koszul-signed action: substituting $\sigma\tau^{-1}$ in the sum
absorbs the sign of $\tau$. No invertibility is needed for the construction.

| --- | --- | --- |

| Test | Kind | Instance and error detected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `antisymmetrization.test_degree_two` | computation | $\alpha_2(v\wedge w)=v\otimes w-w\otimes v$. |

Source: Conrad, *Exterior powers*, §4, display (4.1), p. 12, and p. 13, where the
finite-dimensional vector-space discussion identifies skew-symmetric tensors
and computes the factor $k!$. The all-module unit-factorial comparison below
follows from the explicit two-composite argument and the current-library API.

**New target:** `GC.3/alternating-invariants-exterior` (theorem; Lean
`antisymmetrization.bijective`). If $d!$ is a unit in $K$, then $\alpha_d$ is an
isomorphism from $\wedge^dV$ onto the Koszul-signed invariants
$(V^{\otimes d})^{S_d}$, with inverse $(d!)^{-1}\pi_d$. Indeed $\alpha_d\circ\pi_d$
is the sum of the Koszul-signed permutations, which is $d!$ on invariants. The
isomorphism is natural, hence Frobenius-equivariant; for $V$ free of rank $n$ the
invariants are free of rank $\binom nd$ (Mathlib `exteriorPower.finrank_eq`), zero
for $d>n$. As the parent notes, over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ every $d!$ is
invertible, including when the prime $\ell$ divides $d!$; only integral or
torsion coefficients would need more care, and GC.3 does not use them. Checks: for $\dim V=1$ and $d=2$
the invariants vanish while the symmetric invariants would not; over
$\mathbf Z/2$ the statement fails, so the hypothesis cannot be dropped. This
discharges the parent gap EXTERIOR-COMP and is the input of the parent lemma
`GC.3/koszul-exterior`.

### Target catalogue

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-koszul-sign-action"></a>

#### Koszul-signed permutation action on tensor powers

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/koszul-sign-action` · definition · implementation unchecked.

Let K be a commutative ring, V a K-module and d≥0. The Koszul-signed action of S_d=Perm({1,…,d}) on the tensor power V^{⊗d} sends σ to sgn(σ)·P_σ, where P_σ(v_1⊗⋯⊗v_d)=v_{σ⁻¹(1)}⊗⋯⊗v_{σ⁻¹(d)} is Tau Ceti's permutation representation PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation. It is a representation of S_d by K-linear maps, natural in V. It is the S_d-action on the degree-d summand of the graded tensor power of a graded module concentrated in cohomological degree one: exchanging two factors of odd degree contributes −1. On a tensor power of degree-zero factors the same permutation acts by P_σ, without sign.

**Hypotheses.** K is a commutative ring, V any K-module and d a natural number.; In GC.3 the case used is K=Q̄ℓ and V=H¹(X⊗k̄,j_*L)≅H¹(X_1^√R⊗k̄,L), on which geometric Frobenius acts K-linearly.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation`, `tauceti:PiTensorProduct.commute_reindexRepresentation_map`, `mathlib:PiTensorProduct.reindex`, `mathlib:PiTensorProduct.map_reindex`, `mathlib:TensorPower`, `mathlib:Equiv.Perm.sign`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. P_σ is the reindexing of the tensor factors along σ, and σ↦P_σ is already a representation (tauceti:PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation).
2. sgn:S_d→{±1} is a homomorphism with values in the centre of End_K(V^{⊗d}), so σ↦sgn(σ)P_σ is again a representation.
3. For a K-linear f:V→W, use mathlib:PiTensorProduct.map_reindex to commute f^{⊗d} with P_σ, then with its sign twist. The Tau Ceti commute_reindexRepresentation_map citation covers the endomorphism case only.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction` (data): For σ∈S_d, the K-linear endomorphism sgn(σ)·P_σ of V^{⊗d}.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction.apply_tprod` (simp): σ·(v_1⊗⋯⊗v_d)=sgn(σ)·v_{σ⁻¹(1)}⊗⋯⊗v_{σ⁻¹(d)}.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction.one` (structure): The identity permutation acts as the identity.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction.mul` (structure): στ acts as the composite of the actions of σ and τ.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulRepresentation` (constructor): The representation S_d→End_K(V^{⊗d}), σ↦sgn(σ)P_σ.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction.eq_sign_smul_reindexRepresentation` (compatibility): The action is sgn(σ) times Tau Ceti's unsigned PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction.swap_tprod` (relation): For d=2 the transposition sends v⊗w to −w⊗v.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulPermAction.naturality` (functoriality): For K-linear f:V→W, f^{⊗d}∘σ_V=σ_W∘f^{⊗d}; for a Frobenius acting K-linearly on V this is Frobenius equivariance.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulRepresentation.test_degree_zero` (degenerate): For d=0 every element of V^{⊗0}≅K is invariant.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulRepresentation.test_degree_one` (degenerate): For d=1 every element of V^{⊗1}≅V is invariant.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulRepresentation.test_line_square` (computation): If 2 is invertible in K, the invariants of the action on K^{⊗2} are zero.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulRepresentation.test_pure_square` (non-example): If 2 is invertible, x⊗x is invariant under the unsigned permutation action but is invariant under the Koszul-signed action only when x⊗x=0; a definition omitting the sign gives symmetric tensors.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.koszulRepresentation.test_char_two` (non-example): Over Z/2 the sign is trivial: the invariants of (Z/2)^{⊗2} are the whole line although ∧²(Z/2)=0.

**Acceptance.** For d=2 and V=K the transposition acts on K⊗K≅K by −1, while P_σ alone acts by +1.; For d≤1 the group S_d is trivial and the action is the identity.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19, proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519; how: S_d acts on H*(X_1^√R⊗k̄,L)^{⊗d} by permuting the factors with the Koszul sign; on a space concentrated in degree one this is the present action; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/koszul-exterior; how: the parent lemma identifies the invariants of this action on H¹ with ∧^dH¹; the comparison is GC.3/alternating-invariants-exterior; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-power-cohomology; how: the Künneth identification turns the permutation of the factors of X^d into this action on H¹^{⊗d}

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519 States that the symmetric group acts on the graded tensor power of the cohomology of the root curve by permuting factors with the Koszul sign convention; this node fixes that action on the degree-one part. [TC-TensorAction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Symmetric/TensorAction/Basic.lean) — TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Symmetric/TensorAction/Basic.lean, reindexRepresentation and commute_reindexRepresentation_map Supplies the unsigned permutation representation and its commutation with tensor powers of endomorphisms. <a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-averaging-exactness"></a>

#### Rational averaging: invariants are exact and commute with linear functors

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/averaging-exactness` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Let G be a finite group and K a commutative ring in which |G| is invertible. (i) For a K-linear representation V, e_V=|G|⁻¹Σ_{g∈G}g is an idempotent with image V^G, and V↦V^G is exact: an equivariant surjection is surjective on invariants. (ii) In a K-linear additive category in which idempotents split (for example any abelian category, such as constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves on a scheme), the invariants A^G of an object with a G-action are the image of e_A, and every K-linear additive functor F satisfies F(A^G)≅F(A)^G naturally, because F(e_A)=e_{F(A)}. In particular H^i(Y,A^G)≅H^i(Y,A)^G for a sheaf A with a G-action on a scheme Y, and q_* of invariants is the invariants of q_*.

**Hypotheses.** G finite; |G| a unit in K. Over Q̄ℓ this holds for every finite G, including groups of order divisible by ℓ.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:GroupAlgebra.average`, `mathlib:Representation.averageMap`, `mathlib:Representation.isProj_averageMap`, `mathlib:Representation.invariants`, `tauceti:Representation.range_norm_eq_invariants`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsIdempotentComplete`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Idempotents.isIdempotentComplete_iff_idempotents_have_kernels`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. e is fixed by left and right multiplication by G and e²=e (mathlib:GroupAlgebra.average); its image is V^G (mathlib:Representation.isProj_averageMap; tauceti:Representation.range_norm_eq_invariants).
2. Exactness: if f:V→W is equivariant and onto and w∈W^G, choose v with f(v)=w; then e_V(v) is invariant and f(e_V v)=e_W(w)=w.
3. A preadditive category in which idempotents have kernels, for example an abelian category, is idempotent complete (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Idempotents.isIdempotentComplete_iff_idempotents_have_kernels); any additive functor preserves split idempotents and their images (Stacks §12.4), and K-linearity gives F(e_A)=e_{F(A)}.

**Acceptance.** G=S_2 swapping the coordinates of K² with 2 invertible: the invariants are the diagonal and e(x,y)=((x+y)/2,(x+y)/2).; Without invertibility exactness fails: for G=Z/2 over Z/2, the augmentation (Z/2)[G]→Z/2 is onto but sends the invariant 1+g to 0, so the trivial invariant 1 is not hit.

**Sources.** [ETINGOF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0901.0827v5) — Proof of Theorem 3.8, p. 37 (arXiv v5) In the complex-representation setting, the proof identifies the group average as the projector onto invariants. The general ring case here follows from the same finite-sum calculation with |G| invertible, using the pinned averaging API. [AV99](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9908167v2) — Proof of Lemma 2.3.3, p. 5 For a finite group of order prime to the residue characteristics the averaging operator is a projector exhibiting the invariants as a direct summand, which gives base change of invariants. [STACKS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BSE) — Section 12.4 (tag 09SF), Karoubian categories Gives the splitting characterization for idempotents. Preservation of a chosen splitting by a functor, and hence the K-linear averaging consequence here, follows by applying the functor to the splitting identities. [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — §A.2.1 and proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519 Takes S_d-invariants of a pushforward and identifies the cohomology of the invariant part with the invariants of the cohomology.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-root-curve-character-dictionary"></a>

#### Local systems on the root curve and inertia of order two

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let 𝒳=X_1^√R and let ū be a geometric point of U⊂𝒳. Restriction to U is fully faithful from Q̄ℓ-local systems on 𝒳 to Q̄ℓ-local systems on U. Its essential image consists of the local systems whose monodromy, restricted to the inertia subgroup I_x̄⊂π1(U,ū) of every geometric point x̄ of X above R (for one, equivalently every, path), has order dividing two. In rank one: rank-one local systems on 𝒳 correspond to continuous characters χ:π1(U,ū)→Q̄ℓ^× of the arithmetic fundamental group over k with χ(τ)²=1 for all τ in every I_x̄. Such χ is tamely ramified at R, since the wild inertia is pro-p with p odd. The global monodromy is unrestricted: an unramified χ of order three, or of infinite order, is allowed. At a geometric point of 𝒳 over x∈R the stabilizer μ₂ acts on the stalk through χ|I_x̄, which is trivial or the character of order two; χ|I_x̄ is trivial for every x exactly when the local system descends to X.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; Local systems are lisse Q̄ℓ-sheaves of finite rank. π1(𝒳) is the fundamental group of the Galois category of representable finite étale covers of the Deligne–Mumford curve 𝒳 (Noohi §4), and local systems on 𝒳 are continuous representations of it (gap GC3-STACK-PI1). The stacks and atlas charts used here are normal. Coefficient objects are defined over a finite extension E/Qℓ before scalar extension to Q̄ℓ; no representation dictionary is asserted for arbitrary nonnormal stacks.

**Prerequisites.** `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1/tame-and-prime-to-p`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1/decomposition-inertia`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/etale-fundamental-group`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/adic-local-systems`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/root-stack`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/affine-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-affine-chart), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/regular-dm`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-regular-dm), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre).

**Construction/proof.**

1. U is a dense open substack of the connected normal Deligne–Mumford curve 𝒳 (RS.1/regular-dm), so π1(U,ū)→π1(𝒳,ū) is surjective (IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas); restriction of continuous representations along a surjection is fully faithful.
2. Étale-locally at x∈R with local equation s, 𝒳 is [Spec A[t]/(t²−s)/μ₂] (RS.1/affine-chart, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/root-stack). A local system on U extends over this chart exactly when its pullback to the double cover t²=s extends; the tame inertia of the double cover at t=0 is the subgroup of squares of the tame inertia at x (IG.1/tame-and-prime-to-p, IG.1/decomposition-inertia), so the pullback is unramified in codimension one exactly when the inertia image has order dividing two (Abhyankar's lemma, Stacks 0EYG).
3. A finite étale cover of the punctured regular chart that is unramified in codimension one extends uniquely to a finite étale cover of the chart (Stacks 0H2W); the extension is μ₂-equivariant by uniqueness and descends along the atlas (gap GC3-STACK-PI1).
4. The stabilizer μ₂ at x is the image of the local inertia, so it acts on the stalk by χ|I_x̄. By Noohi Theorem 7.11 the quotient of π1(𝒳) by the closed normal subgroup generated by the stabilizers is π1(X), which gives the descent criterion.

**Acceptance.** R=∅: 𝒳=X and the statement is the ordinary dictionary between local systems on X and representations of π1(X).; X=P¹, R={0,∞}: over k̄, 𝒳≅[P¹/μ₂] for the squaring map, and the admissible geometric characters are the trivial one and the quadratic Kummer character of t ramified at 0 and ∞.; A character whose inertia at some x∈R has order four is excluded; one with χ(Frob)=ζ₃ and trivial geometric monodromy is admitted.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — §A.2, first paragraph, p. 519 States without proof that a rank-one local system on the root curve is the same datum as a rank-one local system on X−R with monodromy of order at most two at the points of R. [STACKS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BSE) — Lemma 58.31.5 (tag 0EYG), Lemma 58.31.2 (tag 0H2W), Example 58.31.4 (tag 0EYF) Abhyankar's lemma for a regular divisor, and the extension of finite étale covers that are unramified in codimension one over a regular scheme. [NOOHI](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0201021) — §4, pp. 8–10; Theorem 7.11, p. 17 The Galois category and fundamental group of a connected algebraic stack, and the comparison of π1 modulo the images of the stabilizers with π1 of the coarse space.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-tame-local-systems"></a>

#### Rank-one local systems on the root curve

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/tame-local-systems` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Rank-one Q̄ℓ-local systems L on X_1^√R correspond to rank-one tame local systems on U=X−R whose geometric inertia characters have order dividing two. Their global monodromy can have arbitrary order; in particular an unramified character of order three is allowed.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-smooth), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-root-curve-character-dictionary).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use local root charts to identify tame inertia with the residual μ₂ action.
2. A tame character factors through this action exactly when its local inertia square is one.
3. Glue using full faithful étale-local-system restriction and descent; the fundamental-group comparison for root stacks is the precise stack extension recorded in gap ST-LISSE.

**Acceptance.** The quadratic cover supplies a special input, not the general definition.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.2 first paragraph, p. 519; the tame order-two inertia condition.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-antisymmetrization"></a>

#### Existing antisymmetrization takes values in the Koszul invariants

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/antisymmetrization` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Use the existing antisymmetrization α_d=exteriorPower.toTensorPower and exterior projection π_d=exteriorPower.fromTensorPower, for a commutative ring K, a K-module V and d≥0. The current library already supplies their generator formulas, π_d∘α_d=d!·id, α_d∘π_d=Σ_σ sgn(σ)P_σ, and naturality. The additional compatibility target here is that every α_d(ω) is invariant for the Koszul-signed action of GC.3/koszul-sign-action. No factorial invertibility is needed for this compatibility. These maps are imports, not new constructions in GC.3; the suggested file uses private light models only because the imports postdate its mandatory pins.

**Hypotheses.** K commutative ring; V a K-module; d≥0. No invertibility is assumed for the construction; d! invertible is needed only in GC.3/alternating-invariants-exterior.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/koszul-sign-action`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-koszul-sign-action), `mathlib:ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower`, `mathlib:exteriorPower.ιMulti`, `mathlib:exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv`, `mathlib:exteriorPower.map`, `mathlib:MultilinearMap.alternatization`, `mathlib:AlternatingMap.coe_alternatization`, `mathlib:PiTensorProduct.lift`, `mathlib:PiTensorProduct.tprod`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl#layer-8-schur-weyl-duality`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Reuse exteriorPower.toTensorPower from current Mathlib and exteriorPower.fromTensorPower from Tau Ceti LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basic.lean, with the factorial and naturality API listed in currentLibraryImports. At the old pins the same maps are represented by the alternating-map universal property and PiTensorProduct.lift; these are private signature models, not proposed replacements.
2. On a pure wedge, α_d is the signed sum of the permuted pure tensors. Acting by τ in the Koszul representation and reindexing the sum by σ↦στ⁻¹ returns α_d; generation by pure wedges gives the assertion for every ω.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.antisymmetrization.mem_invariants` (characterisation): α_d(ω) is invariant under the Koszul-signed action for every ω.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.antisymmetrization.test_degree_two` (computation): α_2(v∧w)=v⊗w−w⊗v.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.antisymmetrization.test_degree_zero` (degenerate): For d=0, α_0 is the identification ∧^0V≅K≅V^{⊗0}.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.antisymmetrization.test_projection_factor` (characterisation): π_d∘α_d=d!·id; a definition with the normalizing factor 1/d! would give the identity and fail over Z.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.antisymmetrization.test_char_two` (non-example): Over Z/2 with V=Z/2 and d=2, α_2=0 because ∧²V=0, while the Koszul-signed invariants of V^{⊗2} are nonzero; α_2 is not onto the invariants without d! invertible.

**Acceptance.** For d=2: α_2(v∧w)=v⊗w−w⊗v and π_2(v⊗w−w⊗v)=2·v∧w.; For d=0 and d=1 the maps are the identifications ∧^0V≅K≅V^{⊗0} and ∧^1V≅V≅V^{⊗1}.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19, proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519; how: the Koszul-signed invariants of H¹^{⊗d} are identified with ∧^dH¹; α_d is the explicit map; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/koszul-exterior; how: Supplies the signed-action compatibility for the existing map; the maps and their generic identities are imported from the current library.; where: Conrad, Exterior powers, §4, (4.1), pp. 12–13; how: the embedding of ∧^k(V) in V^{⊗k} as skew-symmetric tensors and the factor k! on returning to ∧^k

**Sources.** [CONRAD-EXT](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/extmod.pdf) — §4, display (4.1), p. 12, and the discussion of skew-symmetric tensors, p. 13 Defines the map from ∧^k(M) to M^{⊗k} by the signed sum over permutations, shows it is injective for free M, and computes that returning to ∧^k multiplies by k!. [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519 Identifies the Koszul-signed invariants of a tensor power of a degree-one space with the exterior power; this node supplies the explicit map. [TC-CurrentExterior](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basic.lean) — LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basic.lean, fromTensorPower through range_toTensorPower (lines 170–247 at the recorded commit) Already implements the exterior projection, both factorial/norm composites, injectivity when d! is a unit, naturality and the image identity. Only compatibility with the new Koszul-signed action is planned here.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-finite-group-rational-acyclicity"></a>

#### Rational acyclicity of finite groups

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/finite-group-rational-acyclicity` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Let G be a finite group and M a G-module on which multiplication by |G| is bijective, for example a Q̄ℓ-vector space with a linear G-action. Then H^r(G,M)=0 for every r>0, and H^0(G,M)=M^G is the image of the averaging idempotent. Applied to the finite stabilizers of a tame Deligne–Mumford stack and to the kernel of μ₂^m→μ₂, this is the rational finite-groupoid cohomology vanishing used for collision fibres and for the coarse pushforward.

**Hypotheses.** G finite; |G| acts bijectively on M. No condition relating |G| to ℓ is needed for Q̄ℓ-vector spaces.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees`, `mathlib:groupCohomology`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/averaging-exactness`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-averaging-exactness).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Reuse the ordinary all-degree annihilation theorem groupCohomology.natCard_nsmul_eq_zero from current Tau Ceti (currentLibraryImports). Its transfer input is TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_subtype_id_comp_corestriction: Cor∘Res through the trivial subgroup is multiplication by |G| (Milne, CFT II.1.30–1.31). ProfiniteCohomology Layer 10 is the existing owner of transfer; the proof here uses the implemented ordinary theorem directly. Layer 3 only compares degrees 0–2, so it is not an all-degree comparison input.
2. H^r(1,M)=0 for r>0, so |G| kills H^r(G,M) (Milne, CFT II.1.31); |G| also acts bijectively on H^r(G,M) because it does on M, so H^r(G,M)=0.
3. Degree zero is GC.3/averaging-exactness.

**Acceptance.** G=μ₂ acting on Q̄ℓ by the sign: H^r=0 for all r≥0, including H^0.; G=Z/2 acting trivially on F_2: H^r(G,F_2)=F_2 for every r, so the hypothesis cannot be dropped.

**Sources.** [MILNE-CFT](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/CFT.pdf) — Chapter II, Proposition 1.30 and Corollary 1.31, p. 70 (v4.03) Corestriction after restriction is multiplication by the index; consequently the order of G kills its cohomology in positive degrees. [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.7, pp. 519–520 Computes the pushforward along [pt/μ₂]^d→[pt/μ₂] as coinvariants of the kernel of multiplication, which uses the vanishing of higher rational cohomology of that kernel. [TC-CurrentCorestriction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Corestriction.lean) — Corestriction.lean, lines 153–169 and 430–445 Implements ordinary restriction/corestriction and all-degree finite-group annihilation over a commutative coefficient ring. The invertible-order consequence is the additional target here.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-monodromy-symmetric-local-system"></a>

#### Symmetric local systems by descent and lisse extension

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Let L be a rank-one Q̄ℓ-local system on X_1^√R with character χ (GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary) and d≥0. (i) The external product L^{⊠d}=pr_1^*L⊗⋯⊗pr_d^*L on (U^d)°, with the S_d-linearization that permutes tensor factors without sign, descends along the finite étale Galois S_d-cover (U^d)°→U_d° to a rank-one local system L_d° on U_d°. Over k̄ its monodromy is YZ19 (A.6): π1((U_d°)_k̄)→π1(U_k̄)^d⋊S_d→Q̄ℓ^×, (g_1,…,g_d;σ)↦∏χ(g_i), with χ valued in Q̄ℓ^× (EGC3-4). (ii) L_d° extends to a rank-one local system 𝕃_d on the smooth connected Deligne–Mumford stack X_d^√R, and the extension with its identification on U_d° is unique up to unique isomorphism. 𝕃_0 is the constant line on Spec k, 𝕃_1=L, and 𝕃_d carries the Frobenius descent datum of the construction over k. At a geometric point D=Σn_x x the stalk is one-dimensional and the stabilizer factor μ₂ at x∈R∩supp D acts through the inertia character of L at x. Notation: U=X−R with j:U→X; X_d=Sym^dX with the finite quotient map q_d:X^d→X_d; U_d°⊂X_d is the open of multiplicity-free divisors supported in U and (U^d)°=q_d⁻¹(U_d°) the ordered distinct points of U; ω_d:X_d^√R→X_d is the coarse map (GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse), an isomorphism over Sym^dU, so U_d° is open in X_d^√R.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; No pushforward along the nonrepresentable ordered map p_d is used; the comparison with the definition (p_{d,!}L^{⊠d})^{S_d} is GC.3/pushforward-description-comparison.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-root-curve-character-dictionary), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/adic-local-systems`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/etale-fundamental-group`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-smooth), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-coarse), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space).

**Construction/proof.**

1. (U^d)°→U_d° is finite étale and Galois with group S_d, and Q̄ℓ-local systems form an étale stack (IG.0/adic-local-systems), so S_d-equivariant local systems descend (IG.0/etale-fundamental-group).
2. The complement of U_d° in X_d^√R is the union of the collision divisor Δ (two points of U meet) and the divisors D_x, x∈R, of root divisors containing x, plus a closed subset of codimension at least two.
3. Along Δ: near a generic point the S_d-cover is the quotient by one transposition of a smooth neighbourhood of the diagonal, and the transposition exchanges two equal lines L_y⊗L_y without sign, hence acts trivially; L_d° is unramified along Δ.
4. Along D_x: near a generic point, X_d^√R is étale-locally X_1^√R near x times U_{d−1}°, and L_d° is L⊠L_{d−1}°; L is a local system on X_1^√R, so L_d° extends over the generic point of D_x.
5. On an étale atlas of X_d^√R by a smooth scheme (GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth), the finite étale covers trivializing the finite-level reductions of L_d° are unramified in codimension one, so they extend (Stacks 0H2W, purity 0BMB); uniqueness of such extensions gives descent data on the atlas (gap GC3-STACK-PI1).
6. Uniqueness follows from full faithfulness on the dense open of the connected normal stack (IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas). For the stabilizer character, the boundary divisor of divisors containing a fixed geometric x is smooth and connected (GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth, YZ19 Lemma A.4, pp. 516–517). Its μ₂-action on a lisse line is locally constant, so is determined at the generic boundary point, where the product chart L⊠L_{d−1}° gives exactly χ|I_x. This remains true at n·x and at intersections of boundary divisors. This argument uses no pushforward comparison.
7. For f:L→L′, descend f^{⊠d} on the distinct-point locus and extend the map by full faithfulness. This gives map, identity and composition, with scalar a acting by a^d. The empty tensor power gives the identity when d=0, even for f=0.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem` (constructor): For L and d≥0, the rank-one local system 𝕃_d on X_d^√R with its Frobenius descent datum.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.restrictDistinct` (characterisation): 𝕃_d|U_d° is the descent of L^{⊠d}|(U^d)° along the S_d-cover with the unsigned linearization.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.uniqueExtension` (extensionality): Two rank-one local systems on X_d^√R with isomorphisms to L_d° on U_d° are related by a unique isomorphism compatible with them.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.zero` (simp): 𝕃_0 is the constant line on Spec k.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.one` (simp): 𝕃_1=L.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.monodromy` (characterisation): Over k̄ the monodromy on U_d° is the character (A.6) with χ valued in Q̄ℓ^×.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.stalk` (other): At D=Σn_x x the stalk is one-dimensional and the stabilizer factor at x∈R∩supp D acts by the inertia character of L at x.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.multiplicative` (compatibility): add_{d,e}^*𝕃_{d+e}≅𝕃_d⊠𝕃_e, associative, commutative and unital. See [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-multiplicativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-multiplicativity).
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.map` (functoriality): For a morphism f:L→L′, the map on degree d is induced by f^{⊠d}; on distinct points it is the descended tensor power, on stalks the corresponding tensor power.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.map_id` (simp): The map induced by the identity of L is the identity in every degree.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.map_comp` (functoriality): The map induced by g∘f is map(g)∘map(f); these identifications commute with restriction, stalks and Frobenius.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_zero` (degenerate): 𝕃_0 is Q̄ℓ on X_0^√R=Spec k.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_one` (compatibility): 𝕃_1 is L, with the identity on U.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_constant` (computation): For R=∅ and L=Q̄ℓ, 𝕃_d=Q̄ℓ on X_d.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_order_three` (computation): For χ unramified, geometrically trivial, with χ(Frob)=ζ₃, 𝕃_d is geometrically constant with geometric Frobenius acting by ζ₃^d.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_koszul_sign_obstructs` (non-example): Descending L^{⊠2} with the sign-twisted linearization gives a system on U_2° with monodromy −1 around the collision divisor; it has no lisse extension to X_2^√R.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_stabilizer_character` (characterisation): At 2x for x∈R with sign inertia, the stabilizer μ₂ acts on the stalk by the sign, not by its square.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.monodromySymmetricLocalSystem.test_scalar_map` (computation): For L constant and f=2·id, map(f) is 2^d·id. For the zero endomorphism it is zero for d≥1 and identity for d=0; this distinguishes tensor-power functoriality from an additive rule.

**Acceptance.** 𝕃_0=Q̄ℓ on X_0^√R=Spec k and 𝕃_1=L.; R=∅ and L constant give 𝕃_d constant on X_d.; With the Koszul-signed linearization the descended system has monodromy −1 around Δ and does not extend: the unsigned linearization is forced.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19, proof of Lemma A.8, p. 520; how: multiplicativity is proved by comparing the monodromy characters (A.5) and (A.6) on the distinct-point locus, which is the defining property of this construction; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/fibre-triviality and GC.4/high-degree-descent; how: descent along the Abel–Jacobi map needs L_d as a lisse sheaf on X_d^√R; this construction supplies it without stack pushforward; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/divisor-tensor-line; how: the fibre of L_d at a root divisor O(D)^♮ with D supported on U is the fibre of L_d° at D, the tensor product of the fibres of L; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-multiplicativity; how: both sides of add^*L_{d+e}≅L_d⊠L_e are compared on the distinct-point open, where they are given by this descent; where: Morphisms of the input rank-one local system and the cohomology comparison; how: Naturality on distinct-point restrictions and stalks extends by full faithfulness for the lisse construction, and by q_* and the averaging projector for the coarse construction; identity/composition are inherited from external tensor powers.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — §A.2.1 and proof of Lemma A.8, (A.5)–(A.6), pp. 519–520 Defines L_d by symmetric pushforward and proves multiplicativity by identifying its monodromy on the multiplicity-free locus with the character (A.6); here that monodromy is taken as the definition and extended. [STACKS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BSE) — Lemma 58.31.2 (tag 0H2W) and Lemma 58.21.4 (tag 0BMB) Finite étale covers unramified in codimension one extend over a regular scheme; purity of the branch locus.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-local-system"></a>

#### Symmetric tensor local systems

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-local-system` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For L as above and d≥0 define K_d=(p_{d,!}L^{⊠d})^{S_d} with no shift, and L_d=H⁰(K_d). The collision and middle-extension lemmas prove K_d≅L_d, with L_d lisse rank one and L_d[d] perverse. The invariant projector is d!⁻¹Σσ over Q̄ℓ, including when ℓ divides d!.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/tame-local-systems`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-tame-local-systems), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-divisors`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-divisors), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-proper`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-proper).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Take the external tensor product with its genuine symmetry maps.
2. Apply the source-qualified tame stack proper pushforward, then the rational invariant projector.
3. Use the collision kernel and middle-extension lemmas below to prove this is lisse and concentrated in degree zero; the construction itself is the unshifted invariant complex.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.zero` (simp): L_0 is the coefficient line on Spec k.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.one` (simp): L_1=L under p_1=id.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.invariantProjector` (characterisation): L_d is the image of d!⁻¹Σσ on the unshifted p_{d,!}L^{⊠d}.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.perverseShift` (compatibility): L_d[d] is the perverse intermediate extension from the distinct-point open. See [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/middle-extension`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-middle-extension).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.test_zero` (degenerate): The zeroth symmetric local system is the coefficient line in degree zero.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.test_one` (compatibility): The first symmetric local system is L in degree zero.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.test_shift` (non-example): At d=1 the complex L[1] is perverse, while L is the unshifted lisse sheaf.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem.test_order_three` (non-example): An unramified order-three character still gives this construction.

**Acceptance.** L_0=Q̄ℓ and L_1=L; the shift does not belong in the degree-zero local-system definition.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 Lemmas A.6–A.11; how: Supplies the cohomology, translation and character-sheaf maps.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.2.1 p. 519, corrected perverse shift (packet source issue E1; upstream PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19/E26).

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricLocalSystem`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-alternating-invariants-exterior"></a>

#### Koszul-signed invariants are the exterior power

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/alternating-invariants-exterior` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let K be a commutative ring in which d! is invertible and V a K-module. The antisymmetrization α_d is an isomorphism from ∧^dV onto the invariants (V^{⊗d})^{S_d} of the Koszul-signed action, with inverse (d!)⁻¹·π_d restricted to the invariants. The isomorphism is natural in V, hence commutes with any K-linear Frobenius. Consequences: for d=0 both sides are K; for d=1 both are V; if V is free of rank n the invariants are free of rank C(n,d), in particular zero for d>n. Over K=Q̄ℓ, a field of characteristic zero, d! is invertible for every d, including when the prime ℓ divides d!.

**Hypotheses.** K commutative ring with d! a unit; V any K-module (no finiteness needed for the isomorphism).; The rank statement assumes V free of finite rank n and K nontrivial.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/antisymmetrization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-antisymmetrization), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/koszul-sign-action`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-koszul-sign-action), `mathlib:exteriorPower.finrank_eq`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl#layer-8-schur-weyl-duality`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. α_d lands in the invariants and π_d∘α_d=d!·id (GC.3/antisymmetrization), so α_d is injective when d! is a unit.
2. Reuse the current-library identity α_d∘π_d=Σ_σ sgn(σ)P_σ (currentLibraryImports). For an invariant tensor t this is Σ_σ σ_Koszul(t)=d!·t, giving the inverse (d!)⁻¹π_d. The companion identity π_d∘α_d=d!·id proves injectivity.
3. Naturality is that of α_d and π_d; the rank follows from mathlib:exteriorPower.finrank_eq, C(n,d)=0 for d>n.

**Acceptance.** d=2, V of rank 2: the invariants are spanned by e_1⊗e_2−e_2⊗e_1, of rank 1=C(2,2).; dim V=1, d=2: the invariants are zero, while the unsigned (symmetric) invariants would be the whole line.; Over Z/2, d=2, V=Z/2: the statement fails (invariants the whole line, ∧²=0), so the hypothesis on d! cannot be dropped.

**Sources.** [CONRAD-EXT](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/extmod.pdf) — §4, p. 13 The cited discussion treats finite-dimensional vector spaces and the factorial normalization. The all-module statement here follows by the two composite identities, already implemented in the current library, and the explicit invariant argument in proofSteps; it is not attributed verbatim to Conrad. [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519 Uses that the Koszul-signed S_d-invariants of the d-th tensor power of a space in degree one are its d-th exterior power, in degree d.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-tensor-character-kernel"></a>

#### The tensor character factors through multiplication

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/tensor-character-kernel` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Let A be a commutative group, χ:A→Q̄ℓ^× a character and m≥1. The character (a_i)↦∏χ(a_i) of A^m is χ∘μ_m, where μ_m is multiplication, so it is trivial on N_m=ker μ_m and invariant under permutations. This algebraic assertion needs no finiteness. If A is finite, the derived N_m-invariants of this line are concentrated in degree zero and the quotient A^m/N_m≅A acts by χ. In GC.3 use A=μ₂(k̄). The translation into pushforward along B(A^m)→B(A), and the geometric stalk at n·x, is made only in GC.3/pushforward-description-comparison, using GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD; it is not a consequence of character algebra alone.

**Hypotheses.** A is a commutative group and χ a homomorphism; m≥1.; The cohomological corollary assumes A finite and Q̄ℓ coefficients. Without finiteness, rational higher group cohomology need not vanish.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:map_prod`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/finite-group-rational-acyclicity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-finite-group-rational-acyclicity).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Because χ is a homomorphism and A is commutative, ∏χ(a_i)=χ(∏a_i) (mathlib:map_prod).
2. For finite A, N_m is finite and acts trivially on the line. Its invariants are that line and its higher rational cohomology vanishes by GC.3/finite-group-rational-acyclicity; the surjection μ_m (m≥1) identifies the quotient action with χ.
3. A permutation of the factors fixes ∏χ(a_i), and on L_x^{⊗n} it acts by the identity because the line is in degree zero.

**Acceptance.** A=μ₂, χ the sign, m=2: (−1,−1)∈N_2 and χ(−1)χ(−1)=1.; If the two factors carried different characters (sign and trivial), the element (−1,−1)∈N_2 would act by −1: the kernel acts trivially only because every factor carries the same character.; At 2x with sign inertia the stabilizer acts on the stalk by the sign; the square of the sign would be trivial.; Finiteness is essential for the cohomological corollary: for the infinite discrete group A=ℤ, trivial χ and m=2, N_m≅ℤ has H¹(N_m,Q̄ℓ)=Hom(ℤ,Q̄ℓ)≠0.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.7, pp. 519–520 At dx the ordered map restricts to [pt/μ₂]^d→[pt/μ₂] through multiplication; the restriction of L is the trivial or sign character, the kernel acts trivially on its d-th tensor power, so the stalk is one-dimensional.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-coarse-model"></a>

#### The coarse symmetric-power sheaf

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-coarse-model` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For L with character χ as above, let F=j_*(L|U), a constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaf on X with stalk F_x=L_x̄ at x∈U, F_x=L_x̄ at x∈R where the inertia character is trivial, and F_x=0 at x∈R where it is the sign. Define 𝓜_d=(q_{d*}F^{⊠d})^{S_d} on X_d=Sym^dX: the S_d-invariants, for the unsigned permutation of the tensor factors and of the coordinates of X^d, of the pushforward along the finite map q_d of F^{⊠d}=pr_1^*F⊗⋯⊗pr_d^*F. It is a constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaf with Frobenius descent datum, 𝓜_d|U_d°=L_d°, and at a geometric point D=Σn_x x its stalk is ⊗_x F_x^{⊗n_x}: one-dimensional when the inertia character at every point of R∩supp D is trivial, zero otherwise. Notation: U=X−R with j:U→X; X_d=Sym^dX with the finite quotient map q_d:X^d→X_d; U_d°⊂X_d is the open of multiplicity-free divisors supported in U and (U^d)°=q_d⁻¹(U_d°) the ordered distinct points of U; ω_d:X_d^√R→X_d is the coarse map (GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse), an isomorphism over Sym^dU, so U_d° is open in X_d^√R.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; Constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves on schemes of finite type over k and k̄, with finite pushforward and proper base change, are the scheme theory requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (upstream EtaleCohomologyFoundations).

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-root-curve-character-dictionary), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/averaging-exactness`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-averaging-exactness), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-monodromy-symmetric-local-system), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1/decomposition-inertia`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. q_d is finite and S_d-invariant, and F^{⊠d} is S_d-equivariant by permuting factors; take the image of the averaging idempotent in the abelian category of constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves on X_d (GC.3/averaging-exactness).
2. Stalks: proper base change for the finite q_d identifies (q_{d*}F^{⊠d})_D with the sum over the reduced ordered preimages of D (étale cohomology ignores the nilpotent structure of the finite fibre); S_d permutes them transitively with stabilizer ∏_x S_{n_x}, and a permutation acts trivially on a tensor power of a line, so the invariants are ⊗_xF_x^{⊗n_x}.
3. F_x for x∈R is the inertia invariants of L_x̄, which is the whole line or zero (IG.1/decomposition-inertia; GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary).
4. Over U_d° the map q_d is the S_d-torsor and F=L, so 𝓜_d|U_d° is the descent L_d°.
5. For the subsheaf assertion, use local finite quadratic root charts f:Y→X: the pullback of L is lisse on the regular chart Y, and F=j_*L is the μ₂-invariant summand of f_*L_Y. On products of these charts, the same finite-pushforward and commuting-projector description applies to F^{⊠d}. Restriction of a lisse sheaf on a normal chart to the dense distinct-point open is injective; finite pushforward and invariant summands preserve this injection. Hence F^{⊠d} and then 𝓜_d inject into the direct images of their distinct-point restrictions. Maps f^{⊠d}, followed by q_* and the invariant projector, give functoriality and its identity/composition laws.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel` (constructor): 𝓜_d=(q_{d*}(j_*L)^{⊠d})^{S_d} on Sym^dX with its Frobenius descent datum.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.stalk` (characterisation): (𝓜_d)_D≅⊗_x F_x^{⊗n_x} for D=Σn_x x.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.restrictDistinct` (compatibility): 𝓜_d|U_d°≅L_d°, compatibly with Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.zero` (simp): 𝓜_0=Q̄ℓ.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.one` (simp): 𝓜_1=j_*L.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.subsheaf` (other): The restriction map 𝓜_d→j′_*(L_d°), for j′:U_d°→X_d, is injective: 𝓜_d has no nonzero sections supported off U_d°.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.map` (functoriality): For a morphism f:L→L′, the map on degree d is induced by f^{⊠d}; on distinct points it is the descended tensor power, on stalks the corresponding tensor power.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.map_id` (simp): The map induced by the identity of L is the identity in every degree.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.map_comp` (functoriality): The map induced by g∘f is map(g)∘map(f); these identifications commute with restriction, stalks and Frobenius.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.test_zero` (degenerate): 𝓜_0 is Q̄ℓ on Spec k.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.test_one` (compatibility): 𝓜_1 is j_*L on X.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.test_kummer_stalks` (computation): For X=P¹, R={0,∞} and the quadratic Kummer character, (𝓜_2)_{2·0}=(𝓜_2)_{0+∞}=0 and (𝓜_2)_{y+y′} is a line for y,y′∈U.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.test_not_lisse` (non-example): If the inertia at some x∈R is the sign, 𝓜_d (d≥1) vanishes on the image of D_x but not on U_d°, so it is not lisse, while 𝕃_d on the stack is; the coarse model carries cohomology, not descent.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.symmetricCoarseModel.test_scalar_map` (computation): For L constant and f=2·id, map(f) is 2^d·id. For the zero endomorphism it is zero for d≥1 and identity for d=0; this distinguishes tensor-power functoriality from an additive rule.

**Acceptance.** 𝓜_0=Q̄ℓ on X_0=Spec k and 𝓜_1=j_*L.; If χ is unramified at every x∈R, F is the lisse extension of L to X and 𝓜_d is Deligne's lisse symmetric-power system on X_d.; X=P¹, R={0,∞}, χ the quadratic Kummer character: the stalks of 𝓜_2 at 2·0, at 0+∞ and at 0+y with y∈U vanish, and the stalk at y+y′ with y,y′∈U is a line.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19, proof of Lemma A.6, p. 519; how: the cohomology of L_d is computed as S_d-invariants of a tensor power of cohomology; on the coarse space this is the cohomology of 𝓜_d; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/rational-coarse-comparison; how: the coarse pushforward of the stack local system 𝕃_d is 𝓜_d; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-power-cohomology; how: its cohomology is the Koszul-signed invariants of the tensor power of H*(X⊗k̄,j_*L); where: Morphisms of the input rank-one local system and the cohomology comparison; how: Naturality on distinct-point restrictions and stalks extends by full faithfulness for the lisse construction, and by q_* and the averaging projector for the coarse construction; identity/composition are inherited from external tensor powers.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — §A.1.3 and §A.2.1, pp. 515–519 X_d is the coarse space of X_d^√R and L_d is formed by taking S_d-invariants of a symmetric pushforward; this node is the same construction on the coarse space. [AV99](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9908167v2) — Lemma 2.2.3, p. 4 Étale-locally on its coarse space a separated Deligne–Mumford stack is a quotient of a scheme by a finite group.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-collision-kernel"></a>

#### Collision kernels act trivially on the tensor line

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/collision-kernel` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

At a geometric divisor Σm_x x, the relative inertia of the ordered map over a branch point x is ker(μ₂^{m_x}→μ₂). It acts trivially on L_x^{⊗m_x}, since the same rank-one character occurs in every factor.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-power-cohomology` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; X^d is proper over k; Künneth for constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves and finite pushforward are the scheme inputs requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.

2. Invariants commute with cohomology (GC.3/averaging-exactness): H*(X_d,𝓜_d)=H*(X^d,F^{⊠d})^{S_d}.
3. Künneth for the proper X^d gives H*(X^d_k̄,F^{⊠d})≅H*(X_k̄,F)^{⊗d}, Frobenius-equivariantly; under it the permutation of the coordinates of X^d and of the factors of F^{⊠d} becomes the Koszul-signed permutation, because the external cup product is graded commutative (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2; upstream EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.2.6–F.2.7, F.4.5).

**Acceptance.** d=0: both sides are Q̄ℓ in degree zero; d=1: the identity.; R=∅, L=Q̄ℓ, X=P¹: Sym^dP¹=P^d, and the right side is spanned by the products of the degree-two class, matching H*(P^d).; If H*(X⊗k̄,j_*L) is concentrated in degree one, the right side is concentrated in degree d.

[UP-ECF](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/651c49797943811c7dd6d8ab4b5771b7ede1ec0d/TauCetiRoadmap/EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) — §F.2.6 Ordinary finite-coefficient étale Künneth; §F.2.7 Compact-support projection and Künneth; §F.4.5 Rational realization The scheme Künneth isomorphisms and the passage to rational adic coefficients that this theorem applies on X^d.

#### Comparison with the symmetric pushforward description

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/pushforward-description-comparison` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

The local system 𝕃_d of GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system is canonically isomorphic, compatibly with Frobenius, to the S_d-invariant part (p_{d,!}L^{⊠d})^{S_d} of the proper pushforward along the ordered map p_d:(X_1^√R)^d→X_d^√R (GC.1/ordered-divisors), which is the parent definition GC.3/symmetric-local-system; in particular the latter is concentrated in degree zero and is a rank-one local system.

Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; p_d is proper and quasi-finite but not representable at collisions of branch points: on stabilizers it is multiplication μ₂^m→μ₂ (GC.1/ordered-proper; EGC3-2). Proper base change for such morphisms of tame Deligne–Mumford stacks with Q̄ℓ coefficients is gap GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-monodromy-symmetric-local-system), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/tensor-character-kernel`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-tensor-character-kernel), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/finite-group-rational-acyclicity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-finite-group-rational-acyclicity), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-divisors`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-divisors), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/ordered-proper`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-ordered-proper), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-local-system), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.1/closed-fibre`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-rs-1-closed-fibre).

**Construction/proof.**

1. p_d^*𝕃_d and L^{⊠d} are rank-one local systems on the connected normal stack (X_1^√R)^d that agree on the dense open (U^d)°, S_d-equivariantly, so they are isomorphic (IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas); adjunction gives an S_d-invariant map 𝕃_d→p_{d*}L^{⊠d}=p_{d,!}L^{⊠d}.
2. At D=Σn_xx, proper base change and nilpotent invariance (GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD) reduce the geometric fibre to a finite groupoid. The unreduced fibre is not asserted to equal these gerbes (RS.1/closed-fibre; EGC3-5). The tensor character is trivial on this finite kernel, so higher cohomology vanishes; S_d acts transitively on the orderings, with unsigned tensor permutation acting trivially on their lines. If L is geometrically nontrivial, that is, χ is nontrivial on π1(U⊗k̄), then H⁰(X⊗k̄,j_*L)=0 and H²(X⊗k̄,j_*L)=0, so H*(X⊗k̄,j_*L) is concentrated in degree one, Frobenius-equivariantly. By GC.3/rational-coarse-comparison for d=1 the same holds for H*(X_1^√R⊗k̄,L).

The cited duality statement is used over a finite coefficient field E/Qℓ and extended flatly to Q̄ℓ; no integral or torsion duality is used.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/exterior-cohomology` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For geometrically nontrivial L, H^i(X_d^√R_kbar,L_d)=0 for i≠d, and H^d≅∧^dH¹(X_1^√R_kbar,L), naturally and Frobenius-equivariantly. This includes d=0; exterior powers vanish for d above dim H¹.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/collision-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-collision-descent), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/cohomology-vanishing`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-cohomology-vanishing), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/koszul-exterior`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-koszul-exterior), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/rational-coarse-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-rational-coarse-comparison), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-power-cohomology`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-power-cohomology), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/twisted-curve-cohomology`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-twisted-curve-cohomology), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/alternating-invariants-exterior`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-alternating-invariants-exterior).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use GC.3/rational-coarse-comparison and symmetric-power-cohomology to reduce to rational symmetric invariants on the coarse symmetric power.
2. GC.3/twisted-curve-cohomology concentrates the curve complex in degree one. Apply alternating-invariants-exterior to its Koszul action. All comparisons commute with Frobenius; include the empty tensor power and the exterior vanishing range.

**Acceptance.** At d=0 the result is H⁰=Q̄ℓ; it does not contradict input H⁰ vanishing.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.6 p. 519

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-associativity"></a>

#### Associativity of symmetric multiplicativity

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-associativity` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For d,e,f≥0 the two composites of α_{d,e}, α_{d+e,f} and α_{e,f}, α_{d,e+f} agree after the specified tensor/addition associators.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-multiplicativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-multiplicativity), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/multiplicity-free-product`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-multiplicity-free-product).

**Construction/proof.**

1. On the distinct-point ordered cover both composites are the same reassociation of three tensor blocks.
2. Use full faithfulness of dense-open restriction on the normal product to extend that equality.

**Acceptance.** This equality is needed for auxiliary-divisor comparisons, not an unspecified coherence field.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.8 and concluding exercise, p. 520; Proposition A.11(3) and its proof, p. 523.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-symmetry"></a>

#### Symmetry and degree-zero unit

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-symmetry` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

The α_{d,e} isomorphisms commute with exchanging d,e and with the ordinary symmetry of rank-one sheaves; α_{0,d} and α_{d,0} are the canonical unit isomorphisms.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-multiplicativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-multiplicativity), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/multiplicity-free-product`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-multiplicity-free-product).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Check permutation of two tensor blocks on the ordered distinct-point locus.
2. At degree zero the empty tensor is the coefficient line and concatenation is identity.
3. Extend the equality using the same restriction full faithfulness.

**Acceptance.** There is no Koszul sign on these degree-zero local systems; the sign belongs to degree-one cohomology.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.8 and concluding exercise, p. 520; Proposition A.11(3), p. 523.
