<a id="gc-4"></a>

## GC.4 — High-degree Abel–Jacobi descent

The family evaluation sequence supplies the actual Abel–Jacobi two-fibre and its quadratic chart transitions. Its scalar quotient is proper and geometrically simply connected. Proper degree-zero base change yields a chart line; full faithfulness and smooth descent glue it with its normalization. The proof separates the true two-fibre from the scalar quotient, whose Picard object twists under descent. Empty R uses the ordinary projective quotient.

**Planets.** Weighted quotient simple connectivity — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-simply-connected`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-simply-connected); High-degree Abel–Jacobi descent — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/high-degree-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-high-degree-descent); Abel–Jacobi fibre charts — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/family-fibre-presentation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-family-fibre-presentation); Weighted projective quotient — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/relative-projective-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-relative-projective-quotient); Abel–Jacobi descent line — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/chart-descent-line`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-chart-descent-line); High-degree Abel–Jacobi descent — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/high-degree-effective-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-high-degree-effective-descent).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### How the family proof fits together

For a locally Noetherian test scheme \(T\) and an actual object
\(b=(L,K_R,\iota):T\to P_d\), write \(\pi:X_T\to T\) and
\(\pi_R:R_T\to T\). The imported coherent theorem gives

\[
 E=\pi_*L,\quad U=\pi_*L(-R),\quad
 G=(\pi_R)_*(L|_{R_T}),\quad H=(\pi_R)_*K_R,
 \qquad 0\longrightarrow U\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow G
 \longrightarrow0.
\]

Their ranks are \(n,a,\rho,\rho\), respectively. For the first two
bundles, the needed inequality is \(d-\rho>2g-2\).
[Stacks, Lemma 53.22.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E3A)
checks the vanishing bound; [Lemma 30.22.1 and Remark 30.22.2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07VJ)
supply the universal coherent base-change input. These statements concern
proper schemes with coherent base-flat coefficients, with a Noetherian
original base and arbitrary base changes. Applying them here gives a
degree-zero locally free pushforward because the fibrewise higher
cohomology vanishes. Finite étaleness of \(R_T\) gives the other two bundles.

The unsplit, canonical construction is

\[
 \widehat C_b=V(E)\times_{V(G)} V(H),\qquad
 q(\alpha)=\iota(\alpha^2),\qquad
 C_b=\widehat C_b\times_{V(E)}(V(E)\setminus0).
\]

It represents the actual two-pullback \(T\times_{P_d}S_d\), with no
compatible automorphisms left over the identity of \(b\). Split \(R_T\)
étale locally, choose frames and split evaluation by \(\sigma:G\to E\).
The chart is

\[
 (u,\alpha)\longmapsto(u+\sigma(q(\alpha)),\alpha),
 \qquad \widehat C_b\simeq\mathbf A_T^{a+\rho}.
\]

Only its section coordinate is \((u,\alpha^2)\); the chart retains
\(\alpha\). The excluded closed locus has ideal
\((u_i,\alpha_j^2)\). It has the same underlying support as the zero
section \((u_i,\alpha_j)\), so **the open complements agree**. The two
closed subschemes need not agree. Over \(\mathbf F_3[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\),
\((0,\epsilon)\) is a nonzero tuple with zero section coordinate and is
excluded, whereas \((1,\epsilon)\) is effective and retains its nilpotent
root coordinate. A replacement by nonzero ring-valued tuples, or by a
reduced chart, fails one of these checks.

Changing the splitting to \(\sigma+t\) changes the kernel coordinate to
\(u-t(q(\alpha))\). This transition is quadratic, not a linear change of
frame. It respects the weight-two kernel/weight-one root action, and its
identity and composition laws come from differences of splittings. Thus
the punctured affine chart is used with its actual transition maps, not as
a claim of a globally split vector bundle.

For \(R\ne\varnothing\), the central scalar action on \(C_b\) is
\((s,\alpha)\mapsto(c^2s,c\alpha)\). The automorphism
\((c^2\operatorname{id}_L,c\operatorname{id}_{K_R})\) of \(b\) gives
coherent isomorphisms of its images in \(S_d\). Consequently there is a
map \(h_b:Q_b=[C_b/\mathbf G_m]\to S_d\). For empty \(R\), use the
ordinary weight-one scalar action and \(Q_b=\mathbf P(E)\), with the
convention that \(\mathbf P(E)\) parametrizes lines in \(E\).

One must distinguish the two maps out of \(Q_b\). Its projection
\(q_b:Q_b\to T\) is a proper smooth tame DM morphism. Its map to \(S_d\)
does **not** make its composite to \(P_d\) the constant object \(b\):
scalar descent twists \(L\) by the square of the scalar line and \(K_R\)
by that line. These composites become identified on \(C_b\), but that
identification does not descend to an identification on \(Q_b\). The
square with \(P_d\) used for checking descent is the square for \(C_b\),
not the square for \(Q_b\).

On a split chart with \(\rho>0\), the square-coordinate map gives

\[
 \mathbf P_T^{n-1}\longrightarrow W_T(2^a,1^\rho),
 \quad [x,y]\longmapsto[x_1^2,\ldots,x_a^2,y].
\]

It is representable finite locally free of rank \(2^a\): before taking
quotients its coordinate algebra is free on squarefree monomials in the
\(x_i\), and both sides use the same scalar group. It is not an étale
torsor under its generic sign group. This finite flat projective cover
also proves properness of the quotient: the relation is finite over the
projective cover, its map to the separated product is proper, and proper
diagonal and universal closedness descend. Smoothness follows from the
punctured affine atlas. Stabilizers are trivial if a root coordinate is
nonzero and \(\mu_2\) if all root coordinates vanish. Odd characteristic
makes this a tame DM stack.

For geometric simple connectivity, pull a connected representable finite
étale cover back to \(\mathbf P^{n-1}\).
[SGA 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0206203v2), Exposé XI, Proposition 1.1,
recomposed p. 219 (original margin p. 285), makes that pullback trivial.
A component produces an intermediate extension of the generic
\(\mu_2^a\)-extension. A proper subgroup is killed by some nontrivial
character, indexed by a nonempty set \(I\). On a chart \(y_\rho\ne0\)
the resulting quadratic extension has
\(z^2=\prod_{i\in I}u_i\); its valuation along any included coordinate
divisor is odd, so it ramifies there. It cannot be part of an étale
cover. Thus the subgroup is the whole sign group and the cover is
trivial. This is the parent weighted-ramification argument; the ordinary
empty-\(R\) case uses projective space directly.

No simple-connectivity assertion is made for \(C_b\) itself. In
characteristic \(p\), an equation \(z^p-z=u_1\) gives a connected finite
étale Artin–Schreier cover of punctured affine space: its derivative is
\(-1\), and the pole of order one in \(u_1\) prevents splitting over the
function field. The relevant sheaf is pulled from the scalar quotient;
it is not an arbitrary lisse sheaf on a punctured affine fibre.

Now let \(F\) be any rank-one lisse sheaf on \(S_d\). Pull it to
\(F_Q=h_b^*F\) and put \(M_b=(q_b)_*F_Q\), first at finite coefficients.
[ACV01](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0106211v1), Appendix A, Theorem A.0.8,
preprint pp. 34–35, gives degree-zero proper base change on this proper
tame DM map. The stalk of \(M_b\) is therefore \(H^0\) of the geometric
fibre. That fibre is simply connected, so evaluation is an isomorphism

\[
 q_b^*M_b\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Q.
\]

This also proves lissity: smooth local scheme atlases of \(Q_b\) give
sections of \(q_b\) étale locally on \(T\); pull the displayed isomorphism
through these sections. Constant stalk dimension alone is not used as
a lissity criterion. The coefficient adapter constructs compatible
reductions of local integral lattices and then passes to lisse
\(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\)-sheaves. It does not assume every lisse
object comes with one chosen global lattice. This generic adapter is
one of the explicit supplier leaves.

Pulling the evaluation map to the actual \(C_b\) compares \(f_b^*M_b\)
with \(F|_{C_b}\). Here \(f_b:C_b\to T\) is smooth surjective with
geometrically connected fibres. If a connected finite étale cover of
\(T\) is pulled back along \(f_b\), the resulting open surjection to that
cover has connected fibres and hence connected total space. The
finite-cover/fibre-functor equivalence gives a surjection on fundamental
groups and therefore full faithfulness of \(f_b^*\). The scheme sheaf
comparison is [Stacks, Lemma 59.65.1 and Remark 59.65.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DV4);
the stack and adic forms are exposed in the adapter.

Take a smooth locally finite type scheme atlas \(T\to P_d\). Its double
and triple overlaps can be algebraic spaces. Choose étale scheme covers
of these overlaps before applying the scheme finite-cover argument above.
The two restrictions of \(M_b\) pull back to the same sheaf on each
**actual** Abel–Jacobi checking chart. Full faithfulness gives the unique
comparison compatible with \(F\); uniqueness descends it from the scheme
refinements. On the triple overlap its cocycle holds after that faithful
pullback and hence on the overlap. Effective smooth descent for lisse
sheaves on the Artin Picard stack glues the line and comparison. The same
argument descends morphisms and all coherence diagrams. This proves the end statement without a general
nonproper-fibration homotopy or effective-descent theorem for \(AJ_d\).

#### Worked acceptance cases

1. **Small ramified fibre.** For \(g=1,\rho=1,d=2\), one has
   \(n=2,a=1\), the actual fibre is \(\mathbf A^2\setminus0\), and its
   proper quotient is \(W(2,1)\). On the root-coordinate-nonzero chart,
   \([x:y]\mapsto[x^2:y]\) becomes \(x/y\mapsto(x/y)^2\), a finite
   flat double cover ramified at zero. At the point with zero root
   coordinate the quotient retains its \(\mu_2\) stabilizer.
2. **Small unramified fibre.** For \(g=1,R=\varnothing,d=1\), the actual
   fibre is \(\mathbf G_m\), while its ordinary scalar quotient is
   \(\mathbf P^0\). It is this quotient, with ordinary weight one, that
   supplies the proper descent chart. The Picard stack still retains
   its scalar automorphisms.
3. **The bound and residue degrees.** For a degree-two closed point in
   \(R\), evaluation has a rank-two restriction bundle after base
   change, even though the support has only one closed point. At
   \(d=2g-2+\rho\), choosing \(L=\omega_X(R)\) gives
   \(H^1(L(-R))=H^1(\omega_X)\ne0\). For a genus-one curve with a
   rational \(R\), this is \(d=1\), and evaluation fails to be
   surjective. Conversely \(g=0,\rho=2,d=3\) satisfies the source bound;
   no claim that it is the optimal bound is imposed.
4. **Arithmetic normalization.** A constant geometric line with
   geometric-Frobenius eigenvalue a primitive cube root of unity
   descends with that eigenvalue. Geometric constancy does not turn
   arbitrary global monodromy into signs. If \(\theta\) is rescaled,
   the unique comparison of normalized descent pairs compensates
   by the matching scalar. Bare sheaf automorphisms are not erased.

### Target catalogue

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-evaluation-surjective"></a>

#### High-degree section evaluation is surjective

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/evaluation-surjective` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

If d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1), then for a degree-d line bundle L, H¹(X,L(−R))=0. In families, π_*L and π_*L(−R) are vector bundles of ranks d−g+1 and d−ρ−g+1, commute with base change, and π_*L→π_*(L|_R) is surjective.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use Serre duality and the negative degree of ω_X⊗L⁻¹(R) to obtain H¹ vanishing.
2. Use the coherent base-change theorem for the smooth proper family to obtain locally free pushforwards and the evaluation exact sequence.
3. Apply cohomological Riemann–Roch for the ranks; none of these scheme-family facts follows just from the built function-field theorem.

**Acceptance.** The bound counts deg R, including residue-field degrees.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.9 and proof pp. 520–521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-empty-ramification-descent"></a>

#### High-degree descent with empty ramification

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/empty-ramification-descent` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

When R=∅ and d≥max(2g−1,1), the symmetric local system descends along the ordinary Abel–Jacobi map to the degree-d Picard stack. The ordinary scalar action has weight one; the projective fibre quotient is P^{d−g}.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-monodromy-symmetric-local-system), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/symmetric-multiplicativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-symmetric-multiplicativity), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the ordinary coherent Riemann–Roch/base-change fibre description.
2. The weight-one scalar quotient is projective space and has trivial geometric fundamental group.
3. Apply the source-qualified effective lisse-sheaf descent theorem, with connected fibres.

**Acceptance.** This coalesces the unramified YZ17/49 route; no second unramified character-sheaf theory is planned.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.9 p. 520, opening unramified case; proof p. 521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-quadratic-section-coordinates"></a>

#### Split quadratic section coordinates

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/quadratic-section-coordinates` · definition · implementation unchecked.

For a commutative ring A and index types I,J, quadraticSection sends (u,alpha) in A^I x A^J to (u,(alpha_j^2)_j). In a split family chart I indexes the evaluation kernel and J the root coordinates. This is the section coordinate in E only: the full fibre-product chart sends (u,alpha) to ((u,alpha^2),alpha), retaining alpha. This polynomial function is neither asserted linear nor invertible.

**Hypotheses.** A is any commutative ring, including a nonreduced ring; I and J are arbitrary index types. Finite I,J are used for affine schemes.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:mul_pow`, `mathlib:map_pow`, `mathlib:sq_eq_zero_iff`, `mathlib:DualNumber`, `mathlib:DualNumber.eps_pow_two`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the existing native product and function carriers and ordinary ring powers; the definition has its displayed real body.
2. The YZ19 split fibre description identifies the section coordinate with this function. Scalar equivariance follows from mul_pow; change of coefficient ring follows from map_pow.
3. For reduced A, sq_eq_zero_iff gives quadraticSection(v)=0 iff v=0. Over dual numbers this implication fails, which is why the geometric construction uses an open subscheme rather than raw nonzero ring-valued tuples.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection` (constructor): For v=(u,alpha), return (u,alpha^2) on the existing product of function spaces.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.kernelCoordinates` (projection): The first projection of quadraticSection(v) equals u.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.rootCoordinates` (simp): The jth second coordinate is alpha_j squared.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.baseChange` (functoriality): For a ring homomorphism h:A->B, applying h to both coordinate blocks commutes with quadraticSection.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.weighted` (compatibility): For any c in A, quadraticSection(c^2 u,c alpha)=c^2 quadraticSection(u,alpha), where the scalar on the right multiplies both output blocks.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.zero_iff` (characterisation): If A is reduced, quadraticSection(v)=0 if and only if v=0; the reduced hypothesis is retained.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.test_small` (computation): Over Z with one coordinate in each block, quadraticSection(2,3)=(2,9).
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.test_empty_root` (degenerate): For an empty root index Fin 0, quadraticSection(u,alpha)=(u,alpha).
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.test_not_injective` (non-example): Over Z with one coordinate in each block, (0,1) and (0,-1) are distinct and have the same section coordinate.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.test_nilpotent` (non-example): Over DualNumber(F_3), the tuple (0,epsilon) is nonzero but quadraticSection(0,epsilon)=0.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.quadraticSection.test_effective_nilpotent` (computation): Over DualNumber(F_3), quadraticSection(1,epsilon)=(1,0); the full chart still retains epsilon in its root coordinate.

**Acceptance.** At I=J=Fin 1 over Z, (2,3) maps to (2,9).; Over F_3[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), (0,epsilon) is nonzero but its section coordinate is zero.

**Consumers.** where: GC.4/family-fibre-presentation; how: Identify the polynomial section coordinate after splitting evaluation and compute its effective open.; where: YZ19, Lemma A.9, p. 521; how: Verify that kernel and root blocks carry weights two and one.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.9, proof, p. 521 The split evaluation description supplies the quadratic coordinate formula; the native ring formulation and nilpotent checks are its algebraic interface, not a claim that the source develops ring-valued charts.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-affine-fibre-chart"></a>

#### The Abel–Jacobi affine fibre chart

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/affine-fibre-chart` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

At a fixed geometric root-Picard object (L,K_R,ι), the two-fibre of AJ_d is M=H⁰(X,L) minus {0}×_{H⁰(R,L|_R)}H⁰(R,K_R), with the second map α↦ι(α²). For ρ>0 and the degree bound, a splitting of evaluation identifies M≃A^n minus {0}, n=d−g+1. Scaling K_R by λ and L by λ² gives weights two on n−ρ coordinates and one on ρ coordinates.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ρ>0 and d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1).

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/evaluation-surjective`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-evaluation-surjective), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-abel-jacobi`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-abel-jacobi).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the definition of the two-fibre over a fixed object: there are no remaining compatible automorphisms of that object.
2. Choose a splitting of the surjective evaluation map; write a=u+split(ι(α²)).
3. The effective condition removes the origin; the scaling law gives the displayed weights. The weighted quotient maps to the moduli stack but is not identified with this fixed-object fibre.

**Acceptance.** M itself is not asserted simply connected in positive characteristic.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.9 p. 521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-family-fibre-presentation"></a>

#### The family Abel–Jacobi fibre chart

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/family-fibre-presentation` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For a root Picard object b=(L,K_R,iota) on X_T, with T locally Noetherian over k, put E=pi_*L, U=pi_*L(-R), G=pi_R*(L|R), H=pi_R*K_R, and q:H->G induced by alpha->iota(alpha^2). The imported high-degree vanishing yields a universally base-change-compatible exact sequence 0->U->E->G->0 of locally free sheaves of ranks a,n,rho, and H has rank rho. Define C_hat_b=V(E) x_{V(G)} V(H), with V(F) parametrizing sections of F, and C_b as the inverse image of V(E) minus its zero section. Then C_b is the actual two-pullback T x_{P_d} S_d. Etale locally on T, split R_T, choose frames and an evaluation splitting sigma; the isomorphism (u,alpha)->(u+sigma(q(alpha)),alpha) identifies C_hat_b with A_T^n and C_b with A_T^n minus the zero section as OPEN SCHEMES. These presentations and their effective opens commute with every base change T_prime->T, without a flatness or reducedness assumption on T_prime.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.; d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.; P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.; T is locally Noetherian over k for the coherent pushforward theorem; base changes from T may be arbitrary. No rational point on X and no global Poincare line bundle on a Picard scheme are chosen.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/quadratic-section-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-quadratic-section-coordinates), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/evaluation-surjective`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-evaluation-surjective), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-abel-jacobi`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-abel-jacobi), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.1/root-symmetric-space`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-1-root-symmetric-space), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/line-bundle-degree-bounds`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-stack-curve`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.sections_surjective`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Import parent evaluation-surjective, SF.3/line-bundle-degree-bounds and the existing coherent sections_surjective theorem: H1(L_t(-R))=0 since d-rho>2g-2, and H1(L_t)=0. Relative coherent base change gives E,U and the exact evaluation sequence; finite etale R_T gives G,H and their arbitrary base change. The genus and ranks come from coherent Riemann–Roch.
2. Use GC.1/root-abel-jacobi and SF.1/two-fibre-product to identify the fixed-object two-pullback with the displayed section equation. An automorphism inducing the identity of b is the identity; the fibre is a scheme, not the weighted quotient.
3. Etale split R and trivialize K_R and U; frame L|R using iota. Locally split E->G. The displayed inverse is (s,alpha)->(s-sigma(q(alpha)),alpha). These are polynomial maps, with the section coordinate given by quadraticSection.
4. In these coordinates the inverse image of the zero section of E is defined by (u_i,alpha_j^2). Its radical equals that of (u_i,alpha_j), so its complement is exactly the usual punctured affine open. Do not identify the two CLOSED subschemes or discard nilpotents in the complement.
5. If sigma_prime=sigma+t for t:G->U, the transition is (u,alpha)->(u-t(q(alpha)),alpha). This quadratic transition is equivariant for weights (2,1), and the identity/composition laws follow by adding differences of splittings. The unsplit fibre product gives their canonical gluing and all base-change comparisons.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre` (constructor): C_b is the two-fibre T x_{P_d} S_d, represented by the effective open in the square-evaluation fibre product.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.evaluationSequence` (data): Supply 0->U->E->G->0, ranks (a,n,rho), rank(H)=rho, and arbitrary base change for all four sheaves and evaluation.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.splitIso` (equivalence): An evaluation splitting and compatible etale frames identify C_hat_b with A_T^n by (u,alpha)->(u+sigma(q(alpha)),alpha), and restrict to C_b.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.effectiveOpen` (characterisation): The removed closed locus has ideal (u_i,alpha_j^2); the complement equals A_T^n minus the zero section, without identifying the closed loci.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.changeSplitting` (compatibility): For sigma_prime=sigma+t the coordinate transition is u_prime=u-t(q(alpha)), with alpha fixed; it respects weighted scaling.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.baseChange` (functoriality): The fibre product, effective open and chart comparison commute with every T_prime->T and with isomorphisms of b; the identity and composition comparisons satisfy the cocycle law.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.smoothConnected` (structure): C_b->T is smooth and surjective with geometrically connected fibres A^n minus the origin.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.test_minimal_elliptic` (computation): For g=1,rho=1,d=2 the chart has one kernel coordinate and one root coordinate and section coordinate (u,alpha^2).
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.test_nilpotent_excluded` (non-example): For T=Spec F_3[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), u=0 and alpha=epsilon do not define a T-point of C_b: the global section is zero, even though (u,alpha) is a nonzero tuple.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.test_nilpotent_retained` (computation): On the same base, u=1 and alpha=epsilon lie in C_b, and their root coordinate remains epsilon under the chart; no reduction of the scheme is allowed.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.test_empty` (degenerate): If R is empty, G=H=0 and C_b=V(E) minus its zero section, the ordinary section-stack fibre over the Picard STACK.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.test_splitting` (compatibility): For one-dimensional G,U and t the identity, replacing sigma by sigma+t sends u to u-alpha^2. Retaining u unchanged would fail the section equation.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiFibre.test_residue_degree` (non-example): A single closed point of residue degree two contributes rho=2 and two geometric root coordinates; it is not counted as rho=1.

**Acceptance.** For g=1,rho=1,d=2, the ranks are (a,n,rho)=(1,2,1), and the split equation is s=(u,alpha^2).; At d=2g-2+rho, L=omega_X(R) has L(-R)=omega_X and nonzero H1. The requested threshold cannot silently lose rho or replace strict vanishing by equality.; T may have square-zero nilpotents: the effective open is tested on all geometric fibres, not by whether its raw section tuple is unequal to zero.

**Consumers.** where: GC.4/relative-projective-quotient; how: Supply the canonical family carrying the scalar action and its local positive weights.; where: GC.4/high-degree-effective-descent; how: Prove that the actual checking map C_b->T is smooth surjective with geometrically connected fibres.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Definition A.2, p. 515; §A.1.5, p. 517; Lemma A.9, pp. 520–521 Defines effectiveness by geometric fibres and the two Abel–Jacobi maps, then describes a geometric fibre by the square-evaluation equation. The node promotes that equation to families and records the scheme-theoretic open and transition maps. [StacksVanishing](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E3A) — Lemma 53.22.1, tag 0E3A, Algebraic Curves §53.22 (online numbering) Nonvanishing of H1(L(-R)) forces d<=2g-2+rho, giving the strict high-degree vanishing used by the imported coherent supplier. [StacksBaseChange](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07VJ) — Lemma 30.22.1 and Remark 30.22.2, tag 07VJ, Cohomology of Schemes §30.22 (online numbering) A proper scheme with coherent base-flat coefficients has a perfect cohomology complex compatible with arbitrary ring maps. With fibrewise higher-cohomology vanishing it yields the locally free degree-zero pushforward used here.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-cover"></a>

#### A projective cover of the weighted quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-cover` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For n≥ρ+1 and ρ≥1, set a=n−ρ. The coordinate map [x₁,…,x_a,y₁,…,y_ρ]↦[x₁²,…,x_a²,y₁,…,y_ρ] defines a finite cover P^{n−1}→[A^n minus {0}/G_m], with weights (2^a,1^ρ). Its generic Galois group is μ₂^a.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ρ≥1; n≥ρ+1; a=n−ρ.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/affine-fibre-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-affine-fibre-chart), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. The coordinate map is equivariant for the ordinary weight-one source and weighted target.
2. Descend to the projective quotient and check finiteness on charts.
3. The independent signs of the x_i give the generic μ₂^a action.

**Acceptance.** The positive weight-one block is essential; the all-weight-two quotient has residual generic μ₂ inertia.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.9 p. 521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-ramification"></a>

#### Nontrivial intermediate weighted covers ramify

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-ramification` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

A proper subgroup Γ⊊μ₂^a gives an intermediate cover of the weighted quotient that is ramified along at least one coordinate divisor x_i=0 in a chart where a weight-one coordinate y_ρ is nonzero. Hence such an intermediate cover cannot be finite étale.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ρ≥1; n≥ρ+1.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-cover`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-cover).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Choose a nontrivial character of μ₂^a/Γ, represented by a nonempty coordinate subset I.
2. On y_ρ≠0 its invariant root is the monomial ∏_{i∈I}x_i with square ∏_{i∈I}z_i.
3. This quadratic subcover ramifies along each z_i=0 for i∈I since two is invertible.

**Acceptance.** The nonempty subset I and the weight-one affine chart are both required.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.9 p. 521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-simply-connected"></a>

#### Simple connectivity of the weighted quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-simply-connected` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

After base change to an algebraically closed field K of characteristic not two, the weighted quotient [A_K^n minus {0}/G_m,K] with weights (2^{n−ρ},1^ρ), ρ≥1 and n≥ρ+1, has no nontrivial connected finite étale cover. Thus every rank-one lisse Q̄ℓ-local system on the original quotient is geometrically constant.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ρ≥1; n≥ρ+1.; The simple-connectivity assertion is on the geometric base change to an algebraically closed field K; ρ≥1 and n≥ρ+1.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-cover`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-cover), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-ramification`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-ramification), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Pull a connected finite étale cover back to P^{n−1}; the supplier’s projective-space simple connectivity makes that pullback trivial.
2. A component supplies a lift of the projective cover, and the generic function field is an intermediate μ₂^a extension.
3. The ramification lemma forces Γ=μ₂^a; the cover has degree one, hence is an equivalence. Apply the stack lisse/fundamental-group comparison.

**Acceptance.** At ρ=0 the proof does not apply; the ordinary Abel–Jacobi argument uses ordinary projective fibres.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Claim in proof of Lemma A.9 p. 521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-fibre-triviality"></a>

#### Triviality of the symmetric sheaf along Abel–Jacobi fibres

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/fibre-triviality` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

Under the high-degree bound and ρ>0, L_d restricts to a constant sheaf on each geometric two-fibre M of AJ_d.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/affine-fibre-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-affine-fibre-chart), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/weighted-simply-connected`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-weighted-simply-connected), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-monodromy-symmetric-local-system).

**Construction/proof.**

1. The map M→X_d^√R factors through the weighted quotient by the scalar root-Picard automorphisms.
2. Pull L_d to that quotient; it is lisse because L_d is lisse.
3. Simple connectivity makes this pullback constant, hence constant on M.

**Acceptance.** This does not invoke false simple connectivity of punctured affine space.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proof of Lemma A.9 p. 521

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-relative-projective-quotient"></a>

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/relative-projective-quotient` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For b and C_b as above, define Q_b=[C_b/G_m,T]. If rho>0 the scalar c acts by (s,alpha)->(c^2 s,c alpha); its automorphism of b is (c^2 id_L,c id_K_R). If rho=0 use the ordinary scalar c id_L and weight one on s. The map C_b->S_d is 2-equivariant for this scalar action and the trivial action on S_d, hence induces h_b:Q_b->S_d. The projection q_b:Q_b->T is proper smooth surjective with geometrically connected, geometrically simply connected tame DM fibres of dimension n-1. For rho>0 it is etale locally W(2^a,1^rho); for rho=0 it is the ordinary projective bundle parametrizing lines in E. All data are functorial in b and commute with base change. Although f h_b and b q_b agree after pullback to C_b, they are generally NOT 2-isomorphic on Q_b: the scalar descent twists the Picard object. No factorization over P_d is claimed.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.; d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.; P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.

Before quotients it is finite free of rank 2^a, with basis the squarefree monomials in the a source kernel coordinates. Equivariance for the SAME G_m makes the descended P_T^{n-1}->Q_b representable finite locally free of that rank. It is a branched map, not a torsor under its generic sign group.

This finite faithfully flat cover by projective space proves properness: its relation is finite over projective space, hence proper over T and over the separated product; descend the proper diagonal and universal closedness. Smoothness follows from the punctured affine smooth atlas. Stabilizers are trivial when a root coordinate is nonzero and mu_2 on the remaining locus, so the stack is DM and tame in odd characteristic. These properties descend along the etale chart cover.

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiQuotient.projectiveCover` (data): For rho>0 in a split chart, P_T^{n-1}->Q_b is representable finite locally free of rank 2^a, generically Galois with independent sign changes.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiQuotient.properSmooth` (structure): q_b is proper smooth surjective tame DM with geometrically connected fibres of dimension n-1.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiQuotient.geometricCovers` (characterisation): Every connected representable finite etale cover of a geometric fibre of q_b has degree one.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiQuotient.baseChange` (functoriality): The intrinsic quotient and h_b commute with base change and isomorphisms of b, with identity and composition coherence.

**Checks.**

#### The canonical local descent line

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/chart-descent-line` · construction · implementation unchecked.

Let F be a rank-one lisse sheaf on S_d. For every b:T->P_d as in the family construction, set F_Q=h_b^*F on Q_b and M_b=(q_b)_*F_Q at finite coefficient level. Proper degree-zero base change and the geometric simple connectivity of Q_b give a canonical evaluation isomorphism e_b:q_b^*M_b->F_Q. M_b is lisse of rank one, and its pullback to the actual C_b is canonically F|C_b. Define the adic and Qbar_ell version by compatible local coefficient lattices and reduction, invert ell, and extend coefficients; it is independent of these presentations. Base change, isomorphisms of b, and morphisms of F give coherent comparison maps for M_b, including composition and identity laws.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.; d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.; P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.; F is an arbitrary rank-one lisse input on S_d; it need not be the particular symmetric local system L_d. The generic stack-lisse interfaces listed in gap GC4-LISSE-ADAPTER are required and are not claimed present in a scheme-only supplier.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/relative-projective-quotient`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-4-relative-projective-quotient), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-monodromy-symmetric-local-system), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/adic-local-systems`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the previous construction to obtain q_b proper smooth surjective tame DM and F_Q. At finite coefficient level apply ACV01 Theorem A.0.8 in degree zero: the stalk of (q_b)_*F_Q is H0 of its geometric fibre.
2. By the parent weighted simple-connectivity theorem (or ordinary projective simple connectivity for R empty), F_Q on a geometric fibre is constant, and evaluation of its global sections at any point is an isomorphism. Therefore the adjunction counit q_b^*(q_b)_*F_Q->F_Q is an isomorphism on all geometric stalks.
3. The smooth surjection q_b has sections etale locally after choosing a smooth scheme atlas of Q_b. Pull the counit back along such sections: M_b becomes a rank-one lisse sheaf there. This proves local constancy, instead of inferring it merely from the rank of its stalks.
4. Proper base change gives M_{b|T_prime} canonically isomorphic to the inverse image of M_b. The comparisons are the natural base-change maps and satisfy identity and composition. Pull the counit through C_b->Q_b to compare on the actual Abel–Jacobi fibre product.
5. Do the construction for finite reductions of local O_E lattices. Full faithfulness of inverse image along q_b (unit checked by the same fibre H0 calculation) forces the coefficient reductions and comparisons to be compatible; pass to the local adic category, invert ell and extend scalars. Glue different local lattices using the same full faithfulness. This coefficient/stack adapter is the explicit generic supplier gap, not an extra assumption of effective Abel–Jacobi descent.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine` (constructor): At finite coefficients M_b=(q_b)_*h_b^*F, extended by compatible local adic presentations.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.evaluation` (equivalence): The canonical counit e_b:q_b^*M_b->h_b^*F is an isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.onFibreProduct` (compatibility): Pulling e_b along C_b->Q_b gives f_b^*M_b isomorphic to F|C_b for f_b:C_b->T.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.baseChange` (functoriality): For T_prime->T the proper base-change comparison identifies M_{b|T_prime} with the pullback of M_b and respects e_b; identity and composition commute.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.map` (functoriality): A morphism F->F_prime induces M_b(F)->M_b(F_prime); identity and composition are preserved.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.coefficients` (compatibility): Reduction of compatible integral lattices, inversion of ell and finite coefficient extension commute with the construction and its evaluation; different local lattice presentations give the same lisse Qbar_ell line.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.tensor` (compatibility): The natural tensor comparison M_b(F) tensor M_b(G)->M_b(F tensor G) is the unique isomorphism whose pullback is the tensor of the evaluation maps; it respects units, associators and symmetry.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.test_unit` (degenerate): The constant coefficient line on S_d gives the constant coefficient line on T, with the identity evaluation comparison.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.test_arithmetic` (non-example): For F pulled back from Spec k with geometric Frobenius zeta_3, M_b is the same arithmetic line on T; it is not forced to have Frobenius 1 or -1.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.test_square_zero_base` (compatibility): The base change from Spec F_3[epsilon]/(epsilon^2) to Spec F_3 commutes with M_b and e_b, despite not being flat.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.test_scalar` (computation): Multiplication by c in the coefficient field on F induces multiplication by c on M_b, including c=0; the construction acts on sheaf morphisms, not just isomorphism classes.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.abelJacobiDescentLine.test_empty` (compatibility): If R is empty, the construction is q_*h^*F for the ordinary projective bundle q:P(E)->T, with its ordinary evaluation comparison.

**Acceptance.** A geometrically constant arithmetic line with geometric Frobenius eigenvalue zeta_3 descends with eigenvalue zeta_3; geometric constancy does not force arithmetic triviality or sign-valued global monodromy.; For a constant coefficient line on S_d, e_b is its canonical constant-line comparison.; The construction retains rank one at every geometric point and commutes with nonflat base changes.

#### Effective high-degree Abel–Jacobi descent

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.4/high-degree-effective-descent` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

At d>=rho+max(2g-1,1), inverse image along f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d is fully faithful on rank-one lisse Qbar_ell sheaves and every rank-one lisse sheaf F on S_d is in its essential image. In particular there is a rank-one L_d^Pic with a comparison theta:f^*L_d^Pic isomorphic to the unshifted symmetric rank-one L_d from GC.3. Given two pairs (M,theta),(M_prime,theta_prime) for the same F, there is exactly one isomorphism M->M_prime whose pullback intertwines the two comparisons. This uniqueness is for the normalized pair, not for the underlying sheaf with its scalar automorphisms. Descent, comparisons, tensor operations and any supplied geometric-Frobenius structure are compatible with base change over k. The empty-R branch uses ordinary projective quotients.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.; R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.; d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.; P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.

**Construction/proof.**

1. For each smooth locally finite type scheme atlas T->P_d, construct M_b and its comparison using chart-descent-line. This uses a proper DM map Q_b->T, not properness or a homotopy exact sequence for the nonproper AJ_d.
2. By family-fibre-presentation, the actual f_b:C_b->T is smooth surjective with geometrically connected fibres. Pulling back any connected finite etale cover of connected T leaves a connected space: the projection to that cover is an open surjection with connected geometric fibres. The finite-cover/fibre-functor comparison therefore gives a surjection on pi1, so f_b^* is fully faithful on finite locally constant sheaves. The local adic formalism gives the same full faithfulness for rank-one lisse sheaves.
3. The double and triple overlaps of the scheme atlas over the Artin stack P_d may be algebraic spaces. Choose etale scheme covers of these overlaps and apply the preceding scheme-chart full-faithfulness argument after each refinement. On the double overlap the two M_b pull back to the same F on its actual Abel–Jacobi fibre product, so this supplies the unique overlap isomorphism compatible with those comparisons. Uniqueness makes these isomorphisms descend from the refinements. On the triple overlap the cocycle holds because its pullback holds. Effective smooth descent for lisse sheaves glues M and theta on P_d; no scheme fundamental-group statement is applied directly to an algebraic stack or algebraic space.
4. Check arbitrary morphisms on the atlas and its overlaps by the same full faithfulness; this proves full faithfulness globally and normalized uniqueness. It also identifies this construction with parent high-degree-descent for the specific symmetric L_d, without assuming that parent end theorem to prove itself.
5. Apply the comparisons to tensor products, units and any Frobenius pullback; uniqueness makes their coherence diagrams descend. Carry out the same argument using P(E) when R is empty.

The normalized pair has only its identity automorphism, but a bare rank-one sheaf retains its coefficient-field scalars.; The source L_d is unshifted and lisse. The perverse normalization would be L_d[d] on S_d, not the object in this rank-one descent statement.

## GC.5 — All-degree character sheaves

Translate each integer-degree component into the high-degree range with an effective divisor away from R, then remove its Frobenius line. Common enlargements and the cocycle make the result independent of choices. The signed translation contract, normalized universal property and whole-section-space multiplication include negative degrees and nonzero zero-section stalks. No rational point of degree one is needed.

**Planets.** All-degree Picard character sheaf — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/all-degree-extension`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-all-degree-extension); All-degree Abel–Jacobi comparison — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/effective-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-effective-pullback); Character-sheaf unit — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/unit-trivialization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-unit-trivialization); Picard character multiplication — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/all-degree-multiplication`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-all-degree-multiplication); Hat Abel–Jacobi character pullback — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/hat-character-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-hat-character-pullback); Divisor tensor line — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/signed-divisor-line`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-signed-divisor-line).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Conventions and imported objects

Let $k$ be a finite field of odd characteristic, $X/k$ a smooth projective
geometrically connected curve of genus $g$, and $R\subset X$ a reduced
finite closed subscheme. Put $U=X\setminus R$, $\rho=\deg R$, and

$$
 B=\rho+\max(2g-1,1).
$$

The empty ramification locus is allowed. Fix a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$
and coefficients $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The input $L$ is an arbitrary
rank-one lisse local system on $X_1^{\sqrt R}$, with its $k$-descent.
Its inertia at $R$ has order dividing two. Its global monodromy can have
order three or infinite image. The sheaves in this document are unshifted
rank-one local systems: $L_n[n]$, rather than $L_n$, is the perverse
normalization.

Write $\mathcal P^d=\operatorname{Pic}_X^{\sqrt R,d}$. Over a test scheme
$T/k$, an object is a degree-$d$ line bundle $M$ on $X_T$, a line bundle
$K_R$ on $R_T$, and an isomorphism $K_R^{\otimes2}\simeq M|_{R_T}$.
Morphisms preserve this isomorphism. These are the actual Picard-stack
objects of `FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`; this layer does
not introduce another stack. Tensor product gives
$m_{d,e}:\mathcal P^d\times\mathcal P^e\to\mathcal P^{d+e}$.
The unit $e$ has both line bundles trivial and their standard comparison.
No chosen $k$-rational point of $X$ is part of the data. Ordinary
$\operatorname{Pic}^d$ is used as a torsor where appropriate, without
identifying it with a pointed Jacobian.

For $n\ge0$, the parent supplies the effective root-divisor space
$X_n^{\sqrt R}$, the whole section space $\widehat X_n^{\sqrt R}$, and
maps $AJ_n$ and $\widehat{AJ}_n$ forgetting section data. A whole-space
object also has a global section $a$ of $M$ and a root section
$\alpha_R$ of $K_R$, with $i(\alpha_R^2)=a|_{R_T}$. The effective open
and its symmetric local system $L_n$ are those of GC.1 and GC.3; this layer
does not redefine what effective means in a family.

The parent `GC.4/high-degree-descent` supplies a lisse sheaf $H_n$ on
$\mathcal P^n$, with $AJ_n^*H_n\simeq L_n$, for $n\ge B$, uniquely
with this comparison. Its effective descent and full-faithfulness theorem
are prerequisite results with a recorded gap. Connected geometric fibres
alone are insufficient to assert that an arbitrary sheaf descends.

A divisor $D\in\operatorname{Div}(U)$ means a finite integer combination
of closed points of $U$. Its degree is
$\sum_x n_x[\kappa(x):k]$, not $\sum_x n_x$.
The canonical rational section of $\mathcal O_X(D)$ is nonvanishing at
$R$; its restriction determines the trivial root there. Denote that
root-Picard $k$-point by $\delta_D$ and its translation by

$$
 t_D:\mathcal P^d\longrightarrow\mathcal P^{d+\deg D},\qquad
 M\longmapsto M\otimes\delta_D.
$$

This exists for signed divisors. Addition of a divisor on an effective
symmetric space, denoted $T_D$, is used only when $D\ge0$. Tensoring with
a Frobenius line means tensoring with its inverse image from
$\operatorname{Spec}k$. An arithmetic line need not be Frobenius-trivial.
Use geometric Frobenius throughout. All comparisons below are
Frobenius-equivariant maps of sheaves, not just equalities of functions on
rational points.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/auxiliary-divisors` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For every integer d and bound B there exists an effective divisor D on U=X−R with d+deg D≥B. The construction requires no rational point of degree one. For two choices D,E, a common effective enlargement is D+E.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

1. Choose a closed point of the nonempty affine open U.
2. A sufficiently large multiple of that point exceeds any prescribed degree bound.
3. Use sums of effective divisors for a common comparison enlargement.

#### The tensor line attached to an effective divisor

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/divisor-tensor-line` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For an effective D=Σn_x x supported on U, define the Frobenius line L_D as the tensor product of the fibres of L over all geometric points above x, each repeated n_x times, with its Frobenius permutation descent. This is the value of L_{deg D} at the canonical root divisor O(D)^♮.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/high-degree-multiplication` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For d,e≥B, mult*L_{d+e}^Pic≅L_d^Pic⊠L_e^Pic on the product Pic^√R,d×Pic^√R,e. The pullback comparison uses AJ_d×AJ_e, not AJ_{d+e}.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Pull back by the product of the two Abel–Jacobi maps.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-signed-divisor-line"></a>

#### Signed divisor tensor line

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/signed-divisor-line` · construction · implementation unchecked.

For D=sum_x n_x[x] with n_x in Z, tensor, for each closed x, all conjugate geometric stalk lines of L over x, each to power n_x (negative power means dual), with the cyclic Frobenius permutation and local action. Equivalently for D=A-C with A,C effective away from R, set Lambda_D=Lambda_A tensor Lambda_C^dual. The effective sum comparison induces canonical decomposition-independent identifications and a symmetric monoidal functor to the groupoid of one-dimensional Qbar_ell vector spaces with continuous k-Galois action. Its value agrees with the parent effective line for effective D; no ordering or chosen geometric lift belongs to the data.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, rho=deg R, U=X minus R.; ell is a prime different from char(k); coefficients are Qbar_ell. The input L is an arbitrary rank-one lisse local system on the square-root curve X_1^sqrtR, with its k-descent. Inertia over R has order dividing two; global monodromy is not assumed quadratic.; Use the actual root Picard stack P^d of triples (M,K_R,i:K_R tensor K_R isomorphic to M restricted to R), and the parent unshifted symmetric local systems L_n and high-degree descents H_n for n at least B=rho+max(2g-1,1). 1. Use the parent effective divisor line and sum comparison, whose coherence is inherited from GC.3 symmetric multiplicativity, associativity and symmetry.
2. Define the negative factors by actual duals of rank-one Frobenius lines. For A-C=Aprime-Cprime, use A+Cprime=Aprime+C and the effective sum comparison, then tensor-cancel the C,Cprime factors. Coherence gives independence of intermediate decomposition.
3. Check zero, addition, inverse and symmetry on a common effective refinement. Geometric conjugate permutations supply descent at a nonrational closed point; the dual inverts that action.
4. The necessary lisse tensor/dual carriers and coherence are the inherited GC.3 supplier gap, not new coherent-module theory.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.signedDivisorTensorLine.effective` (compatibility): For effective D, the signed line is identified with parent divisorTensorLine(D), preserving its sum comparison and Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.signedDivisorTensorLine.sum` (structure): Lambda_(D+E) is canonically Lambda_D tensor Lambda_E; the maps satisfy associativity, symmetry and both unit diagrams.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.signedDivisorTensorLine.neg` (equivalence): Lambda_-D is canonically Lambda_D^dual, with evaluation giving Lambda_D tensor Lambda_-D isomorphic to Qbar_ell.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.signedDivisorTensorLine.decomposition` (characterisation): For D=A-C, Lambda_D is Lambda_A tensor Lambda_C^dual. All such identifications agree via A+Cprime=Aprime+C and satisfy their cocycle.

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.signedDivisorTensorLine.test_degree_two_negative` (computation): For a degree-two closed point x, Lambda_(-[x]) is (L_x1 tensor L_x2)^dual, with the dual cyclic Frobenius action; one selected stalk is insufficient.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-normalized-character-universal-property"></a>

#### Universal property of normalized character presentations

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/normalized-character-universal-property` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Fix d in Z and the geometric conventions. For every effective admissible D let Q_D=t_D^*H_(d+degD) tensor Lambda_D^dual. Write c_DE:Q_D isomorphic to Q_E for the parent canonical comparisons and q_D:Q_D isomorphic to P_d for their canonical identifications with the parent all-degree character. They satisfy q_E composed with c_DE=q_D. For any actual lisse sheaf M on P^d, precomposition with all q_D gives a bijection from Hom(P_d,M) to families f_D:Q_D to M satisfying f_E composed with c_DE=f_D for every D,E. Consequently any lisse sheaf equipped with compatible isomorphisms from all Q_D has a unique isomorphism from P_d respecting every normalization. This uniqueness includes the comparison data, not the bare underlying sheaf.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, rho=deg R, U=X minus R.; ell is a prime different from char(k); coefficients are Qbar_ell. The input L is an arbitrary rank-one lisse local system on the square-root curve X_1^sqrtR, with its k-descent. Inertia over R has order dividing two; global monodromy is not assumed quadratic.; Use the actual root Picard stack P^d of triples (M,K_R,i:K_R tensor K_R isomorphic to M restricted to R), and the parent unshifted symmetric local systems L_n and high-degree descents H_n for n at least B=rho+max(2g-1,1). Use geometric Frobenius throughout; all sheaf maps are Frobenius-equivariant.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the nonempty effective choice set from the parent auxiliary-divisors theorem; use the parent choice-comparison and choice-cocycle to obtain q_D and its compatibility.
2. Choose one admissible D0 only for the proof. For a compatible family set f=f_D0 composed with q_D0 inverse. The cocycle identity shows f composed with q_D=f_D for every D.
3. The same identity proves independence of D0; since q_D0 is an isomorphism it also proves uniqueness. Apply the result to isomorphism families for the final uniqueness statement.
4. This is a consequence of the normalization construction in A.2.2, not an additional descent theorem or an assertion that arbitrary Picard sheaves are classified by divisor values.

**Acceptance.** A scalar twist of q_D0 at one choice and no others is not a compatible family unless the scalar is 1.; For high d, use the admissible zero divisor and recover the original high-degree descent H_d with its pullback comparison.; At d=-1 use any sufficiently large multiple of an away closed point; the uniqueness proof never requires a degree-one divisor.

The bijection is a derived API statement, not a separately numbered theorem in the paper.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.picardCharacter.normalizedUniversalProperty`.

<a id="gc-6"></a>

## GC.6 — Ramified norms and quadratic traces

A root-unit equalizer identifies the root Picard torsor stack. A local determinant calculation proves the root norm and its branch-square compatibility. Keep the two based torsor fibres and their connecting obstructions separate from invariance of Picard classes. Existing weak approximation moves support while preserving root frames; the actual modified-unit image is retained. A cyclic tensor trace gives the closed-point scalar once, then signed translation identifies the character on every degree. The quadratic specialization has split value +1 and inert value −1.

**Planets.** Root multiplicative sheaf — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-multiplicative-sheaf`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-multiplicative-sheaf); Ramified root norm — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-norm`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-norm); Ramified norm sheaf exactness — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/exact-sheaf-complex`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-exact-sheaf-complex); Quadratic root-curve local system — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/quadratic-input`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-quadratic-input); Ramified geometric class field theory — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/quadratic-trace`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-quadratic-trace); Norm descent obstructions — [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-descent-obstruction`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-descent-obstruction).

### Proof architecture and boundary calculations

#### Obstruction convention and the source interpretation

The nullhomotopy target fixes the trivialization carried by a difference line d(M)=M tensor (sigma^*M)^dual. This matters even if the underlying norm class vanishes. If tau:N(L) isomorphic to 1 is a chosen norm trivialization, define P_tau as the preimage of the unit in the corresponding B-torsor. A change of convention is pinned as

\[
 \tau_{\mathrm{new}}=c^{-1}\tau,\qquad
 [P_{\tau_{\mathrm{new}}}]=[P_\tau]+\delta_N^0(c).
\]

Consequently

\[
 \omega(L)=
 [\delta_q^1(P_\tau)]\ \in\
 H^2(A)/\operatorname{im}(\delta_q^1\delta_N^0)
\]

is independent of tau. Its vanishing is the criterion for the *underlying* line class to be a difference. For a *fixed* tau, the criterion is instead delta_q^1[P_tau]=0 in H²(A) itself. The proof is a pair of applications of exactness in the already existing derived cohomology, followed by the imported torsor/H¹ comparison. It requires no assumption that a chosen ordinary covering computes H², and no claim that every obstruction gerbe has already been classified.

The full fibre groupoid of pairs (M,beta:q_*M isomorphic to 1), allowing isomorphisms of M that preserve beta, is Tors(A) and has H⁰(A) automorphisms. This does not say that, after fixing both M and an identification of a descent's pullback with M, the resulting groupoid still has every scalar automorphism. That distinction prevents a further loss of the specified descent data.

The parent source issue `FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII/E8` concerns the unqualified Picard-stack exactness display (A.11) in Yun–Zhang, A.3.3, printed p.525. Its confirmed interpretation gap is inherited without creating a duplicate finding. The two based torsor fibres and the obstruction formulas above are the precise replacement used here. They do not assert that every possible intended coherent interpretation of the source display is false. The published author-hosted copy was reread on 18 October 2026; the correction search recorded by the parent is dated 2 October 2026 and is not claimed as a new search. No new source issue was found in this pass. The quadratic trace proof depends on multiplication, Frobenius transport and support moving, independently of this display.
