#### The root multiplicative sheaf

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-multiplicative-sheaf` · definition · implementation unchecked.

On X_et define G_m,X^√R=G_m,X×_{i_*G_m,R,[2]}i_*G_m,R. Its sections are pairs (u,v) of a unit and a root unit on R satisfying u|_R=v². Its torsor stack is the root Picard stack.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Take the fibre product in sheaves of abelian multiplicative groups.
2. A torsor for this group is equivalently a G_m line-bundle torsor with a square-root torsor of its restriction and a compatible square identification.
3. Use effective line-bundle/torsor descent to identify the resulting Picard stack.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf.sections` (characterisation): Its sections are exactly (u,v) with u|_R=v².
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf.forget` (projection): Forget v to G_m,X.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf.torsors` (equivalence): Its torsor stack is Pic_X^√R.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf.test_empty_R` (degenerate): At R=∅ this is G_m,X.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf.test_kernel` (computation): The forgetful kernel on R is μ₂.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf.test_nonadditive` (non-example): For odd-characteristic residue rings the square map is multiplicative but does not define an additive ring map.

**Acceptance.** This is a sheaf of multiplicative groups, not a fibre-product ring using the square map.

**Consumers.** where: YZ19 A.3.1–A.3.3; how: Receives the root norm and its exact sheaf sequence.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.1 p. 524

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.rootMultiplicativeSheaf`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-trace-character"></a>

#### The Frobenius trace is a character

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/trace-character` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

The Frobenius trace of L^Pic is a multiplicative Q̄ℓ×-valued function on isomorphism classes of Pic_X^√R(k), normalized to one at the tensor unit. Via the adelic equivalence it defines an idele character. For general input L its range is not restricted to {±1}.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/all-degree-multiplication`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-all-degree-multiplication), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/character-associativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-character-associativity), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/character-symmetry-unit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-character-symmetry-unit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/adelic-root-groupoid`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-adelic-root-groupoid).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply Frobenius to the multiplication isomorphism and take the trace of the rank-one tensor line.
2. Use the canonical unit to fix the value at e.
3. Transport through the groupoid equivalence, preserving descent invariance.

**Acceptance.** The unramified order-three input has a character of order three, not a quadratic one.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.2.2, pp. 521–523; Proposition A.11 and its proof, pp. 522–523.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-unit-coordinates"></a>

#### Root-unit coordinates

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-unit-coordinates` · definition · implementation unchecked.

For a homomorphism r:A0 to B0 of commutative rings, rootUnitCoordinates(r) is the native subgroup of A0^units times B0^units cut out by Units.map(r)(u)=v^2. It is the equalizer of the restriction of the first projection and the square of the second projection. It retains both coordinates and their unit proofs. On a framed etale chart this is the section formula for the imported root multiplicative sheaf, not a substitute for its sheaf or stack.

**Hypotheses.** A0 and B0 are commutative rings in arbitrary universes; r is a ring homomorphism. No nontriviality, reducedness, surjectivity of r or invertibility of 2 is needed for this coordinate definition.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:MonoidHom.eqLocus`, `mathlib:powMonoidHom`, `mathlib:Units.map`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Compose the two native product projections with Units.map(r) and the power homomorphism.
2. Take their existing subgroup equalizer. Restriction maps preserve the defining equality; the geometric comparison is supplied by root-torsor-comparison.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.mem_rootUnitCoordinates` (characterisation): Membership of (u,v) is equivalent to Units.map(r)(u)=v^2.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rootUnitCoordinates_ext` (extensionality): Two bundled coordinates are equal exactly when both unit coordinates agree.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rootUnitCoordinates_fst_kernel` (characterisation): The elements over u=1 are precisely (1,v) with v^2=1.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rootUnitCoordinates_empty_residue` (compatibility): If B0 is a subsingleton ring, the subgroup is the entire product. Consequently its first projection is the canonical equivalence with A0^units; the suggested signature states the subgroup equality.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rootUnitCoordinates_mk` (constructor): Given units u,v and h:Units.map(r)(u)=v^2, bundle (u,v) as a coordinate; both projections recover the given units. The multiplication, inverse, identity and their projection formulas are inherited from the native subgroup.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rootUnitCoordinates_map` (functoriality): For ring maps f:A0 to A1 and g:B0 to B1 with g composed with r = r1 composed with f, map (u,v) to (Units.map(f)(u),Units.map(g)(v)). This is a group homomorphism, with identity and composition laws and both projection formulas. It supplies restriction between framed charts.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.coordinates_empty_residue` (degenerate): When B0 is the zero ring there is no residue-root constraint; rootUnitCoordinates(r) is the whole product.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.coordinates_two_roots` (computation): For r=id_Z, (1,1) and (1,-1) are distinct members. An implementation identifying them loses the relative mu_2.
- `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.coordinates_not_arbitrary` (non-example): For r=id_Z, (-1,1) is not a member.

**Acceptance.** The square operation is on units; it is never treated as a ring homomorphism.; The first projection need not be injective, and forgetting the second coordinate is not the definition.

**Consumers.** where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-multiplicative-sheaf; root-torsor-comparison below; how: Evaluates actual sheaf sections on a chosen chart and tests that root labels survive.; where: FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units; actual-unit-image-determination below; how: Separates the root-unit group from its image in ordinary ideles.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.1, p. 524, fibre-product sheaf formula The source gives the sheaf formula; the native subgroup is its framed section adapter. [NATIVE-PINS](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Approximation.lean) — MonoidHom.eqLocus; Units.map; powMonoidHom at the recorded pins Use the existing equalizer and homomorphisms rather than rebuilding their group laws.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rootUnitCoordinates`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-unit-residue-approximation"></a>

#### Nonzero residue interpolation

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/unit-residue-approximation` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For fields k and F with a k-algebra structure, a finite injective family P_i of native TauCeti places and units y_i in their residue fields, there is a unit g in F, integral at every P_i, with residue y_i at every P_i. This includes the empty family. With chosen local rational line frames, the existing order approximation theorem also gives every finite required precision for the section coefficients.

**Hypotheses.** k and F are fields, F is a k-algebra, i ranges over a finite type, and i mapped to P_i is injective. No finite constant field, global function-field instance or completion is needed for the native statement.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.Place.exists_forall_residue_eq`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Place.exists_forall_ord_sub_eq`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the existing residue theorem to the underlying residues. If the family is nonempty, one prescribed nonzero residue shows g is not0 and hence defines a unit.
2. If the family is empty choose g=1 explicitly; do not try to infer nonzeroness from a nonexistent residue.
3. For greater precision apply exists_forall_ord_sub_eq to the finitely many rational coefficient targets with orders exceeding the needed local bounds. The geometric place/frame dictionary is a separate input to support moving.

**Acceptance.** Two distinct places can be assigned different nonzero residues.; No prescribed residue is required to be a square; the root-framing use supplies its own values.; The empty-family proof still returns a unit.

**Sources.** [NATIVE-PINS](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Approximation.lean) — TauCeti.Place.exists_forall_residue_eq and exists_forall_ord_sub_eq, Approximation.lean at f790474 The two theorems are already implemented; only the nonzero/empty-case corollary is new. [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.5 and (A.4), p. 518 The adelic presentation fixes the root framing and inverse-uniformizer convention. The nonzero residue corollary and its support-moving use are authored deductions from native approximation, not statements of Lemma A.5.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.exists_unit_with_residues`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-rank-one-cyclic-tensor-trace"></a>

#### Cyclic tensor trace in rank one

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/rank-one-cyclic-tensor-trace` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let E be a field, V a finite-dimensional E-vector space with dim V=1, d=n+1 a positive integer and a in E. On the native tensor product over Fin d, let T be cyclic left shift followed by multiplication by a on the last factor. Thus T(v_0 tensor ... tensor v_(d-1))=v_1 tensor ... tensor v_(d-1) tensor a*v_0, including d=1. Then Tr(T)=a. In particular it is not a raised to the closed-point degree. Different one-dimensional stalk factors with isomorphisms around a cycle reduce to this statement by transporting bases; a is the scalar of their composite around one cycle.

**Hypotheses.** E is a field in arbitrary universe, V is an E-module with additive group, finite-dimensional with finrank E V=1, n is a natural number and a is any scalar, including0. No characteristic or a squared=1 assumption.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:PiTensorProduct.map`, `mathlib:PiTensorProduct.reindex`, `mathlib:LinearMap.trace`, `mathlib:finRotate`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Choose a basis vector e of V; the pure tensor of d copies of e is a basis of the one-dimensional tensor product.
2. Reindex by the inverse finRotate so the new factor i is the old forward-cyclic factor. Apply a times identity at the last factor and identity elsewhere. The basis tensor goes to a times itself.
3. Take the native linear trace. For distinct stalks transport all factors along the cycle; exactly one remaining map is the full-cycle scalar.

**Acceptance.** For d=1 the operator is a times identity and trace=a.; For d=2 and a=-1 the trace is-1, whereas a squared=1.; For d=3 over Q with a=2 the trace is2, not8.; For a=0 the trace is0; invertibility is not a hidden linear-algebra hypothesis.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.4, pp. 525–526,(A.12) The source cyclic operator applies one full local Frobenius in the cycle. This node isolates its rank-one linear-algebra trace, with degree and orientation explicit. [NATIVE-PINS](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Approximation.lean) — PiTensorProduct.map/reindex, LinearMap.trace and finRotate at Mathlib082e2d3 These give honest native tensor and trace carriers for the suggested signature.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.rankOne_cyclicTensor_trace`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-residue-square"></a>

#### The norm restricts to a square at ramification

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-residue-square` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For the smooth geometrically connected double cover ν:X′→X with reduced ramification R′≃R and involution σ, restriction of Nm(u) to R is (u|_{R′})². For a line bundle L′, Nm(L′)|_R≅(L′|_{R′})² canonically.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ν:X′→X is finite flat of degree two, X′ smooth projective geometrically connected, R its reduced branch divisor, R′≃R.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-multiplicative-sheaf`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-multiplicative-sheaf), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. At a branch point use the finite-flat local double-cover algebra, with involution t↦−t.
2. The product of u and σu restricts to the same residue twice.
3. For line bundles use the corresponding determinant norm and its base-change compatibility from the supplier.

**Acceptance.** The isomorphism is on the actual residue fibre, not an equality between unrelated line bundles.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.1–A.3.2 p. 524

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-closed-point-trace"></a>

#### Closed-point tensor trace

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/closed-point-trace` · lemma · implementation unchecked.

For a closed point x∈U of degree δ, Tr(Fr_k,(L_δ)_{[x]})=Tr(Fr_x,L_x). On the tensor of δ conjugate rank-one fibres, Frobenius cyclically permutes factors and applies Fr_x on the wrapped factor.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/divisor-tensor-line`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-divisor-tensor-line), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/effective-pullback`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-effective-pullback), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/rank-one-cyclic-tensor-trace`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-rank-one-cyclic-tensor-trace).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the symmetric stalk description for the divisor [x].
2. Choose identifications of successive Frobenius-conjugate fibres; the product tensor action wraps around once.
3. For a rank-one line its scalar is the local Fr_x scalar, independent of the choices.

**Acceptance.** Using the δ-th power of that scalar on every tensor factor would give the wrong answer.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Proposition A.12 proof, (A.12) pp. 525–526

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-torsor-comparison"></a>

#### Root frames and the torsor stack

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-torsor-comparison` · comparison · implementation unchecked.

For every T, the groupoid of C-torsors on (X_T)_et is naturally equivalent to the groupoid of triples (M,J,alpha:J^2 isomorphic to M restricted to R_T). It sends a triple to the sheaf of simultaneous frames (e,f) with alpha(f^2)=e|R_T. Its automorphisms are actual compatible frame changes (u,v) with res(u)=v^2. Likewise B-torsors identify with line bundles on Xprime_T; A-torsors identify with line bundles on X_T. These are symmetric monoidal equivalences natural under arbitrary base change and on all arrows.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.; On the small etale site of X_T write A=G_m, B=nu_*G_m, C=G_m^sqrtR, N=(Nm,res), K=ker N, j:K to B, q:B to K induced by b/sigma(b), and i:A to B the invariant inclusion. In cohomology use additive notation for these abelian sheaves.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-multiplicative-sheaf`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-multiplicative-sheaf), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-groupoid`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-stack-curve`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/two-fibre-product`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/quotient-stack`, `tauceti:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.additiveUnitsFunctor`, `tauceti:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.additiveUnitsFunctor_obj_obj`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-unit-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-unit-coordinates), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/small-etale-site`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/sheaf-stack`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-cohomological`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Choose local frames of the two lines. The discrepancy in alpha is a unit on R_T; after an etale refinement lift its square root, using 2 invertible, to obtain simultaneous frames. This proves local nonemptiness of the frame sheaf.
2. The coordinate subgroup acts simply transitively on simultaneous frames. Conversely extend a C-torsor through the two projections and glue the two trivial lines; the defining equality gives alpha. Cocycle descent makes these inverse on objects and arrows.
3. For B, apply Stacks Lemma 31.18.1 (0BUT): a line on the inverse image of a finite morphism becomes trivial over the inverse image of a Zariski neighbourhood on the base. Thus its B-frame sheaf is already locally nonempty in the etale topology, for arbitrary T.
4. Tensor the frame torsors and compare both constructions locally to get monoidal and base-change coherence. Import general descent, never re-plan it.

**Acceptance.** For R empty recover the ordinary Picard groupoid, with its scalar automorphisms.; At a geometric point of R keep both roots of unity as arrow labels.; The result concerns torsors, not arbitrary sections with a square-zero root; no full root-section fibre is replaced by a gerbe.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.1, p. 524; Definition A.1, p. 514 The paper identifies root Picard objects with torsors. The simultaneous-frame equivalence and its arrows are the explicit descent verification. [STACKS-TORSORS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03AG) — Definition 21.4.1 and Lemma 95.14.2, tags 03AG and04UJ Tag 03AG supplies torsor local triviality. Lemma 95.14.2 (04UJ) is stated on the big fppf site; its gluing proof is applied here on the small etale site through the generic SF.1/sheaf-stack contract, descending the sheaf, action and local torsor condition. The root-frame and based-fibre comparisons are authored deductions. [MILNE-LEC](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/LEC.pdf) — Theorem 11.4, pp. 78–79 Rank-one locally free modules and G_m torsors agree; the finite-cover frame argument supplies the direct-image version. [STACKS-NORMS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BCX) — Lemma 31.18.1, tag 0BUT Line bundles over a finite inverse image trivialize over inverse images of base Zariski neighbourhoods; this proves local nonemptiness of the B-frame torsor without a limit argument.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.root_torsor_comparison`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-ramified-determinant-chart"></a>

#### Ramified determinant and residue square

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/ramified-determinant-chart` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

On a quadratic chart S0=A0[t]/(t^2-a) with 2 invertible and involution t mapped to -t, the norm of c+d*t is c^2-a*d^2. Modulo a the norm is the square of the image of c. The reduced branch section has t=0; after every base change this gives res Nm(u)=(res_Rprime u)^2 on units and the natural isomorphism (Mprime|Rprime_T)^2 isomorphic to Nm(Mprime)|R_T on lines. For a norm-one unit with residue1 at the branch, w=1+u is locally invertible there and u=w/sigma(w); ordinary norm-one without residue1 does not suffice.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.; A0 is a local chart ring, a cuts out the branch divisor, and the pulled-back cover is the displayed quadratic algebra. After arbitrary base change a need not be a non-zero-divisor; the determinant identity still holds.

**Prerequisites.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/line-bundle-norm`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-unit-coordinates`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-unit-coordinates), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-multiplicative-sheaf`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-multiplicative-sheaf).

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-residue-square`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-residue-square), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-kernel`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-kernel), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-norm-surjective`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-norm-surjective).

**Construction/proof.**

1. In the basis (1,t), multiplication by c+d*t has matrix with rows (c,a*d) and (d,c); compute its determinant.
2. Reduce modulo a and use t=0 for the specified Rprime section, retaining the nonreduced inverse-image algebra with t^2=0. Apply the formula to transition units of Mprime, not just to one trivial line.
3. The residue of w is2. The identity sigma(u)=u inverse gives sigma(w)=w/u, hence local surjectivity of q onto K near R. Away from R split the etale double cover. For ker q, write b=c+d*t: sigma(b)=b forces 2*d=0 and hence d=0, so b is an invariant unit; this remains true after nonflat base change. The invariant inclusion is injective because the chart is free with basis (1,t). Together these calculations give exactness at every term of the parent sheaf complex.
4. For a target (u,v) in C, choose etale-locally a square root z of u whose restriction along R is v. Such a branch choice extends etale-locally because z squared=u is etale with 2 and u invertible. Then the invariant unit nu^*z has norm u and branch residue v. Away from R the split cover gives surjectivity directly. This proves epimorphism of sheaves, not global sections.

**Acceptance.** For c=0,d=1 the norm is -a, including the sign; its branch restriction is0.; At a=0 the upstairs algebra has t^2=0 and is not replaced by its reduction.; For u=-1, ordinary norm is1 but branch residue is-1; such u is not in ker N when the branch is nonempty.; Etale surjectivity of N is checked by lifting a square root of the first coordinate with the prescribed branch value. It is not asserted on all global sections.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.1 and A.3.3, pp. 524–525 The residue-square and sheaf exactness assertions are expanded by this chart calculation. [STACKS-NORMS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BCX) — Lemma 31.18.6, tag 0BD2 Finite locally free norm is the multiplication determinant and commutes with base change.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.ramified_determinant_chart`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-framed-support-moving"></a>

#### Moving a root-framed line away from the branch

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-framed-support-moving` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Every k-object (M,J,alpha) of the root Picard stack has a presentation O_X(D)^natural for a signed k-rational divisor D supported in U. More precisely, choose a nonzero frame e_J of J on the finite etale k-scheme R. There is a nonzero rational section s of M, regular and nonvanishing at R, with s|R=alpha(e_J squared). Its signed divisor D avoids R, and the isomorphism O_X(D) to M sending the canonical rational section to s, together with 1 mapped to e_J, is an isomorphism of root Picard objects. Its degree is deg M; no effective-degree or rational-basepoint hypothesis is imposed.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; The ordinary signed divisor-line comparison and the identification of closed points with native function-field places are supplied through SF.3. Here T=Spec k; family support moving over arbitrary T is not asserted.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/unit-residue-approximation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-unit-residue-approximation), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-divisor-groupoid`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-divisor-groupoid), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. An invertible module on each residue field of R is free, so choose e_J componentwise. Choose any rational frame of M.
2. Choose local regular frames at the finitely many branch points. Translate the target alpha(e_J squared) into nonzero residue coefficients in those frames and then into finite approximation conditions on the rational frame coefficient. Native weak approximation supplies them, including the precision needed to cancel any pole of the original frame.
3. The resulting s has order0 and the prescribed value at each branch point. Its divisor is signed and k-rational with support in U. The ordinary divisor-line comparison and the stated root frame give the desired isomorphism.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-signed-divisor-trace"></a>

#### Frobenius trace on every signed divisor

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/signed-divisor-trace` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For the rank-one lisse sheaf L and its all-degree character extension P, set alpha_x=Tr(Fr_x,L_x) for every closed point x of U, with Fr_x geometric. For a signed divisor D=sum_x n_x[x] supported in U, the trace of geometric k-Frobenius on P at O_X(D)^natural is the product of alpha_x raised to n_x. For a single closed point of degree d, the Frobenius operator on the tensor of its d conjugate stalks is the cyclic operator with one full Fr_x and its trace is alpha_x. Unit, addition and inverse formulas follow from the chosen all-degree multiplication and unit, not from an effective-only comparison.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; ell is a prime different from p; coefficients are Qbar_ell, including ell=2. L is a rank-one lisse sheaf on the square-root curve with its k-descent, not assumed to have globally quadratic monodromy. P=L^Pic is the parent all-integer-degree character sheaf with its unit and coherent multiplication. Every Frobenius is geometric.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/rank-one-cyclic-tensor-trace`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-rank-one-cyclic-tensor-trace), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/signed-divisor-line`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-signed-divisor-line), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/signed-character-translation`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-signed-character-translation), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/unit-trivialization`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-unit-trivialization), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/character-associativity`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-character-associativity), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.5/character-symmetry-unit`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-5-character-symmetry-unit), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/trace-character`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-trace-character).

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/closed-point-trace`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-closed-point-trace).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the k-defined GC.5 signed translation isomorphism at the unit to identify P at O(D)^natural with the Frobenius line Lambda_D. Its descent datum cyclically permutes conjugate stalks at every closed point.
2. For a positive point transport the stalk factors around the Frobenius cycle. Apply the native cyclic trace theorem, with the full-cycle scalar equal to alpha_x.
3. For n_x negative use the dual line with its dual Frobenius, whose scalar is alpha_x inverse. The coherent unit has trace1. Tensor multiplication gives the finite signed product.

**Acceptance.** D=0 has trace1 in degree0.; For D=-[x], the trace is alpha_x inverse; a nonquadratic L distinguishes this from alpha_x.; At degree-two inert x the quadratic trace is-1, not1.; No trivialization of every stalk and no globally quadratic hypothesis is used for the general formula.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.4,(A.12), pp. 525–526 Closed-point cyclic Frobenius is the source input. The signed/all-degree extension is the precise GC.5 transport, correcting any effective-only or Frobenius-inversion shortcut.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.signed_divisor_trace`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-actual-unit-image-determination"></a>

#### Characters determined away from the branch

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/actual-unit-image-determination` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let H be the image of O_sqrtR^units to the ordinary idele group I_F, and Q=I_F/(F^units times H). At a branch place this image consists of local integral units whose residue is a square; off R it is all integral units. The map from signed divisors supported in U to Q sends [x] to the inverse-uniformizer class and is surjective. Hence homomorphisms Q to any abelian group are equal when they agree on every such class. For trace characters use Qbar_ell^units. The root-unit kernel, a product of mu_2 on R, survives as arrow labels in the double action groupoid even though Q is its class quotient.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; F=k(X). Use the parent adelic-root-groupoid equivalence with its inverse-uniformizer convention, and the FA.2 function-field ideles. All homomorphisms in the determination statement are actual homomorphisms on Q; no density or continuity argument substitutes for surjectivity.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-framed-support-moving`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-framed-support-moving), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/adelic-root-groupoid`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-adelic-root-groupoid), `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2/projective-ideles`, `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2/idele-divisor-exact-sequence`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the root-unit coordinate equation res(u)=v squared to compute the actual image and its kernel. Squares in every finite residue field are tested componentwise.
2. Use the imported adelic root groupoid to identify isomorphism classes with Q. Apply root-framed-support-moving to a representative root Picard object to get a signed divisor in U.
3. The associated class is the product of the inverse-uniformizer classes to their signed multiplicities. Evaluate both characters on this finite product. There is no passage to a profinite completion.

**Acceptance.** Using the full ordinary unit subgroup at R discards the square-residue distinction and changes Q.; For R empty recover the ordinary idele/Picard-class determination.; A negative multiplicity gives the inverse character value.; All closed points, rather than only k-rational points, are required.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — Lemma A.5 and (A.4), p. 518; A.3.4, p. 525 The adelic root quotient and approximation justify the determination step; the statement keeps the actual unit image rather than forgetting its branch condition.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.actual_unit_image_determination`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-reciprocity-root-unit-triviality"></a>

#### Quadratic reciprocity factors through the root quotient

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/reciprocity-root-unit-triviality` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

Let eta be the quadratic idele character associated with the given double cover, obtained from the finite Artin norm quotient. It is trivial on principal ideles and on H, the actual modified-unit image. At every x in U it takes the inverse uniformizer to the trace of geometric Frobenius on the quadratic rank-one local system: +1 at split x and -1 at inert x. At x in R the local character on integral units is the quadratic character of the residue field, so every square-residue unit is killed. Thus eta defines a character of Q.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.; Use arithmetic local Artin maps in FA.4, so an inverse uniformizer corresponds to geometric Frobenius. Values are mapped from {+1,-1} into Qbar_ell^units with ell different from p.

**Prerequisites.** `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4/global-artin-norm-isomorphism`, `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4/local-abelian-existence`, `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.2/root-units`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-2-root-units), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/ramified-determinant-chart`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-ramified-determinant-chart).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Import the finite global Artin norm quotient, which supplies principal triviality. The quadratic representation takes its values in the two signs.
2. At unramified places integral units act trivially. At a tame ramified place the determinant chart shows that the residue of the norm of a unit is a square. Conversely a square-residue unit is a square in the complete local field by Hensel with 2 invertible, hence is the norm of its invariant square root. A unit norm can only come from a unit in this totally ramified degree-two extension. The local norm quotient from FA.4 therefore gives exactly the residue quadratic character. Request the completion/Hensel/residue adapter there.
3. Multiply the local values in the finite quotient; only finitely many are nontrivial. Invert the arithmetic uniformizer action to get geometric Frobenius. On the two geometric points above an unramified x this action is the identity in the split case and exchanges the points in the inert case, hence acts on their anti-invariant line by +1 and -1 respectively. This argument does not assume the parent quadratic-input conclusion that eta kills H.

**Acceptance.** An ordinary local unit with nonsquare residue at a branch point has value-1 and cannot be added to H.; At a degree-two inert closed point the inverse uniformizer still has value-1.; No isomorphism between the uncompleted idele class group and the absolute Galois group is asserted.; The same sign formula holds for ell=2, since Qbar_2 has characteristic0.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.4, p. 525, first paragraph and proof of Proposition A.12 The quadratic input and local evaluations are used here; the existing FA.4 finite Artin theorem supplies global reciprocity. The tame residue adapter remains a precise request.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.reciprocity_root_unit_triviality`.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ν:X′→X is finite flat of degree two, X′ smooth projective geometrically connected, R its reduced branch divisor, R′≃R.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-quadratic-local-values"></a>

#### Split and inert Frobenius signs

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/quadratic-local-values` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

On U, the anti-invariant summand of nu_*Qbar_ell is a rank-one lisse sheaf. At every closed point x, geometric Frobenius acts on its fibre by+1 if the two-point etale fibre splits over k(x), and by-1 if it is inert. The same scalar is eta(inverse_uniformizer_x). This identifies the local trace values needed in the quadratic trace theorem, including non-rational closed points.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.; ell is a prime different from char k, including2; coefficients are Qbar_ell and the anti-invariant projector is (1-sigma)/2. Only U, where nu is etale, is used for this fibre calculation.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/reciprocity-root-unit-triviality`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-reciprocity-root-unit-triviality), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.3/tame-local-systems`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-3-tame-local-systems), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/quadratic-input`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-quadratic-input).

**Construction/proof.**

1. The stalk is the permutation representation on the two geometric points of the fibre. Its anti-invariant line is generated by their difference.
2. The geometric Frobenius permutation is identity in the split case and the transposition in the inert case. The difference vector has the stated eigenvalue, independent of the degree over k.
3. Compare with the local Artin description for the quadratic extension. Geometric and arithmetic Frobenius are inverse; for these signs their eigenvalues coincide, while the global convention is still fixed.

**Acceptance.** The split two-point fibre has anti-invariant trace+1, not the full permutation trace2.; The inert fibre has anti-invariant trace-1, not the full permutation trace0.; The argument remains valid for ell=2 because the coefficient field contains1/2.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.4, pp. 525–526, definition of L and proof of Proposition A.12 The quadratic sign is computed on the anti-invariant rank-one summand, which is the local system used by the character construction.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.quadratic_local_values`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-exact-sheaf-complex"></a>

#### The exact ramified norm sheaf sequence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/exact-sheaf-complex` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

The étale sheaf complex 1→G_m,X→ν_*G_m,X′→^{1−σ}ν_*G_m,X′→^{Nm^√R}G_m,X^√R→1 is exact, with specified zero composites. Passing to torsor groupoids requires its connecting obstruction data; this theorem does not claim a short exact sequence of Picard groups.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ν:X′→X is finite flat of degree two, X′ smooth projective geometrically connected, R its reduced branch divisor, R′≃R.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-kernel`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-kernel), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/root-norm-surjective`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-root-norm-surjective).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Use the two local kernel calculations and sheaf surjectivity.
2. Check each composite equals the multiplicative unit by the norm/involution and residue relations.
3. Retain the intermediate kernel sheaf K=im(1−σ) for the two short exact sequences used in derived descent.

**Acceptance.** A nontrivial line bundle can become trivial under an étale pullback; group injectivity is not inferred.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-descent-obstruction"></a>

#### Norm lifts and their secondary obstruction

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-descent-obstruction` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For a C-torsor Q a B-torsor lift with a quotient identification exists exactly when delta_N^1[Q]=0 in H2(K). If nonempty, this lift groupoid is acted on simply transitively by Tors(K), hence is equivalent to Tors(K) after choosing one lift; its class set is a torsor under H1(K) and its automorphisms are H0(K). For a line L upstairs with norm trivialization tau, write P_tau for the corresponding K-torsor. Then (L,tau) is isomorphic to (d(M),tau_M) for some M exactly when delta_q^1[P_tau]=0 in H2(A). On the underlying norm-trivial line class define omega(L) as delta_q^1[P_tau] modulo the image of delta_q^1 composed with delta_N^0:H0(C) to H2(A). This class is independent of tau, and vanishes exactly when [L] is in the image of d_* on H1(B).

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.; On the small etale site of X_T write A=G_m, B=nu_*G_m, C=G_m^sqrtR, N=(Nm,res), K=ker N, j:K to B, q:B to K induced by b/sigma(b), and i:A to B the invariant inclusion. In cohomology use additive notation for these abelian sheaves.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/connecting-maps`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-connecting-maps), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/difference-norm-nullhomotopy`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-difference-norm-nullhomotopy), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/torsor-fibre-sequences`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-torsor-fibre-sequences), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/abelian-torsor-h1`.

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/picard-descent-obstructions`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-picard-descent-obstructions).

**Construction/proof.**

1. The first lift criterion is exactness at H1(C). Tensoring a lift by a K-torsor with its canonical quotient trivialization gives the action; taking the quotient of two lifts gives its inverse.
2. For a fixed tau, lift P_tau through q by the second long exact sequence. Identify the resulting norm-trivialized line with the canonical d(M) using the nullhomotopy comparison.
3. Fix the convention that changing tau by c means tau_new=c inverse times tau. The inverse-image-of-unit definition gives [P_tau_new]=[P_tau]+delta_N^0(c). Thus the displayed quotient class is independent of the choice.
4. If its representative is in the boundary image, alter tau by the opposite c, then lift P_tau through q. Conversely an isomorphism L isomorphic to d(M) transports tau_M to a trivialization with zero representative. This proves the underlying-class criterion.

**Acceptance.** H2(A) is not declared zero; no Brauer vanishing over X_T is assumed.; A merely trivial norm class does not supply a canonical tau.; The fixed-trivialization and underlying-class criteria use different obstruction groups.; For Q=1 with its unit B-lift the lift groupoid is Tors(K), including H0(K) automorphisms.

**Sources.** [MILNE-LEC](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/LEC.pdf) — Section9 property(c), p. 64 and Section11, pp. 76–79 Exactness and the torsor interpretation prove the primary obstruction and the secondary calculation. [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.3, p. 525, display(A.11) This is an authored, obstruction-sensitive replacement for the recorded interpretation gap E8; it is not attributed as a theorem stated there.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.norm_descent_obstruction`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-invariance-versus-descent"></a>

#### Invariant lines and descent data

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/invariance-versus-descent` · theorem · implementation unchecked.

For an upstairs line M, descent to a line on X_T is equivalent to q_*[M]=0 in H1(K). Sigma-invariance of its class is equivalent to q_*[M] lying in the image of delta_N^0:H0(C) to H1(K). The kernel of pullback i_*:H1(A) to H1(B) equals the image of delta_q^0:H0(K) to H1(A). A chosen trivialization of q_*M determines an effective descent object. The full fibre groupoid of pairs (M,beta), allowing isomorphisms of M compatible with beta, is Tors(A) and retains H0(A) automorphisms; this is not the fibre with both M and a specified pullback identification fixed. In particular a chosen isomorphism M isomorphic to sigma^*M alone is not descent data.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.; nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.; On the small etale site of X_T write A=G_m, B=nu_*G_m, C=G_m^sqrtR, N=(Nm,res), K=ker N, j:K to B, q:B to K induced by b/sigma(b), and i:A to B the invariant inclusion. In cohomology use additive notation for these abelian sheaves.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/connecting-maps`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-connecting-maps), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/torsor-fibre-sequences`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-torsor-fibre-sequences).

**Refines.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/picard-descent-obstructions`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-picard-descent-obstructions).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply exactness to H1(A) to H1(B) to H1(K) for the descent criterion and to H0(K) to H1(A) for the pullback kernel.
2. The class of d(M) is j_* q_*[M]. By the other long exact sequence its vanishing is equivalent to q_*[M] belonging to image(delta_N^0).
3. Use the second torsor fibre equivalence for the actual descended line and arrows; do not extract descent solely from the vanishing of d(M).

**Acceptance.** If M is pulled back, its q-torsor has the canonical trivialization.; An invariant M may have nonzero q_*[M]; the next degree test forces this possibility.; If a descent exists, changing its specified isomorphism upstairs need not preserve a previously chosen descent structure.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.3, p. 525, display(A.11) The source display motivates the question; the two long exact sequences supply the corrected distinction. [MILNE-LEC](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/LEC.pdf) — Section9 property(c), p. 64; Theorem 11.4, pp. 78–79 The exactness and line/torsor comparison give the stated criteria.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.invariance_versus_descent`.

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-picard-descent-obstructions"></a>

#### Descent obstructions for the Picard-stack sequence

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/picard-descent-obstructions` · application · implementation unchecked.

Let K=ker Nm^√R. Interpret the exact sheaf complex as the two short exact sequences G_m→ν_*G_m→K and K→ν_*G_m→G_m^√R, and apply their derived cohomology and torsor descent. Any Picard-stack exactness statement must specify the connecting maps, coherent norm trivializations and effectiveness obstructions, rather than replacing the result by an ordinary kernel of 1−σ on line-bundle classes.

**Hypotheses.** For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.; ν:X′→X is finite flat of degree two, X′ smooth projective geometrically connected, R its reduced branch divisor, R′≃R.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/exact-sheaf-complex`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-exact-sheaf-complex), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.0/root-picard`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-0-root-picard), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`, [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-descent-obstruction`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-descent-obstruction), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/invariance-versus-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-invariance-versus-descent).

**Construction/proof.**

1. Apply the supplier’s derived torsor/cohomology comparison to each short sequence separately.
2. Track the H⁰(G_m^√R)→H¹(K) and H¹(K)→H²(G_m) connecting maps rather than dropping them.
3. For the displayed (A.11) fix a coherent exactness convention and prove its stated Picard-stack consequence; this remaining source gap is NORM-2EXACT, and is not treated as a proved theorem.

**Acceptance.** For ν:P¹→P¹, t↦t², O_{P¹}(1) is σ-invariant but is not pullback from downstairs because pullback doubles degree. This rules out naive kernel exactness at the first upstairs Picard group.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.3 p. 525 (A.11), source-interpretation gap

<a id="functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-degree-descent-counterexample"></a>

#### The double projective line degree test

`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/degree-descent-counterexample` · application · implementation unchecked.

Let k be finite of odd characteristic and nu:P1_k to P1_k be t mapped to t^2, with sigma(t)=-t and R={0,infinity}. The line O(1) upstairs is sigma-invariant but is not pulled back from the base: pullback multiplies degree by2. Hence q_*[O(1)] is nonzero although j_*q_*[O(1)]=0, and lies in image(delta_N^0). The same holds for O(-1). Norm preserves degree and sends O(1) to O(1); these statements do not contradict the obstruction-sensitive torsor fibres.

**Hypotheses.** k is a finite field of characteristic different from2; both projective lines and the displayed finite flat double cover are defined over k.

**Prerequisites.** [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/invariance-versus-descent`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-invariance-versus-descent), [`FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:GC.6/norm-section-comparison`](#functionfieldarithmeticpartii-gc-6-norm-section-comparison), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/line-bundle-norm`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Construction/proof.**

1. Automorphisms of P1 preserve O(1). The degree of nu^*O(m) is2m, so O(1) and O(-1) cannot descend.
2. Use the corrected invariance criterion to locate their nonzero K-torsor classes in image(delta_N^0).
3. The ordinary finite-flat norm sends the degree-one point0 upstairs to the degree-one point0 downstairs. The line/divisor norm comparison gives Nm O(1)=O(1).

**Acceptance.** A statement identifying invariant line classes with pullback classes must fail this test.; A norm formula doubling degrees must fail this test.; The negative-degree version prevents a hidden effective-divisor restriction.

**Sources.** [YZ19](https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/GZW_ramified_published.pdf) — A.3.3, p. 525, display(A.11) This authored example tests the unqualified interpretation of the display, not every coherent interpretation of it. [STACKS-NORMS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BCX) — Lemmas31.18.2 and31.18.6, tags 0BCY/0BD2 These give the ordinary line norm and its determinant. The divisor-pushforward comparison is imported from SF.3/line-bundle-norm through GC6-CURVE-DICTIONARY; it is not asserted in these two Stacks lemmas.

**Suggested name.** `TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GC6.degree_descent_counterexample`.

## Shared interface frontier and reconciliation

ASM-STACK-LISSE is one interface with one intended supplier owner. It combines GC3-STACK-PI1 (normal DM fundamental groups, continuous rank-one monodromy and atlas descent) and GC4-LISSE-ADAPTER (finite-cover comparison, smooth Artin descent, proper degree-zero base change, lissity and compatible local adic coefficients). Their exact hypotheses remain in the layer entries above. GC3-COARSE-STALKS and GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD are separate exports of that same proposed stacks extension: nilpotent invariance, coarse stalks/Leray and proper nonrepresentable base change are not merged into a scheme theorem. No registered stage is fabricated for this owner.

The accepted GC.3 exterior comparison replaces the parent's former EXTERIOR-COMP mathematical question. The accepted GC.6 based-fibre/connecting-map targets specify the norm obstructions, and its native approximation targets replace the former request for a new generic approximation theorem. Their implementation and precise curve/lisse adapters remain open. The parent ST-LISSE/ST-OPS records are narrowed accordingly. The assembly handoff collects every retained request and restructuring proposal, including broader parent integration requests that a refinement makes more precise.


**ST-LISSE.** Shared stack-lisse interface, consolidated as ASM-STACK-LISSE in the assembly handoff: normal DM finite-cover/monodromy comparison and atlas descent (GC3-STACK-PI1), with smooth Artin-stack lisse descent, local adic coefficients and Hom/tensor/base-change compatibility (GC4-LISSE-ADAPTER). GC.4 uses the reviewed proper-quotient/chart-gluing route, not a general nonproper Abel–Jacobi descent assertion. The proposed EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves stacks Part II is the intended owner; its provisional ST stage names are not registered prerequisites.

**ST-OPS.** The parent pushforward/perverse description retains a precise stack comparison frontier: GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD supplies proper base change for the nonrepresentable ordered map, and GC3-COARSE-STALKS supplies coarse pushforward, nilpotent invariance and Leray. Rational finite-group acyclicity is planned by the accepted GC.3 follow-up; cohomology, Künneth and duality proceed on schemes. Consumers needing only the lisse line use monodromy-symmetric-local-system. No general stack decomposition theorem is assumed.

**NORM-2EXACT.** The accepted GC.6/torsor-fibre-sequences, connecting-maps, norm-descent-obstruction and invariance-versus-descent now specify the based fibres, compatible norm trivializations and primary/secondary cohomological obstructions. Their actual geometric/torsor carriers remain to be integrated. Source issue E8 remains an interpretation qualification of (A.11), not a missing statement of ordinary Picard-class exactness and not a claim to know the authors’ intended two-categorical exactness.

GC.6/unit-residue-approximation, root-framed-support-moving and actual-unit-image-determination specify its application, including the empty family and the actual modified-unit image. ## Suggested forms and acceptance boundary

The [aggregate suggested file](../suggested/FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII.lean) has one standard note, one import block and the ten fragments in layer order. It contains light native definitions, end/milestone statements and representative checks that can be typed at the mandatory atlas pins. The full geometric targets and every API/test in the catalogue remain required even when their carriers cannot be stated there. The file's omission ledger identifies those families. In particular, elaboration of the coordinates does not supply a root stack, an infinite torsor, geometric lisse descent, a norm obstruction calculation or a Frobenius comparison.

The former large parent prototype is superseded as suggested code. The GC.2 diagonal/action/functor development and GC.3 private copies of current tensor/exterior maps are also omitted from the aggregate suggested forms; their complete mathematical contracts and tests remain above. This follows the current roadmap shape and prevents an implementation attempt from becoming a prerequisite to writing a plan.

A future implementation must discharge the exact supplier contracts, instantiate the real geometric carriers, prove the admitted milestones and run the discriminating checks, including nilpotents, wild exponents, empty ramification, negative degrees, residue degrees, nontrivial torsor labels, arbitrary global characters and geometric Frobenius. Acceptance of this assembly is acceptance of a coherent plan, not closure of those obligations.
